paragraphs.text: This verse was explained in the introduction, and it shows the following:
1- The name of the prophet, Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah.
2- That he was a priest.
3- His birthplace, which was the village of Anathoth in the tribe of Benjamin.

Jeremiah began his prophecy in the thirteenth year of the reign of Josiah the son of Amon, who was king over the kingdom of Judah, whose capital was Jerusalem and which included the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin. It is called the southern kingdom, as was mentioned in the introduction.

The prophecy continued from the days of Jehoiakim the king, the son of Josiah, until Zedekiah the king, the last king of Judah, in the eleventh year of whose reign the captivity took place. The other kings who reigned during the period of the prophecy are not mentioned, because they reigned only for short periods; all this was explained in the introduction.

The word of God began to Jeremiah, informing him that he was chosen for the ministry even before he was formed in his mother's womb, just as the Holy Bible declares God's love for us when it says, “According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love” (Eph 1:4). In His love God knew and sanctified, that is, He set Jeremiah apart to carry out this ministry, that is, to prophesy to His people. This was in the eternal mind of God before the creation of the world. It appears in this verse that Jeremiah is a prophet not only to the Jewish people living in the kingdom of Judah, but to the peoples of the whole world, since he calls them to return to God: “I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.”

God loved you and set you apart to live for Him, and He declared this when you came out of Baptism and were sanctified by the Holy Myron. So do not be distracted from Him by the concerns of the world, or turn away from Him through many sins, for you are consecrated to Him; please Him in everything and serve Him faithfully.

Jeremiah felt the greatness of the responsibility of the ministry, and in humility he declared his inability to carry it out, since he was young, so he said, “I am a child.” What is meant by a child is one younger than thirty years, for the Jews considered a man to be mature only when he had passed the age of thirty, which is why Christ began His ministry at this age.
It is good to know your weakness, so that you do not rush into any work but count the cost, and declare your weakness before God so that He supports you.

God encouraged him so that he would not make an excuse because of his young age, and promised to be with him and to deliver him from the hands of the wicked if they opposed him, until he completed his ministry.

God was not content to support Jeremiah with promises, but stretched out His hand and touched his lips, giving him the power to speak the word of God, so that Jeremiah would no longer speak ordinary human words but would utter the powerful and profound word of God. We do not know the form in which God stretched out His hand and touched Jeremiah's mouth. Did a hand appear and touch him? Or did he only feel someone touching his mouth? Or did a light appear before him? In any case, Jeremiah felt a tangible touch on his mouth while he was hearing these words from God.

God gave Jeremiah authority over the kingdoms and peoples about whom he would prophesy, such as the kingdom of Judah, Babylon and Philistia, so that he might rebuke their evils until they repent, and thus root out evil from them, pull it down and destroy it, and at the same time build up their spiritual life by the word of God and plant faith in them. In this he is a type of the incarnate Christ, who uproots evil from the souls of those who receive His word, and builds up faith and life with Him in them.

Speak with authority when you proclaim the word of God, so that you call everyone to life with Him. Do not be troubled by the opposition of the wicked or their mockery. With the gentleness of love, let your speech be definite and strong, and know that they are troubled however much they oppose you, because the word is not from you but from God.

entries.section: (3) The vision of the almond rod and the swollen pot

paragraphs.text: Rod: the stem of the almond plant.

The first vision that God revealed to Jeremiah is the rod of the almond plant. This plant is planted in winter and appears to have no life in it, but before the beginning of spring, that is, in the month of February, it puts forth white blossoms that turn into almond fruit. So the plant seems to be without fruit throughout the winter, but afterwards it gives sweet fruit in the spring. This shows how God watches over and cares for this plant throughout the winter and gives it sweet fruit in the spring. It is worth mentioning that the Hebrew word translated “almond” also means “watcher.”

entries.section: (3) The vision of the almond rod and the swollen pot

paragraphs.text: I will hasten: I will carry it out, for the word of God is true and must be fulfilled.

God praised Jeremiah because he understood and discerned the almond rod that he saw, and He interpreted the meaning of the vision to him, which is God's watchfulness and concern for the effect of His word on people. God is long-suffering, but at the right time He carries out everything: He punishes the children of Israel for their sins with captivity, and He also punishes those whom He used to punish them, namely the kingdom of Babylon, by the destruction of their kingdom at the hands of the kingdom of the Medes and Persians.

The almond fruit has a green outer covering that falls away with time, and then a strong dry shell which, when broken, reveals within it the sweet fruit that is eaten. In the same way, the word of God does not reach its sweetness except after we endure bitter striving and severe pains to break the powers of evil, but in the end we must taste its sweet effect in our lives.

Those who are far from God claim that the world goes on without God's intervention, and consequently they neglect His commandments. But God's long-suffering does not cancel His word, which must be fulfilled; He rewards the righteous and repays the wicked, because He watches over His word to perform it. What is meant here is to warn the people through Jeremiah by this prophecy, so that they obey God and His word, which will be fulfilled, and do not persist in their evil, or else He will punish them with captivity.

entries.section: (3) The vision of the almond rod and the swollen pot

paragraphs.text: A swollen pot: a large vessel with a mouth, shaped like a sphere, like the pot used for beans whose belly is swollen. Its face is toward the north: its mouth is turned toward the north.

The second vision that Jeremiah saw is a swollen pot, which signifies the pride of the Jews, who thought that as long as the temple of God was among them no harm would come to them, and that as long as they had the outward forms of personal worship they were safe. The mouth of the pot, turned toward the north, signifies the Babylonian attack from the north upon Jerusalem and Judea, and their occupation and destruction.

entries.section: (3) The vision of the almond rod and the swollen pot

paragraphs.text: From the north the kingdom of Babylon will arise and attack the surrounding countries of the world and Jerusalem, and will destroy it.

entries.section: (3) The vision of the almond rod and the swollen pot

paragraphs.text: His throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem: this means the occupation of the city and control of its gates. Its walls: that is, control of the walls and their destruction.

All the cities of Judah: that is, all the lands of the kingdom of Judah, which is the southern kingdom of the Jews. God continues His speech with Jeremiah, saying that the kingdom of Babylon will attack Jerusalem and occupy it, and will also occupy all the lands of the kingdom of Judah, take captive those who are in them, plunder their wealth and destroy them.

entries.section: (3) The vision of the almond rod and the swollen pot

paragraphs.text: I will utter my judgments: I will declare My punishment.
God explains that the destruction of Jerusalem and Judea and their captivity is a punishment for His people because they worshiped idols and walked in many evils.
So God warns His people by the first vision, so that they may repent, and if they do not repent, the second prophecy comes upon them, which is destruction.

May you pay attention to the word of God that He sends to you to keep you away from evil and draw you to His love, so that you enjoy peace and are delivered from many troubles. For if you neglect His word, nothing awaits you but anxiety and turmoil in this life, and then eternal torment in the life to come.
Gird up thy loins: put on a girdle, that is, a wide belt around the waist. This signifies intensity of work and ministry.

God asked Jeremiah to proclaim these visions and their interpretation to the people, and to prepare for the labors of this ministry, and not to fear the people's opposition to him, or their rebuke, or their rejection of his word, or their threats against him. He reminds him that what matters most is the fear of God, not the fear of people.

So that Jeremiah would not draw back from his ministry, He warned him that if he neglected his ministry and feared the people, God would make him afraid and punish him. God had to warn Jeremiah in this way because He knew the severity of the opposition he would meet from the wicked, so this warning was to protect him from drawing back.
The fear of God keeps you away from sin and helps you hold fast to His commandments and perform His service faithfully, so that you enjoy His care and His love.
A defenced city: Jeremiah becomes a support for those who fear God, by his encouragement and care for them, like a fortified city that protects them within it.

An iron pillar: that is, a strong foundation upon which the house of God is built, so that he proclaims His word and supports His children. Brasen walls: brass is a strong material, so brazen walls protect those within them, like Jeremiah, to whom God will give strength so that he is not shaken by the doubts and opposition of the wicked.

God strengthened Jeremiah with powerful promises that He would make him like a fortified city, a strong iron pillar and brazen walls for everyone who believes and lives with God, and that he himself would stand firm in strength before the wicked. This indeed happened for more than 40 years, during which he rebuked everyone and they opposed him, and he was not shaken until he was martyred in the end.

God continued His speech with Jeremiah and made known to him that his people would oppose him and fight against him, but they would not be able to silence him; rather he would remain strong to complete his message and his prophecy, even after they took him against his will to Egypt.
Warning Jerusalem so that she may repent

Here begin the words of the prophecy that God commanded Jeremiah to speak to the people in Jerusalem, for the words in the first chapter were either commands to Jeremiah as a servant, or visions that he proclaims to the people. In God's speech with His people here, the following appears:
1- That it is a rebuke of love, whispered in the ears of His bride whom He loved, the ears of Jerusalem, since He regards Jerusalem and her people as a bride whom He loves very much.

If you notice something wrong in one of your loved ones, rebuke him gently between you and him. Praise him first before you show his faults, encourage him to overcome them, and show him your attachment to him and your trust in him, so that you win his heart; for if you do not win him first, he will not allow you to criticize him.
2- The kindness of thy youth:

God commends Jerusalem, that is, His people the children of Israel, for their holy zeal toward Him when they left the worship of idols in Egypt and worshiped Him alone in the wilderness of Sinai. This is the zeal of Jerusalem in her youth, before she dwelt in the Promised Land.
3- The love of thine espousals:

He compares Jerusalem to a bride whom He betrothed to Himself, and how she loved Him by her worship of Him in the Tabernacle of Meeting at Sinai. She was His betrothed at Sinai, then she became His bride by continuing her worship of Him in Canaan and in the temple of Solomon.
4- Thou wentest after me in the wilderness:
This means the children of Israel leaving Egypt with all its good things and going out into the barren wilderness of Sinai, where nothing is sown, in order to worship God far from the idols of Egypt.
It is noted here that God commends His people and focuses on their virtues, forgetting their faults in this period, such as murmuring and disobedience.
God shows His love for Jerusalem and her place with Him by what He says about her:

1- Holiness unto the LORD: all the children of Israel are the people of God, like Aaron, who was consecrated to his ministry and who put a plate of gold on his turban with “Holiness to the LORD” written on it. They are His people and He cares for them with His love.

2- The firstfruits of his increase: the Law commanded the people of God to offer Him the firstfruits, that is, the first of the harvests. The children of Israel are the first of the peoples who believed and lived for God, to be the firstfruits of the whole world when people from every place believe in Christ. So it is a privilege for Jerusalem to enjoy clinging to God before the other peoples.

3- All that devour him shall offend: if the children of Israel sin and God allows the Gentiles, such as the kingdom of Assyria and Babylon, to take them captive, this is a discipline for Israel; but at the same time God is not pleased with the evil of the Gentiles who wrong His people, and He punishes them with destruction, as happened to Assyria and then Babylon.
God directs His prophetic speech to all the Jews in:
1- The house of Jacob: that is, the kingdom of Judah, whose capital is Jerusalem.

2- All the families of the house of Israel: the rest of the tribes who formed the northern kingdom, which Assyria then took captive; some of them remained in the kingdom of Israel, and others were scattered throughout the world by the Assyrians.
So the speech is directed to the people of God in every place and time.
Iniquity: injustice.
After vanity: after the vain idols that they worshiped.
Became vain: they walked in lusts and sins that profit nothing.
God rebukes His people because He did not wrong them, but cared for them with His love, and yet they left Him and worshiped idols and plunged into evil lusts.
The shadow of death: the people were exposed to the dangers of death, whether at the hands of enemies or of wild beasts, but God kept them and defended them.

The people of God forgot His power that delivered them from the slavery of Egypt by the ten plagues and the parting of the Red Sea, and how He cared for them with manna and quail and water from the rock, shaded them with the cloud and guided them by the pillar of fire by night, although no human being can live in the wilderness of Sinai because of its dryness and the impossibility of life there, especially for a great people numbering about 2 million; and He fought for them against enemies such as Amalek.
An abomination: unclean through the worship of idols, with which they defiled the Promised Land.

God brought His people into the fertile land of Canaan, filled with orchards of fruit and every good thing, and they ate and were filled, but they turned away from God by worshiping idols, and so they defiled the land that God had cleansed for them.

God is ready to keep you in afflictions however hard they may be, and to provide for you in them as He provided for His people in the barren wilderness of Sinai, and then to give you many spiritual good things in the Church, so that you may be filled with them and not defile them with your evil thoughts, your outward worship or your pride. Do not repay God's love with evil, but keep His commandments and thank Him for His gifts.
Here God shows the turning away from Him of all the groups of the people, who are:
1- The priests: they performed the rite outwardly and did not bind the people to the love of God and to repentance from their sins.

2- They that handle the law: these are the spiritual teachers who were occupied with other things than the worship of God, and consequently did not teach the people, but taught them teachings that turned them away from God.
3- The pastors: that is, the leaders and kings who were proud and did not keep the commandments of God, and so led the people astray after them into many sins.
4- The prophets: instead of prophesying the word of God, they became false prophets who prophesied for pagan gods such as “Baal,” so their prophecies were mistaken and misleading to the people.
From this appears the difficulty of the spiritual situation, since all the groups of the people had turned aside, and no one was left but Jeremiah to proclaim the voice of God.

God calls His people in Jerusalem and all of Judea to stand before the court, and He becomes an adversary to them, bringing His case against them, and not only against them but also against their children, because they taught their children evil.
Chittim: Cyprus.
Kedar: tribes that dwell in the Arabian Peninsula.

God calls the nations of the world as witnesses against His people, whether those in the north-west, such as the island of Crete, or in the south, such as the tribes of Kedar, who worship their pagan gods and do not exchange them for unknown gods; but the people of God changed their true God and worshiped what are no gods, namely the idols, which do not profit them at all but harm them, deprive them and separate them from God.
Be astonished: be amazed.
Be horribly afraid: tremble.

God bears witness against His people, not only the pagan nations but also nature, represented by heaven, and so He calls on the heavens to be amazed, to tremble and to be bewildered at the strange and unreasonable conduct of His people in worshiping idols; and by this they fell into two great sins, which are:
1- They forsook God, the source of their life, without whom they cannot live, for He is like a fountain of living waters by the work of His Holy Spirit in them.

2- They sought another support to rely on in their lives, namely the useless pagan gods, which He compares to broken cisterns from which the water leaks out so that they become dry; however many cisterns of this kind a person digs, he finds no water to quench his thirst, but finds only mud and sand, and his life is made dirty by them. The heavens also signify the angels, who bear witness against His people for turning away from their God and running after idols that do not profit, so that they spend their effort all their lives in vain.

Do not waste your time on useless viewing or discussions and neglect your relationship with God, that is, your prayers, your reading and your attachment to the Church, for you will be wearied and lose God's love and care.

God asks a rhetorical question about His people, saying: is he a servant to those who humiliate him, whether Egypt or Babylon? That is, did Egypt or Babylon buy him as a servant, or is he a homeborn slave, the son of a servant born in his master's house? In both cases he is a slave, whether his master bought him or he was born in his house. The proof that He offers is that the people of God have become a prey over which their enemies rule. By this He rebukes them: why have they become slaves to the nations that exploit them? The reason, of course, is their distance from God and their falling into many sins, so it is a call to repentance and return to God.
Roared: the sound of lions and young lions.

He compares the attack of Egypt, Assyria and Babylon on the children of Israel to the roaring of young lions, preparing to pounce on their prey and then attacking, so that they laid waste their land and burned their cities with fire.
Noph and Tahapanes: cities of Egypt, used to stand for all of Egypt.
Have broken the crown of thy head: have broken your head.

God continues His rebuke of the humiliation of His people and the attack of their enemies upon them like young lions, and adds that Egypt has broken the head of His people, that is, shattered their strength and humiliated them.

God declares that the reason for all these calamities is their forsaking His worship along the way of their life, and their preoccupation with lusts and the worship of idols, and that this turning aside was by the will of His people and no one forced them to it, so all these troubles came upon them.
Sihor: the river full of silt, that is, the river Nile in Egypt.
The river: what is meant by it is the river Euphrates, which is in Babylon.

God rebukes His people for their resorting to Egypt, which is represented by the waters of the Nile, or their resorting to Babylon, which is represented by the river Euphrates, when it would have been better for them in their distress to resort to God and not to human beings. Egypt signifies fertility and good things, that is, material lusts, while Babylon signifies pride because of its boasting in its greatness.

God affirms that the reason for the humiliation and ruin that His people will suffer is their sin and their disobedience to God, their lack of fear of Him, their persisting in their evils and their worship of strange gods. God declares His power by saying that His name is the LORD of hosts; it is He who allowed their humiliation so that they would repent, and He is able to humiliate them and also able to deliver them if they repent.

Do not be lax with your sins that you have grown accustomed to, or accept strange sins that the world offers you, so that you anger God and ruin your soul. Do not forget the fear of Him and the torment that awaits you if you persist in this evil. Return quickly, for He loves you and is ready to accept your repentance and to lift from you all these troubles that you brought upon yourself. Temporary pleasure leaves bitterness within you, so do not be deceived by it.

Thy yoke: a crosswise piece of wood placed on the necks of animals, from which another piece of wood extends, at the end of which is the agricultural implement, and it is tied to the necks of the animals by a rope; so it represents the weight and the toil that animals bear in pulling agricultural implements.
Hill: a mound where they offer worship to idols.

God compares His people to animals that people exploited to do their work. God broke the bonds of their servitude when they were in Egypt and gave them freedom to worship Him in the wilderness of Sinai, and then in Canaan, but they returned and enslaved themselves to the pagan gods that they worshiped on the hills or under the shade of trees. He calls idol worship harlotry, because His people, like a bride, turned away from her bridegroom and clung to another, the idol; this is spiritual adultery. Idol worship was also often tied to bodily adultery in order to please the gods.
Noble vine: the finest kind of vine.
Plant: branches.
Vine: a grapevine.

God rebukes His people and compares them to a grapevine of the finest kinds, which God planted when He taught them the truth in the wilderness of Sinai by His commandments and laws. How then did they turn aside from Him and become a strange vine that bears bad fruit? That is, why did they leave His worship and walking in the truth for the worship of idols and walking in evil?!
Nitre: an alkaline salt found in the earth mixed with dust, used like soap for cleaning, and extracted from the soap plant.
Soap: a plant whose ashes, when burned, become suitable for cleaning like good soap.

God rebukes Jerusalem, saying that her concern for the outward forms of worship, or for outward displays of greatness and morals, will not profit her at all; all kinds of cleansing agents, of which the best known are nitre and soap, will not remove her sin from her, because it is engraved on stone before God and cannot be erased except by repentance and returning to Him.
The valley: the valley of Hinnom, in which they offer human sacrifices to the pagan gods, that is, their children, to please the idols.
Dromedary: the female camel, whose nature is to move lightly to the right and to the left, so it signifies being carried away after strange gods.
Hyena: the female hyena, which digs in the ground to eat rotting corpses, so it signifies seeking evil and base lusts.

Jerusalem denied her worship of idols and her defilement by them, so God answers her, bearing witness against her to what she did in the valley of Hinnom by offering her children as sacrifices to the pagan gods. He compares her to a camel running to the right and to the left after the pagan gods, and to a hyena in her search for defiled lusts.
Ass: the female donkey.
The wild ass: the wild donkey.
Used to the wilderness: running in every direction in the desert, and it signifies the female running after every man.
Snuffeth up the wind: an expression of the uselessness of all she does, for she does not breathe in a beautiful fragrance, but wind that has no scent.
In her occasion: in her searching like the hyena for dead corpses, which signifies seeking base lusts. Weary themselves: grow tired.
In her month: the months suitable for mating among animals.

God also compares Jerusalem to the female wild ass that is used to running in the desert, that is, she runs after the pagan gods of the surrounding nations; and when she persists in her lust she is never satisfied, but is as if she were sniffing the wind, and she searches like the hyena for dead corpses, that is, she runs after satisfying her evil lusts. She is like the harlot, whom none who seek her need weary themselves to find, because she offers herself to him and is ready for adultery throughout the period of mating, that is, the months of mating. By this God rebukes her for running after the worship of idols and her constant seeking of defiled lusts.
There is no hope: she rejected God's warning and His admonition.

He continues to compare her to the harlot who runs barefoot after every man and has become thirsty for a lust of which she is never satisfied. For sin makes a person lose his dignity, that is, the wearing of shoes, and makes him never satisfied, but he feels deprivation and the increasing burning of lust within him.

But when God warned Jerusalem of barefootedness and thirst, she rejected His word and declared shamelessly her love of adultery with every stranger; this applies to the various idol worships, and likewise to the persistence in lusts and adultery that was tied to these worships and spread in their lives.

He compares them to the thief who delights in what he steals, but whose shame is great when he is caught. So it is, not only with the people in Jerusalem, but also with all their groups, whether the priests, or the kings, or the prophets.
A stock: idols made of wood, that is, stems or sticks of plants.
A stone: idols made of stones.

The people of God persisted in their sins, and worshiped idols made of wood or stones and called them fathers and mothers and protectors for themselves to keep them in their lives; and by this they left God and gave Him their backs. And when they fall into trials and their pagan gods do not help them, they ask God to deliver them, forgetting that they rebelled and disobeyed Him, so they know Him only because of their need.

God mocks them and says to them: call upon your pagan gods, which have become very many, as many as the cities of the kingdom of Judah, since each city chose for itself one or more of the pagan gods. He says to them: seek them to save you if they can, and of course they have no power, because they are merely statues.
God continues His rebuke of them because they stood as adversaries to Him and disobeyed Him by their worship of the pagan gods.

God declares with sorrow that discipline does not profit them, for they did not return to God in repentance. When He sent His prophets to them to rebuke them for their evils, they rose against them and killed them with the sword or in some other way, so they were like lions devouring the righteous prophets whom God sent to bring them back to Him.

Do not resist God's warnings and rebukes to you that come to you through your father of confession, or your guides, or all those around you, for He wants your salvation. Obey His commandments, submit to His Church and humble yourself before everyone, and you will find your rest and your salvation.

God continues His rebuke of His people who rejected His word, and asks in protest about the reason for their distance from Him, saying: have I been to you a dry, barren wilderness without life, or a land of very great darkness? And why have you wandered, that is, gone far from Me and refused to return to Me? For I was always a light and life to you, as I cared for you in the wilderness of Sinai and in Canaan.

God declares that He is the ornament of His people and the garments of righteousness that clothe them. It is reasonable for a bride to care for her ornaments and her attire, that is, her clothing and everything connected with it that is worn around the waist; so why has Jerusalem, as the bride of God, forgotten her Bridegroom, who is her ornament and her splendor?

He rebukes Jerusalem that she seeks after the worship of idols as a bride seeks the one she loves, or as the harlot seeks those who desire her and whom she loves. Jerusalem sought evil love, that is, the love of idol worship and base lusts, and even taught her sons and daughters this evil; and by the wicked women is meant her daughters.

He adds another sin found in Jerusalem, which is injustice, which He expresses as the blood of the souls of the poor innocents. The sins of Jerusalem are plain and need no digging or searching, but are visible in all her houses and streets.

The evil of Jerusalem increased in that she did not confess her sins but tried to justify herself, and claimed that she was innocent of all evil, and that for this reason God had not punished her until now. Therefore God answers her that she ... that God will judge her and punish her.

God also rebukes Jerusalem for her running to seek help from Egypt, as she ran in the past to seek help from Assyria, which attacked her, destroyed her cities and took captive the whole northern kingdom. Why then does she run now toward Egypt? So He calls her to repent and return to Him instead of resorting to human beings to deliver her from her calamities, or taking refuge from Babylon, which threatens her.
Thine hands upon thine head: in captivity the prisoners go out with their hands on their heads, and this may also happen in the case of intense grief at the death of loved ones.

God declares His punishment of Jerusalem for her disobedience: that she will be taken captive and go out of her land as prisoners go out, in intense grief and humiliation, and those in whom she trusted, such as Egypt and Assyria, “thy confidences,” will not profit her. This is what actually happened years later when Babylon attacked and took Jerusalem and Judea captive, because she did not listen to the voice of God through the prophet Jeremiah and did not repent of her sins.

Remember that your soul is a bride of Christ, and her joy and her greatness are to cling to Him and to be adorned with the virtues that He gives her. So give enough time to being with God, and remove your sins by repentance, and you will keep your beauty as a bride adorned for her bridegroom.
A call to repentance and the hating of sin

The Law states in (Deut 24:1-4) that if a man divorces his wife and she becomes another man's, he may not take her back as his wife afterwards. But God addresses Jerusalem, or His people the Jews, as a bride of His who left Him and attached herself to the worship of idols with many gods, that is, she committed spiritual adultery many times; and yet God shows His surpassing love in His readiness to receive her as His wife a second time if she repents and returns to Him. The love of God surpasses human feelings, which refuse to take back a woman who has lain with others.

God compares His people to the harlot who sits by the road waiting for her customers, or to the Arab who sits in the desert; that is, His people longed for the worship of idols and for clinging to evil lusts, and yet God is ready to receive them if they return to Him in repentance.
Showers: rain.

The latter rain: which falls at the end of the planting season, that is, in the months of March and April. A whore's forehead: the harlot used to put a mark on her forehead so that her customers could easily recognize her, so the forehead of the harlot signifies shamelessness.

Nature expressed its distress at the adultery of the people of God by the withholding of rain, and consequently the drying up of crops and the occurrence of hunger, so that perhaps the affliction would alert the people of God who persisted in adultery; but sadly they refused to obey the commandments of God and return to Him in repentance.

If Jerusalem repents, she remembers God's fatherhood and His care for her in the wilderness of Sinai, and calls Him the guide of her youth, when she enjoyed fellowship with Him and rejoiced in His care.

God is tender, even if He is angry with His people because of their many sins, and even if He allows them the affliction of captivity, it is a temporary affliction, because He returns and receives them and forgives them in spite of all the sins that they committed with insistence and stubbornness; He receives them if they return to Him.

If God is merciful and forgiving toward you whatever your sins may be, then be long-suffering also toward those around you whatever their sins may be. Be merciful and find excuses for others, so that you deserve the mercies of God.

entries.section: (2) Judah's not returning in spite of the captivity of Israel

paragraphs.text: Israel: this includes the ten tribes and is called the northern kingdom, whose capital was Samaria. Jeroboam the son of Nebat divided it after the death of King Solomon, and two tribes remained, Judah and Benjamin, which formed the southern kingdom, called the kingdom of Judah, whose capital was Jerusalem, where the temple was, and Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned over it. The captivity of Israel took place at the hands of the Assyrians, and Judah remained in the days of Jeremiah, but it was taken captive afterwards by Babylon, also during the lifetime of Jeremiah.

The prophecy of Jeremiah began in the thirteenth year of King Josiah, which means that these words were the first of Jeremiah's prophecies that God instructed him in. God spoke to him about the corruption of the kingdom of Israel by its worship of idols on the mountains and also under the shade of trees, that is, it fell into the worship of many pagan gods.

entries.section: (2) Judah's not returning in spite of the captivity of Israel

paragraphs.text: In spite of all the evil that the kingdom of Israel did, God called it to repentance through many prophets, such as Isaiah, but it refused to return to Him; and Judah saw Israel's persistence in its disobedience and its rejection of the prophets, and did not take warning but imitated it.

entries.section: (2) Judah's not returning in spite of the captivity of Israel

paragraphs.text: The reasons: all the evils that Israel did.

A bill of divorce: God rejected her and left her to captivity so that she would be joined to foreign kings who would rule over her. God was long-suffering toward Israel so that she might repent, but she did not repent, so He had to allow her the affliction of captivity, hoping that she might repent. But the kingdom of Judah did not learn from God's punishment of Israel, but she too continued in her spiritual adultery, that is, the worship of idols.

entries.section: (2) Judah's not returning in spite of the captivity of Israel

paragraphs.text: The lightness of her whoredom: the humiliation and shame of her adultery.
Stones: the stone statues of the pagan gods.
Stocks: idols made of wood, or wooden pagan temples. Judah persisted in her evil and fell into the worship of what are not gods, that is, the stone and wooden idols, and left God, her true God.

entries.section: (2) Judah's not returning in spite of the captivity of Israel

paragraphs.text: Judah fell into another sin, which was her pretending to return to God by way of outward worship, so she was false in this return.

entries.section: (2) Judah's not returning in spite of the captivity of Israel

paragraphs.text: By the multitude of Judah's falls she became worse than Israel, who became more justified before God than Judah. For Judah's sin is that she did not learn from God's warning to her through the captivity of Israel, and then she persisted in the worship of idols and refused repentance, hiding behind superficial worship without spirit.

If God alerts you to return to Him in repentance, do not be lax, and do not think that the presence of some social virtues, or people's praise of you, or your attachment to the form of worship in the Church will defend you before God, for there is no way to obtain true righteousness except by repentance.
Toward the north: toward the kingdom of Israel, although it was taken captive to Assyria and only a few Jews remained in it, yet by the prophecy he calls all the captives.

Jeremiah now directs his prophecy to the northern kingdom of Israel, which was taken captive because of its evil, and in his prophecy he shows how Israel is to repent, which is summarized in the following:
1- Returning to God, for there is no solution to all their problems except faith in God and life with Him.
2- Trust in the mercy of God, for He is very compassionate, tender and forgiving.
You have scattered your ways to the strangers under every green tree: this means the worship of strange gods under the trees, where statues of idols were set up.
He continues to lay down steps of repentance:
3- Examining the soul to know its iniquity and its sin.
4- Obeying God, because sin is disobedience to Him.
5- Every sin that a person commits toward others is directed against God, and he must repent of it before God: “You have sinned against the LORD your God.”

I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion: He gathers the people of Israel scattered in the Assyrian kingdom and brings them back from captivity to Jerusalem when they repent. He continues the steps of repentance, saying:
6- Trust in the sonship of God, so I reject the sins that anger Him.
7- God is the only King over the heart, and He solves all problems and brings Israel back from captivity, so it is necessary to return to Him in repentance for the solution of problems.

Look at the tenderness of God and His love that calls you to repentance, so that you are not distressed by the multitude of your sins; for even if you grow weary and hate yourself, God still loves you and is ready to restore to you your splendor and your joy.
According to mine heart: they agree with the will of God.
Knowledge and understanding: knowing the commandments of God and understanding them by His Holy Spirit.
God rejoices in the repentance of His people and gives them many blessings, which are:
1- He gives them pastors, that is, priests and teachers submitted to Him, who speak His word and are faithful in their care of the people.

Neither shall it be done any more: they will no longer perform the worship, or the sacrifices and offerings that are offered in the temple of Solomon. He continues the blessings of repentance, saying:

2- A prophecy about Christianity, when the believers in Christ multiply and no longer need a symbol of the presence of God, which is the Ark of the Covenant, but Jerusalem, that is, the Church of the New Testament, becomes the throne of the Lord and spreads in every place, so that the Gentiles believe in Christ and repent of their straying and their stubbornness in sin.
The land of the north: where they were captive in Babylon.
The land that I have given for an inheritance unto your fathers: the land of Canaan, that is, Jerusalem and Judea.

3- The return from the captivity, which happened at the beginning of the kingdom of the Medes and Persians, when the Jews return, whether from the kingdom of Judah or the kingdom of Israel, and worship the LORD in Jerusalem.
How shall I put thee: it expresses the greatness of the grace of sonship, whose beauty cannot be expressed.
Ye shall not turn away from me: steadfastness in eternal happiness and life with God.

4- The grace of sonship that God gives to His bride, that is, His people, so that she calls Him her Father after He has brought her back from captivity and given her the desirable land of Canaan as an inheritance, which He took from the wicked nations that He drove out before her. The land of Canaan signifies the Church of the New Testament with all the desirable things of the work of the Holy Spirit in it, and it signifies even more the heavenly Jerusalem, in which are all the longings of the souls that loved Christ, and which enjoys the inheritance of the glory of glories that is given to the Gentiles who believed in Christ as an eternal inheritance.

Do not be deceived by the temporary pleasure of sin, for it passes away, but look at the unspeakable blessings that you feel in part in your life on earth and then in heaven, so that you turn to repentance and reject every evil however attached to it you may be.
Her husband: the husband to whom she was joined and united in marriage.

God rebukes His people the children of Israel because they fell into many sins, the most important of which are the worship of idols and adultery and all the sins connected with them. He declares clearly that sin is betrayal of God, since it is clinging to another god, namely the idols and the lusts; and He compares their betrayal to the betrayal of a married woman against her husband by clinging to another man.

The children of Israel plunged into the worship of idols and lusts on high places, such as hills, thinking that on them they draw near to the gods they worship. And on the same places the enemies attacked and seized them and took them captive, so they cried out with bitter weeping because of the evil, the shame and the weakness that came upon them. This is the natural result of sin and of persisting in it.

Do not persist in sin, but if you fall into it, return quickly to God, lest He abandon you and many afflictions come upon you, which He allows because of His love for you, so that you return to Him and find the salvation of your soul.

God intends by afflictions the return to Him of His disobedient children, for He is their Father even while they are in their sins and He seeks the salvation of their souls; and how great is His joy at their repentance and return to Him and their confession that He is their God, and not the strange gods and the evil lusts.
The hills, the multitude of mountains: all the pagan worships that they practiced on these high places in order to draw near to the pagan gods.

When the people return to God they declare the futility of everything they relied on, the strange gods and the evil lusts that they thought were wealth, and they declare that deliverance from every sin and toil, and the gaining of happiness, is from God alone.

Shame hath devoured: one of the effects of sin is that it makes a person lose everything he has, but when the people of God repented they remembered that sin is accompanied by shame and loss, as happened to their fathers when they sinned and lost their possessions of sheep and cattle, and even lost their sons and daughters. Sin is a temporary pleasure with which Satan entices us, but he is fierce, attacking us and devouring the dearest things we have, our children and our resources.

In repentance the people declare that they plunged and lay down in sin and were defiled by it like their fathers, and rejected their loving God and Savior, and this would have led to their eternal destruction, but now they return to God in repentance, so that they may obtain their salvation.
Remember your past and present sins so that they drive you to repent with humility, and you will obtain the mercies of God, for He is a tender Father who cannot reject you whatever your sins may be.
A call to repentance because of the coming ruin
Thine abominations: the idols.
Remove: go astray and depart from God.
God calls His people to repent of their sins, the first and most important of which is to remove the statues of the pagan gods and be rid of them, and so to turn back from the way of their error.

Let your repentance be practical, not only in words, but by cutting off the causes and sources of evil, whether places, or friends, or habits, or viewing, and by beginning spiritual practices, so that you enjoy true repentance and fellowship with God.

The second proof of repentance is not to resort to the pagan gods and trust in them by swearing by them, but to swear by the name of God, the only God on whom His people rely, and by this God blesses His people, and faith even spreads from the people of God to the Gentiles, so that they believe in God and are blessed in their lives, and He becomes their glory and their strength.
Break up: ploughing is an agricultural operation in which the earth is cut open with the blade of the plough and turned over, bringing out the roots of the thorns so that we are rid of them.

The Lord calls to His people in the kingdom of Judah, where His city Jerusalem and His holy temple are, to cleanse their hearts from sin. He compares the heart that is full of evil and then pretends to worship God to ground full of thorns in which good seed is then sown: if this seed sprouts, it will be mixed with thorns. So the ground must first be ploughed to pull out these thorns and be rid of them, and then good plants sown, that is, repentance from sins and purification of the heart, and then the beginning afterwards of holy worship and good works. Circumcise yourselves: this is the cutting of a part of the male reproductive organ, which God commanded Abraham as a sign of his faith and that of his descendants; it signifies the cutting off of evil and the beginning of a new life with God, which is accomplished in the sacrament of Baptism. Foreskins: uncircumcision.

God calls His people not to the physical circumcision but to the spiritual circumcision of hearts, that is, the cutting off of evil from the heart by repentance; and if He means the physical circumcision for those who neglected it, He also means that it should be accompanied by the purification of the heart from every evil as a proof of faith in God.

Then He threatens His people that if they neglect repentance and the purification of their hearts and persist in evil, they thereby provoke God, so He is angry with them and punishes them with a wrath like fire that consumes them, as the Scripture says, “Our God is a consuming fire” (Deut 4:24).

Do not keep any sin in your heart however small, and do not rely on your mastery of worship with its rites and hymns, your knowledge of the Holy Bible, and all the good works you do, for they will not profit you if you do not first repent.

God warns His people of the beginning of the divine wrath against them because of their persistence in evil, so He asks that the trumpet be blown so that the people take refuge in the fortified cities, because the enemies, that is, the Babylonians, will attack and destroy and take them captive.
The fortified cities signify the churches in which the believers of the New Testament take refuge by many prayers, to be delivered from the evils of the world and the wars of the devil.

He warns them by the raising of the standard of war against the Babylonian attack upon them from the north, and cautions them of a great destruction, that is, a crushing defeat that will come upon them.

He compares the Babylonian kingdom to a lion, violent in its attack, coming out of its thicket, that is, Babylon, which destroys cities and kills those in them, while the rest flee and their inhabitants abandon them.

And Babylon, or the lion, signifies Satan, as our teacher Peter says, “Because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour: whom resist stedfast in the faith” (1 Pet 5:8, 9).
Gird you: put on the girdle, which is what is worn on the waist and extends down toward the legs. Sackcloth: coarse garments.

He calls the people so that they may benefit from the affliction of captivity and return to God in repentance, wearing sackcloth as a girdle on their waists and weeping over their sins because of God's wrath against them; and then God receives them, lifts His wrath from them and brings them back from captivity.

From the distress of the enemy's attack, all those responsible for Judah lose their ability to act, whether the king, or the prince, or the priest, or the prophet, because they departed from God and His wrath came upon them.
The sword reacheth unto the soul: the killing of many of the people of God.

The people blame God because He deceived them through the prophets, saying that they would have peace, and then they were surprised by the Babylonians attacking them and killing them. These troubles had not yet happened, but Jeremiah prophesies that they will happen, because the people thought that the false prophets were prophets from God, and they deceived them by prophesying peace to them. This prophecy is a warning to the people of God against listening to the words of the false prophets, and a call to them to repent of their sins, because of which God will bring His wrath upon them and the Babylonian attack.
Fanning: an agricultural operation by which the grains of wheat are separated from the chaff, and the presence of wind helps to accomplish it.

He compares the Babylonian attack to a hot, that is, strong, wind, by which God does not mean to help in agricultural work such as fanning and cleaning the grain, but a violent wind, stronger than the one that helps agricultural operations, which will come from the bare heights, that is, from the high places in the north, that is, Babylon. By this wind or this attack God means to discipline His people and judge them, so that they review themselves and repent.

Do not listen to any teachings foreign to the Church, so that no one leads you astray, and pay attention to the guidance of your father of confession and to prayer, and God will keep you in all your ways and lead you in the way of His Kingdom.
God compares the Babylonian attack, in addition to the lion and the east wind (vv. 7, 8), to the following:
1- Clouds: the enemy will be strong and high above the Jews, and it is not possible to rise to his strength or to repel him.
2- His chariots shall be as a whirlwind: the enemy's war chariots will be strong as a whirlwind, sweeping and overwhelming the Jewish people before them.
3- His horses are swifter than eagles: the enemy's horsemen riding on horses attack with lightning speed as eagles swoop on their prey, killing and capturing the Jews.
The cities of Judah will be destroyed because of the force of the Babylonian attack. All this is by God's permission to discipline His people so that they repent of their sins.

God calls His people in the kingdom of Judah, in the person of the capital Jerusalem, to wash their sins by repentance, that they may be saved from this discipline, because their evil is the cause of these afflictions. He regards all their worship of idols and their evils as vain and without profit, and indeed as the cause of all this punishment.

The only way out for you, and the first thing you do when you fall into an affliction, is to repent of your sins and ask in faith and humility that God lift it from you, so that you are washed in the sacrament of confession and partake of the Holy Mysteries, and are strengthened and your life is renewed.

Here he speaks of the affliction of the northern kingdom of Israel when the Assyrians attacked it, and mentions some of its regions, namely the city of Dan and its surroundings, then the tribe of Ephraim, which holds the largest area in the kingdom of Israel, and how they all felt the calamity that came upon them as a discipline from God.
The nations: the armies of Babylon.
Publish against: declare against.
Give out their voice against the cities of Judah: they occupy them and take control of them.
God commands the prophet to warn Jerusalem that the armies of Babylon, coming from afar, will attack her and besiege her and all the land of Judea and occupy it.

He declares the reason for the discipline of the kingdom of Judah, which is her disobedience and her rebellion against God by the multitude of her sins, so He allowed the Babylonians to besiege her like watchers who surround those they guard, but this guarding is against Judea and not a protection for them.
These: the afflictions that came upon Judea.
Here he affirms the bitterness of the sin that Jerusalem and Judea committed; it was not merely outward faults but came from the heart, so it caused all this distress and humiliation.

entries.section: (5) The prophet's grief for his people

paragraphs.text: Here appear the tender feelings of Jeremiah, who suffers greatly because of the ruin coming upon the kingdom of Judah on account of her sins, and the war and the sound of its trumpet announcing the Babylonian attack, and it appears that his grief is very deep in his bowels and his heart.

May you, as a father, or a mother, or a servant, feel for those you care for, and suffer with their sufferings even if they are stubborn and provoke you, and lift up prayers for them, and continue to offer them your love, and do not despair of their repentance and their salvation.

entries.section: (5) The prophet's grief for his people

paragraphs.text: Destruction upon destruction: defeat following defeat.
My curtains: pieces of cloth set up for dwelling inside them.

The prophet continues his suffering because of the series of defeats that will come upon his people, and cries out everywhere about their coming upon them and about the destruction of their dwellings, to which he refers as tents and curtains. What is meant is not only the tents but also the buildings in which they live.

entries.section: (5) The prophet's grief for his people

paragraphs.text: Here he makes clear that the Babylonian attack continues for a long time and is repeated against the kingdom of Judah, so that he is no longer able to see the standard of war raised against his people, and the trumpet announcing the continuation of the attack.

entries.section: (5) The prophet's grief for his people

paragraphs.text: Here he affirms the reason for this ruin, which is the ignorance and foolishness of the people of God, who departed from His worship and from taking refuge in Him. Although they are the children of God, they did not realize the importance of sonship, and did not live by it in obedience to their Father. On the contrary, they directed their minds and abilities to doing sin instead of worshiping God and doing good.

The prophet shows the results of the Babylonian attack on the kingdom of Judah, and declares the devastation of the land, the emigration of people from the ruined cities, and the disappearance of the inhabitants, with the burning of cities rising to heaven, so that the heavens no longer gave their light through the sun and the moon.

The people of God worshiped the pagan gods on the mountains and hills, which they thought a symbol of strength because of their height, but now they are worthless before the Babylonian attack, and the pagan gods were not able to protect them, and their weakness is expressed by the shaking and trembling of these high places.

The earth signifies the people, and the heavens the priests and pastors, while the mountains and hills signify the leaders, that is, all became humiliated before this ruin because of their sins and their distance from God.

The Jews fled in fear for their lives from the face of the Babylonians, and even the birds of the heavens could not remain because of the fires and the noise and all the disturbance of war, so there was no longer rest or safety for anyone, neither for man nor for beast.

The orchards and fields and all the cultivated lands turned into ruin and became like the barren desert. All this ruin was by God's permission, using the power of the Babylonians in it, to declare His wrath against His people so that they repent and return to Him.

It is noted that he said the word “I beheld” four times in the four preceding verses, as if he were calling out in the four directions of the world, warning all the people, so that they repent, because of the ruin coming upon them.
The love of God appears, who allows ruin, but not complete ruin; He leaves a remnant, because He does not intend their destruction but their repentance.

God declares His determination to discipline His people; He does everything so that they repent when they enter into this distress and weeping over what they have come to, so that they lose their confidence in the pagan gods and return to God.

He declares the signs of the ruin brought about by the Babylonian attack with its horsemen, the archers. The signs of this ruin are the flight of all, the destruction of the cities, and people's taking refuge in the forests and mountains and sheltering behind the rocks so that they would not die.
Crimson: garments of a dark red color worn by kings and the great.
Antimony: the kohl that is put around the eyes.

God addresses the kingdom of Judah, which will be destroyed by the Babylonians, and warns her against relying on her own strength, that is, self-righteousness. He compares her to a woman who wears costly crimson garments and adorns herself with gold and silver, and puts cosmetics on her face, such as kohl, to show her beauty, and He says to her that all this will not profit you and the Babylonians will ruin you. By this He points to the necessity that His people not rely on the outward forms of worship, and the presence of the temple among them in Jerusalem, or on their strength, or their strange gods, for all this is worthless before the wrath of God, and the only solution is repentance with humility.
Travailing: the woman who gives birth and is in pain with the pangs of childbirth.

The anguish as of her that bringeth forth her first child: the woman in her first childbirth suffers more pains than one who has given birth more than once. Sigh: breathes out the air from her nose and mouth with a clear sound, a sign of severe pain.

He goes on with his comparisons to show the sufferings of his people, and compares the kingdom of Judah to a woman giving birth and in pain with the pangs of childbirth; indeed, he declares that her pains are severe like the pains of one giving birth for the first time, and the sound of her sighing declares her agonies, and from the abundance of suffering and grief she throws herself on the ground, spreading out her arms and hands, and loses consciousness because of all that she sees of the ferocity of the Babylonian attack.
Humble yourself in repentance for all your sins, and you will save your soul by the mercies of God from many afflictions and obtain an unspeakable peace.
God's discipline of Jerusalem so that she repents

All the people of God in Jerusalem were led along the way of evil, so they deserved divine punishment; but God in His tenderness wants to pardon them through the intercession of one person who lives by truth and justice, and He asks that such a one be sought, but sadly none was found.

God in His love searches for any good work and virtue in you in order to forgive you and support you with His fatherhood, so do not neglect any opportunity to do good, or to pray and be with God, so that you draw out His mercies whatever your sins may be.

The evil of the people of God appears in their pretending to have a relationship with Him and to worship Him, such as swearing by His name and not by the pagan gods; but sadly this oath was false. This evil is an example of many evils within them that they try to cover with their outward worship.

God looks for truth in the souls of His children, and when He found that they had persisted in evil, He struck them with discipline, whether by words of rebuke or by afflictions, but they were not affected, their hearts were not pained and they did not repent, but they disregarded the word and the discipline as if it were not meant for them.
When God allowed them partial destruction, that is, the loss of some of their possessions, or afflictions to come upon them, they murmured, but they did not return to God in repentance.
Also their hearts were not affected, and no response to the word of God appeared on their faces, but they hardened their faces and did not submit to Him.
The judgment of their God: God's punishment of whoever rejects His commandments.
Jeremiah describes them as poor, because of their distance from the knowledge of God; that is, they passed the sentence of destruction on themselves by rejecting God.

God commanded Jeremiah to speak to the proud, that is, those who are great in their own eyes, who are the students of the word of God, the opposite of the poor and ignorant; but they became proud of this knowledge and did not use it for repentance, but cast off the commandments of God because they felt them to be a yoke and a heavy bond upon them, and by this they insisted on the way of destruction.
In the end, for those who persist in evil there is nothing but to receive the divine punishment through the attack of the armies of Babylon upon them, and he compared it:
1- To a lion that comes from the desert and devours everyone it meets, because of its irresistible strength.
2- To the wolf that goes out in the evening and at night to devour anyone, especially since the wolf devours even if it has been satisfied with its previous prey.
3- To a leopard in its hiding, which may last for several days until it finds the right opportunity and pounces on its prey.
All these comparisons show the ferocity of the Babylonian enemy who attacks His people to discipline them because of their many sins.

God rebukes Jerusalem and the kingdom of Judah, declaring that He will not pardon the iniquities of her sons, because they trusted in the pagan gods and swore by them, instead of worshiping God and trusting in Him alone. In the same verse He rebukes them because they used His gifts for evil: when He gave them many good things they did not worship Him and thank Him, but rushed into lusts such as bodily adultery, in addition to their worship of idols, which is spiritual adultery. And from the abundance of their evil they were not ashamed of their sin, but shamelessly thronged to the houses of harlots to satisfy their lusts.
If you commit any sin, hasten to repentance, and do not try to justify your sins before people, lest you lose your shame and your sense of remorse and persist in sin.
Horses: the plural of horse.
Fed: having eaten their food in abundance.
Neighed: the sound of the horse; that is, they cried out and rushed to fulfill their lusts.

He affirms the same meaning mentioned in the preceding verse by God's comparing His people to animals that have eaten much, so that every male rushes to commit adultery with his neighbor's wife, and these animals are loose, that is, without restraint, because lusts have taken control of them.

God asks whether He will not punish for such an appalling evil and avenge Himself on a nation, or a people, that persists in evil?! And the answer, of course, is that He avenges and punishes, and this is what happened in the Babylonian captivity.
Battlements: her branches.

God commands, through the mouth of His prophet Jeremiah, the armies of Babylon to go up on the walls of Jerusalem and enter the city and destroy it and cut off its branches, that is, every strength she relies on, or fruit that appears in her, because she directed her resources to evil and not to God; but the love of God and His fatherhood appear in His forbidding them to destroy Jerusalem completely, for He intends to discipline her and not to destroy her.

When afflictions come upon you, know that they are by God's permission to alert you to repent and return to Him, but in His tenderness He is ready to help you, so that you make up for all that you have missed and return with greater strength than you had before.
God judges the idol worship of His people as a betrayal of Him, and it is a grievous sin.

The people deceived themselves through the false prophets, expecting that no evil would befall them (expressed as the sword and famine) whatever their sins, and they thought that the mere presence of the temple of God among them in Jerusalem would protect them. By this deception they left God and relied on the pagan gods, because in their eyes they were the true God, and so they exposed themselves to the divine punishment.
God judges the false prophets as mere wind, and their words have no value at all; their speech is like the air that cannot be held, and the word of God has no relation to their words.

The mighty God, who expresses Himself as the LORD of hosts, declares that He will put powerful words in the mouth of His prophet Jeremiah that will be like a fire that easily burns the wicked people. He compares them to wood, that is, dry stalks of plants. By this He means His punishment of His wicked people.
The punishment of God on the kingdom of Judah appears in His allowing Babylon to take vengeance on them, and He describes Babylon as:
1- A nation that comes from afar to take vengeance on them because they rejected their God who was near.
2- Strong in its army, which will shatter the kingdom of Judah.
3- It has an ancient history; it has been strong for a long time and will grow in strength.
4- It has a strange language, so it is impossible to understand it, and it signifies the demons, whose language is evil, foreign to the children of God.
Their quiver: the case in which the arrows are placed.
He expresses their strength in that their arrows are deadly to the people of God, and they are mighty men who will destroy Jerusalem.
Thy vines: your vineyard.
He continues the description of Babylon, that it is:

5- Exploitative and fierce, so it eats the food of the people of God sown in the fields, and likewise the animals they raise, in addition to the fruit of the trees, such as the grapes and figs for which the Jews are famous in their land.
6- It will destroy all the fortified cities on which the people of God rely, because they did not trust in Him.
God affirms His love and His hope for His people, that He will not destroy them but only discipline them, that perhaps they will repent.

When the kingdom of Judah falls into captivity, the people of God murmur, saying: why did God, whom we worship in His temple in Jerusalem, leave us? Ignoring their disobedience to God by the worship of idols in Jerusalem and Judea, so God allowed them to be taken captive to a foreign land whose people worship these gods. For God had cleansed the Promised Land for them and settled them in it to worship Him, but they defiled it with the worship of idols once again, so the land cast them out, and they lost the place with which God had blessed them because of their disobedience to Him.

Keep the grace that God has given you, walk in purity, and thank Him for His gifts, and He will continue His grace to you. But if you neglect Him and are occupied with the world and sin, know that all the graces of God that you have can leave you, and if you lose any of them, do not murmur, but repent and return to God, and He will forgive you and restore His grace to you.

God rebukes His people who believed in Him and lived with Him, but then returned and lost their spiritual senses and fell into ignorance by their disobedience to God and their worship of idols, so that they no longer saw the truth and understood the will of God.

God is astonished at the disobedience of His people and their lack of fear of Him, and He has to remind them through Jeremiah that He is the Controller of all, who sets limits for the sea and for the sandy shores and controls everything in the world; so how is it that His children do not fear Him but worship other gods besides Him to provoke Him?!

God also marvels at their persistence in disobedience and their continuing in the worship of idols, forgetting that it is He who gives them their food by the early and the latter rain that waters the plants, so that they eat of them and live; for without Him they would die of hunger.
God affirms that the reason for the distress and the captivity into which His people will fall, and which will deprive them of all good things, is their sins and their worship of idols.

As he that setteth snares: they crouch at the side of the road, lie in wait and hide, to pounce on people and catch them, that is, seize them, and rob them of their money and take them as their slaves. Snares: traps, or ways to seize people and exploit them and wrong them.

He makes clear some of their sins for which God punishes them, which are their cunning, and their hunting of people by hiding in the roads to rob money and to kill, that is, their practice of every act of injustice.

He also makes clear that their houses, that is, their hearts and thoughts, are full of evil, so they do not fall into injustice by oversight but with insistence and deliberately. He compares their wicked hearts, which deprive people of their freedom, to a cage in which some birds are shut up and kept from freedom and flight; they enslave others and exploit their abilities, and by this injustice they became rich and held great positions, but they are rejected by God, and He will punish them with captivity.

Their strength increased because of their evil, and their strength is expressed by fatness, and their great position by shining, and this drove them to increase in evil and in oppressing the weak, such as orphans and widows, whose rights they robbed; that is, they had outward material success, but their hearts were filled with evil, and deserved divine punishment.
God affirms that they deserve severe punishment for their many evils.
What will ye do in the end thereof: no one can rescue this people from the wrath that will come upon them in the captivity.

He declares that the earth marvels at the evil that happens upon it from His people. The prophets shared in the lie by deceptive prophecies, saying “peace” to the people, and did not rebuke them for their sins that they might repent. The priests joined them and supported them in their false statements, so the people persisted in their evils, supported by their deceiving leaders, and consequently a sad end awaits them, which is punishment by captivity.

When an opportunity comes to you to take the right of another, do not think that you gain anything, but you stir up the wrath of God against you. So be faithful in all your dealings, because God sees you and repays you with good or evil according to your works. The sins that caused the destruction of Jerusalem

Children of Benjamin: the tribe of Benjamin, which is part of the kingdom of Judah whose capital is Jerusalem. Jeremiah calls them because they represent the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the whole kingdom of Judah.
Tekoa: a city about 12 miles south of Jerusalem, and it was the home of the prophet Amos.
Beth-haccerem: a city on a hill south of Jerusalem on the road to Bethlehem, which is five miles from Jerusalem.

Jeremiah warns the inhabitants of Jerusalem that its destruction by the armies of Babylon has drawn near, and asks those who believe his word to flee from it so that they do not die. He also declares that the destruction will be throughout the land of Judea surrounding Jerusalem, and he chooses from it Tekoa and Beth-haccerem.
He also affirms that the attack is fierce like fire that consumes everything it meets, so there will be destruction, that is, a great defeat for the kingdom of Judah.

With the eye of a father, God sees the kingdom of Judah as His beautiful and gentle daughter, even though she disobeyed God and persisted in her evil, so He had to discipline her by the Babylonian attack, that perhaps she would repent and return to her spiritual beauty and gentleness.

After Jerusalem is destroyed and becomes deserted with no one living in it, the shepherds come to it with their flocks to feed around it and pitch their tents there, so it is no longer a city but merely a wilderness in which sheep graze.
Prepare: set apart.

God calls the armies of Babylon to wage a mighty war against Jerusalem to discipline her, so they attack her at noon and in the evening and during the night, that is, they attack her at all times until they destroy her; and therefore the inhabitants of Jerusalem groan at the declining of the day, that is, in the evening, because of the attack coming upon them, and likewise at the coming of night, that is, when the shadows of evening lengthen, because they are surprised by a new attack while the war continues.

This is a fourth attack, during the night, in which they destroy her greatest dwellings, which are called palaces. The Babylonians attacked Jerusalem at noon, in the evening, at the coming of night, and during the night.

When any affliction comes upon you, flee to God by repentance and prayer, and if the affliction increases, do not be distressed, because God who loves you allows it so that you draw near to Him. The affliction does not destroy you, but proves you and makes you grow in the way of the love of God.
A mount: walls built around the besieged city, behind which the enemies stand to prevent its inhabitants from escaping.

God affirms the ruin and destruction that will come upon Jerusalem, for the Babylonians will destroy the areas surrounding Jerusalem and cut down its trees, and then place them against its walls and set fire to them, so the fire attacks the inhabitants of the city from every side and burns them, and if they try to flee they find that the enemies have set up barricades and stand behind them to kill the inhabitants of Jerusalem and prevent them from escaping. All this divine punishment is because its inhabitants fell into the sin of injustice and did not have mercy on the poor, so God did not have mercy on them and allowed their discipline so that they repent.

God declares that the evil of Jerusalem is continual like a spring of water from which water flows constantly, so its inhabitants wrong one another and seize and rob one another, and the weak were afflicted with sicknesses as a result of the injustice of their brothers toward them, and their beating them and assaulting them in various ways.
Lest my soul depart from thee: from estrangement, that is, God rejects her and abandons her.

God warns Jerusalem that He will abandon her if she rejects discipline and does not repent, and so He will allow her more afflictions, namely the Babylonian devastation and destruction, that perhaps she also will return and repent.
Do not wrong another however easy it may be for you, because the just God sees everything, and will punish you for your selfishness and your injustice if you do not return the rights to their owners.

entries.section: (3) The causes of the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: They shall throughly glean: after the grapes are gathered they go through the fields to gather any scattered grapes that remain. Vine: a grapevine.

God declares that the Babylonians will destroy Jerusalem again and again until she is completely destroyed, as grapes are gathered from the vine again and again until hardly a single grape remains on it, and finally God stops them from doing that. So He says to the grape gatherer, put your hand into the basket in which you gather the grapes and do not pick any other grape, so that a remnant remains for His people to repent and return to Him. The conclusion is that the destruction of Jerusalem will be severe.

entries.section: (3) The causes of the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Their ear is uncircumcised: that is, not circumcised, and it means that their ear is stopped from hearing the voice of God, and their inclination to evil has not been cut off, because circumcision signifies the cutting off of the evil nature and faith in God and sonship to Him.

The prophet marvels that he finds no one who hears the word of God, but they stop their ears and neglect His warnings, and more than this they regard the word of God as a reproach, that is, they despise it and reject it, since they rejected the words of Jeremiah and tortured him and threw him into prison because of the word of God with which he warns them, and they regarded obedience to God by submission to Babylon as a reproach, that is, they rejected the divine discipline, so their cities were destroyed and they were killed by the sword.

entries.section: (3) The causes of the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The fury of the LORD: the wrath of God.
I am weary with holding in: they exhausted all of God's long-suffering toward them, so His wrath came upon them.
Him that is full of days: the aged or the old man.

Jeremiah is the voice of God, so he declares that he is full of the divine wrath after the inhabitants of Jerusalem exhausted all their opportunities for repentance, so they deserved death, but God allowed them discipline so that they repent. And He commanded Jeremiah to declare God's pouring out His wrath on all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children and the young men and the elders and the aged, because they fell into evil and rejected the commandments of God.

entries.section: (3) The causes of the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Because the people of God wronged one another, He allowed them the Babylonian captivity, which plundered their houses and violated their wives, so the Babylonians were the outstretched hand of God to discipline His people.

entries.section: (3) The causes of the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: He showed that the reason for their discipline is their refusal to hear the voice of God (v. 10), and here two other reasons for their discipline appear:
1- Their attachment to the love of money, all of them, both great and small.
2- Their falling into deceit and lying as leaders of the people, who are the priests and the prophets, so the people were led after them.

entries.section: (3) The causes of the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Covetousness: corruption.

The fourth sin that caused God's discipline of His people is their superficiality and shallowness in treating their problems, so they tried to treat their spiritual diseases and their inner corruption with deceit, as the prophets said to them “Peace, peace” and it will not come upon you, that is, divine discipline; and it would have been better for them to treat their wounds by uncovering them to God by repentance and returning to Him, and He would heal them.

entries.section: (3) The causes of the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Abomination: uncleanness and evil.

The fifth sin that caused discipline for the people of God is persisting in evil, and not being ashamed of their sins and repenting of them, so they deserved discipline and killing and various disciplines.
Do not persist in your sins if God alerts you to repent of them, and return to Him, for He is merciful, and He will forgive you every evil and you will return with greater strength.
