entries.section: (4) Rejection of the commandments and outward worship

paragraphs.text: God asked His people to review themselves, whether their conduct is sound or mistaken, and asked them to stand at the way of their life to make sure of the soundness of their actions, because they had turned aside in the worship of idols, and He also asked them to look at all their conduct and examine it and ask for the old paths, that is, the books of Moses and the word of God through the prophets, and measure their lives against them, so that if they discover the right way, that is, the commandments of God, they walk in it, and enjoy inner rest and peace from God. But sadly they refused to review themselves so as to walk in the sound ways of the fathers.

entries.section: (4) Rejection of the commandments and outward worship

paragraphs.text: God appointed the prophets as watchmen over His people, to make them hear His voice like a trumpet warning them so that they return to Him, but they refused.

entries.section: (4) Rejection of the commandments and outward worship

paragraphs.text: God calls the pagan nations and the peoples of the world as witnesses to the rebellion and disobedience of His people and the sins in which they walk, since their sins exceeded the sins of the nations.

entries.section: (4) Rejection of the commandments and outward worship

paragraphs.text: He also calls the earth and the people and creatures on it as witnesses to the disobedience of His people, and warns them that He will punish them with disciplines that are the natural result of their evil thoughts and their rejection of the commandments of God.

entries.section: (4) Rejection of the commandments and outward worship

paragraphs.text: Sheba: a state living in the south-west of the Arabian Peninsula, that is, present-day Yemen.

Frankincense: a gummy substance produced from the frankincense plant, which has a sweet smell when burned. Sweet cane: a kind of reed with a sweet smell, and the word “sweet” means a fragrant scent. God declares His displeasure with the offerings and burnt offerings of His people, in which they spend great effort, importing incense materials such as frankincense and sweet cane from distant places like Sheba. This is because this worship is superficial, while their hearts are full of evil, and consequently their worship is worthless, and God rejects it.

entries.section: (4) Rejection of the commandments and outward worship

paragraphs.text: God decrees that He will punish His people by the Babylonian captivity, in which all will stumble and fall, both the great, such as the fathers, and the small, such as the sons, because they all fell into evil.

entries.section: (4) Rejection of the commandments and outward worship

paragraphs.text: He describes the discipline as being carried out by the hand of the mighty kingdom of Babylon, which will come from the north-east of the kingdom of Judah, and come from afar, from the farthest known part of the earth at that time, upon His people, and destroy them and take them captive.

entries.section: (4) Rejection of the commandments and outward worship

paragraphs.text: He continues the description of the strength of Babylon with the following:
1- It uses arrows and the bow to strike the men of Judah from afar and kill them, and spears to kill fiercely and violently whoever it meets.
2- Its attack is violent and its voice is strong like the sea whose waves dash with a roar, that is, the strong sound of the sea.
3- It is organized and possesses many horses ridden by trained horsemen who attack in ranks that sweep through the cities of Israel and kill those in them.

entries.section: (4) Rejection of the commandments and outward worship

paragraphs.text: When the people hear and see the attack of Babylon, they fall into despair and cannot defend themselves, that is, their hands become slack and fear takes hold of them, and they suffer like a woman in her labor (the travailing one).

entries.section: (4) Rejection of the commandments and outward worship

paragraphs.text: The people of God will be very afraid, and will hide in their houses, and will not be able to go out into the fields or the roads lest the enemy kill them.

May you hold yourself to account every day, to turn back from your sins and repent of your evil thoughts and intentions, so that you can offer holy worship from the heart, which God accepts and rejoices in, and lifts His wrath from you however much your sins deserve punishment.
Gird thee: put on a girdle, which is what is worn on the waist and hangs down over the thighs.
Sackcloth: coarse garments that signify abasement.

Mourning for an only son: weeping over the death of the only son because of attachment to him, and when they lose him they lose all the offspring that would come from him, and so the parents have no offspring.

Since the Babylonian army attacked Jerusalem and Judea, God calls her in His fatherhood and calls her His daughter, for He is grieved for her, and calls her to put on sackcloth and wallow in the dust and put it on the head; all these customs they did to show their intense grief and abasement. And He calls her to make a great mourning as for the death of an only son, because of the Babylonians' swooping down on her and destroying her.

When an affliction comes upon you, humble yourself before God and weep over your sins, and trust that your tears are precious to Him, for when He sees your repentance He must intervene and deliver you, because His discipline is temporary for your spiritual benefit.

God calls Jeremiah and describes him as a tower among the people, where he is a watchman over them and calls them to repent. He also describes him as a fortress, because if anyone repents he will take refuge in him, and he will teach him the commandments of God and by this he escapes the wrath of God.

He describes the people as disobedient and rebellious and seeking to cause strife between people and to invent problems, and He describes their unresponsiveness as the hardness of brass and iron, that is, they persist in their evil, insisting on corruption with many sins.
The bellows: that which gives air to the fire so that it stays burning strongly in order to melt metals and be rid of their impurities.
The lead: it is used to separate the impurities from metals.

He compares Jeremiah to the bellows of the metalworker, who blows air to kindle the fire, by proclaiming the voice of God and His warnings so that the people repent, but his work did not bear fruit, and his words went in vain as far as his hearers were concerned, as the lead used for refining the metals is consumed while they have not yet been refined. In the end the bellows itself was burned and the metals do not want to be refined, since they rejected the words of Jeremiah and then killed him by stoning. Thus the refiner did not succeed in his refining of the metals, for the impurities remained in them, that is, the wicked still persist in their evil, rejecting the words of Jeremiah.

In the end the divine judgment comes upon His people who persist in evil, and He describes them as reprobate silver. Silver signifies the word of God, that is, the people know the word of God but do not live by it, so God rejected it; and because they rejected God and insisted on that, God also rejected them.
God's punishment of His people because of their sins and the worship of idols

In the first chapters of this book Jeremiah speaks in the midst of the people so that they repent, but now he stands publicly in the most important place, the gate of the house of the LORD, that is, His holy temple in Jerusalem, where those who come to worship God and bow down to Him throng, to rebuke everyone, people and leaders and priests, in the chapters (chs. 7-10), that perhaps they will repent. This of course brought him many problems, since the leaders rose up against him and tried to kill him several times.

God declares Himself with the attribute of power, that is, the LORD of hosts, and commands His people to amend their works, that is, to repent of their evil works, so that He forgives them and allows them to remain in the holy land, that is, the land of Canaan; and the opposite is true: if they do not repent He will drive them out of it, and this is what happened at the hands of the Babylonians.

God promised His people that He would keep His house forever if they lived with Him by faith, as in the days of King Hezekiah when Sennacherib attacked him, or when they built the temple in the days of Solomon (Isa 33:20; 1 Kgs 9:3). This was on condition of their steadfastness in faith, but they did not understand this and thought that the temple would not be demolished and that their city Jerusalem would remain firm however great their evil.

And God fulfilled His word in the permanence of His temple in the New Testament, to which the temple of the Old Testament points as a symbol, and this temple remains firm forever in the Kingdom of Heaven, where Christ reigns with those who believe in Him.
God requires of His people, so that He may keep them in the holy land, the land of promise, that they do the following:
1- Hold fast to justice in dealings.
2- Not oppress the weak, such as the stranger, the orphan and the widow.
3- Not kill the innocent to fulfil their greed and gains.
4- Keep away from the worship of idols.

It was in God's plan from eternity to give His people the Promised Land, and His promise remains for His people who believe in Him, who will receive faith in Christ, and He gives them the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven, which lasts forever.

However great your opportunity for material gain, do not wrong another even if the law does not punish you, for God sees your works and punishes you for them if you do not repent. And know that He has mercy on the one who has mercy on others, so give up material things to gain what is more important, which is your eternal life, even if you give up some of your rights.
God rebukes His people because of their reliance on the words of the false prophets who promised them peace and security in spite of their evils, so they persisted in them.

God also rebukes His people for treating many sins as permissible, such as stealing, murder, adultery, swearing falsely and the worship of idols, and refusing to repent of them, and then drawing near to God and worshiping Him, thinking that this outward worship is enough for their salvation.

By their insistence on evil and their entering to offer worship to God, they make His house a den of robbers, because they steal the rights of others and come forward to worship God, so God does not accept their worship, but they defile the house of God by their entering it, and make it a meeting place for the wicked who insist on their evil. God is long-suffering and sees all this evil, but He will punish them if they do not repent.

Shiloh: a city located north of Bethel, 17 miles north of Jerusalem, in which the Ark of the Covenant of God was placed for about 300 years in the days of Joshua the son of Nun and in the time of the judges, until it went out to war with the sons of Eli the priest against the Philistines, who took it from them. It did not return to Shiloh, which was ruined afterwards, and it had been destroyed in the time of Jeremiah.

The people thought that Jerusalem would not be destroyed because of the presence of the temple of God in it, so He reminds them of the city of Shiloh, in which the Tabernacle of Meeting was and which was destroyed because of the evil of those who dwelt in it, so that they might repent of their sins.

The people rejected the word of God through His prophets, whether the early ones, that is, those who prophesied before the Assyrian captivity or during it, or before the Babylonian captivity, such as Jeremiah, so God warns them because of their disobedience.

God warns them that He will allow the destruction of His temple and Jerusalem His city and all the kingdom of Judah, as He allowed the Assyrian captivity that struck Shiloh, where the place of His Ark of the Covenant was, and indeed all the land of Ephraim, by which all the kingdom of Israel is meant, that is, the northern kingdom whose capital was Samaria, because of their evils.

God speaks to Jeremiah and forbids him to pray for this people who persist in their evils, for the prayers of Jeremiah and his importunity in asking for them will not profit them. Here He affirms the uselessness of a relationship with the Church, or of the prayers of the saints, as long as we insist on evil.

Do not rely on your outward relationship with the Church, or on your position and name in it, if you were a servant in it or gave something to it, if you insist on your sins. God calls you to return to Him, and then all your worship and works become acceptable and good in His eyes, and you benefit from the prayers of the saints and their intercession.

It seems that the feelings of the prophet Jeremiah were affected when God forbade him to pray for the people, so God makes clear to him here the appalling nature of what the people do, and calls him to see what is happening, which is the cooperation of the whole family to offer worship to idols. The sons, full of vitality, gather wood from different places, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead the dough to make cakes for the pagan gods, from whom they choose the queen of heaven. Thus we find the whole family, that is, the whole society, plunged into the worship of idols.

May every family encourage one another to live with God, whether in prayers, or in group readings at home, or in attachment to the Church and its activities, and if possible may they encourage one another in service and in works of mercy, so that it truly becomes a spiritual family.
The people plunged into the worship of idols and by this they fell into two things:
1- Provoking God and defying Him.
2- They were filled with shame by their worship of stones and wood, that is, the worship of idols.

Because of the plunging into the worship of idols, and the refusal to repent and return to God, He had to punish not only the people for their evil, but all the creation that He created for them, so that they take notice when they lose their material comfort and repent.

God Almighty, the LORD of hosts, declares His rejection of the sacrifices that the children of Israel offer to Him, so He does not bless them or sanctify them, but regards them as mere ordinary slaughtered meat, and says to those who offer them, eat them as meat, for I reject them as burnt offerings because of your worship of idols and your persisting in sins.

God makes clear that when He called His people to bring them out of the land of Egypt, He did not intend that they should slaughter mere sacrifices to eat their meat, but He commanded them to slaughter the Passover lamb, which signifies Christ, that they might be saved by it from the destroying angel; He asks for the spiritual meaning and purity of heart, which are signified by the sacrifice and the burnt offering.

God declares His purpose and His requirements of His people, which are that they believe in Him, obey His word and walk with Him, and so receive blessing and kindness from God, and become His own people whom He cares for.
They turned their back: they rejected the word of God.
The people rejected the word of God and did not live by it, but walked according to their hearts, which were full of evil.

They hardened their neck: as the animal stiffens its neck so that the wooden yoke is not put on it to pull the agricultural implement, so the necks of His people became stiff, refusing to submit to God. God sent His prophets long ago, “early,” and sent His word with them, but the people rejected it and remained in their sins. He means the prophets from their going out of Egypt, that is, the prophet Moses, until Jeremiah.

In spite of the people's stubbornness and persistence in sin, God commanded Jeremiah to speak to them the word of God, and so that he would not be distressed He told him that they would reject him, and then Jeremiah proclaims to them that they are the people who reject the word of God and His discipline, so they departed from the truth in their speech and conduct.
Do not neglect the voice of God that you hear, not only in the Church and from your father of confession, but also what you hear from those around you, lest God condemn you because of your error.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Cut off thine hair: hair is the crown of a woman, and in the case of intense grief she cuts it and shears it as the wool of sheep is sheared, and throws it on the ground, that is, she loses her beauty.

Lamentation: sad words by which the soul expresses its hard calamity, in a last attempt by God to save the kingdom of Judah; He addresses her as a woman and asks her to cut off her hair and raise a lamentation over the people of God whom He has rejected in “His wrath,” that is, over herself.
Wrath: intensity of anger.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Their abominations: statues of the pagan gods that God hates.
The people defied God and placed in His holy temple the statues of the pagan gods whom they worship, so in their eyes God became merely one of the gods, equal to the idols in their worship of Him.

How hard is what you do when your heart is occupied, beside the worship of God, with money and various lusts, which even become your first concern that takes up most of your time, and you are troubled when they diminish. By this you make many idols within your heart, and forget God who gave you His whole life on the Cross, and who asks you to love Him with all your heart and to use the world in such a way that it does not rule your heart.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Tophet: its meaning is place of fire, and it is high places beside the valley of Hinnom on which they offered burnt offerings to the pagan gods.

The valley of the son of Hinnom: a valley south of Jerusalem into which the remains of sacrifices are thrown and burned with fire, and therefore the fire is always burning in it, and from it the name Gehenna was taken, that is, eternal torment and continual fire. To burn their sons and their daughters: they used to offer their children as burnt offerings to the pagan god “Molech” so that he would be pleased with them.

The reason for the divine wrath against the people is their worship of idols and their offering the dearest thing they have, their sons and their daughters, as burnt offerings to please the gods, and this is what God did not command, for He is a tender God who asks for the care of children and compassion toward them.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: God declares what will happen when the army of Babylon attacks and kills many of the Jews, so that the valley of Hinnom near Jerusalem is filled with their corpses, and not the corpses of animals. It is a symbol of the eternal torment that they will meet in Gehenna by their refusal to repent.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Because of the multitude of the corpses of the Jews, birds of prey come and eat from them and no one drives them away, and this is an expression of the total ruin, and of the appalling nature of the Babylonian attack as a discipline for the stubborn people.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: After the demolition of the temple and the destruction of Jerusalem and the killing of the Jews in it, and indeed in the cities of Judah around it, grief casts its shadow over the hearts of those who remain, and their joys and feasts cease, whether personal ones, such as rejoicing in new marriages, or public feasts, because the ruin has become total.
Humiliation and ruin for the people's rejection of God (1) The humiliation of the Jews (vv. 1-3)

1- At that time, saith the LORD, they shall bring out the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of his princes, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of their graves: 2- And they shall spread them before the sun, and the moon, and all the host of heaven, whom they have loved, and whom they have served, and after whom they have walked, and whom they have sought, and whom they have worshipped: they shall not be gathered, nor be buried; they shall be for dung upon the face of the earth. 3- And death shall be chosen rather than life by all the residue of them that remain of this evil family, which remain in all the places whither I have driven them, saith the LORD of hosts.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: At that time: the time of Babylon's attack on the kingdom of Judah.

So that Jeremiah may alert his people to repent and turn back from the worship of idols, such as the worship of the sun and the heavens, he declares to them that when the armies of Babylon attack them they will dig up the graves of their fathers and bring out their bones and throw them everywhere before what they call gods, such as the sun and the heavens, which will not profit them at all. God will allow this humiliation because they did not obey Him, and perhaps they will repent, and this will be done to the graves of the great ones of the Jews, the prophets and leaders and kings and priests, as a degradation of the Jews.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Dung: manure, that is, the droppings of cattle.

When the Babylonians bring out the bones of the dead they are before the sun and the moon and the heavens which they worshiped and which did not profit them at all, and their bones become despised, like the manure of animals thrown on the ground.

When God allows you to be despised by others, review yourself, perhaps He is calling you to repent and hold fast to Him, so that He delivers you from their hands and your relationship with Him increases. So do not fear what they say, and do not be distressed by their contempt, for it is worthless, and God will honor you in the heavens above all.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: The remnant of the Jews will wish for death, after many of them have died from the abundance of distress, to be rid of the humiliation in which they have come to be, and this is because of their lack of attachment to God, to whom they ought to have returned, and He would have received them and delivered them.
(2) The refusal of repentance (vv. 4-12)
4- Moreover thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the LORD; Shall they fall, and not arise? shall he turn away, and not return?

5- Why then is this people of Jerusalem slidden back by a perpetual backsliding? they hold fast deceit, they refuse to return. 6- I hearkened and heard, but they spake not aright: no man repented him of his wickedness, saying, What have I done? every one turned to his course, as the horse rusheth into the battle. 7- Yea, the stork in the heaven knoweth her appointed times; and the turtle and the crane and the swallow observe the time of their coming; but my people know not the judgment of the LORD. 8- How do ye say, We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us? Lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain. 9- The wise men are ashamed, they are dismayed and taken: lo, they have rejected the word of the LORD; and what wisdom is in them? 10- Therefore will I give their wives unto others, and their fields to them that shall inherit them: for every one from the least even unto the greatest is given to covetousness, from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. 11- For they have healed the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace. 12- Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush: therefore shall they fall among them that fall: in the time of their visitation they shall be cast down, saith the LORD.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: God rebukes His people with a fact, which is that whoever falls on the way, or in anything wrong, must go back and return to what is right, and this is the logical course of action. Why then do they persist in their sins and remain firm in evil, relying on the cunning and deceptive words of the false prophets?

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: His course: his way.

He compares their persistence in evil to a horse advancing in battle that does not want to turn back from its way, for this is the order of war: striving to the end, even to death; so they too advanced in evil, insisting on it until death, and do not want to return and repent.

Be attentive to the voice of God that calls you to review your thoughts and your words and your behavior, even if you are accustomed to them, that is, many years have passed over them. Seek God with humility, and submit to your father of confession, and do not be angry with the one who punishes you, or neglect his word.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: The stork: a large bird with a beak, and long legs and a long red neck; it is one of the birds of prey, that is, those that swoop on their prey.
The swallow: a small bird with long wings and swift flight, one of the tame birds, and its voice is beautiful.

God directs the attention of His people to the fact that animals such as birds return from their flight at a fixed time to which they are accustomed, but the sons of His people do not want to return from their sins although they are the best of creatures and the wisest of them, so it would be natural for them to return to their sound position, which is life with God.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: He affirms to them their insistence on deceiving themselves with the words of the false scribes, thinking that they are wise because they possess the Holy Bible, and because of the presence of the temple in their city Jerusalem, but all this is not enough if they do not repent.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: He shows the sad end of those who think themselves wise, that is, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, when the army of Babylon attacks and takes them captive, and this is the natural result for whoever refuses to obey the word of God and to repent.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Given: attached and bound strongly.

God shows a basic reason for their not repenting, which is their attachment to money and material things, and the whole people fell into this sin, even their leaders, such as the priests and the false prophets, and the result is their falling under the Babylonian attack and the taking from them of their wives and fields, that is, their being stripped of all the material things and lusts for which they lived; all this that perhaps in the end they will return to God.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Covetousness: corruption.

One of the reasons for their not repenting is their not treating their sins, but holding fast to the evil within them and believing the words of the false prophets that they have peace and God is pleased with them, although their sins have corrupted them, and they need to be healed from them by repentance.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Abomination: unclean lusts and perversions.
They persisted in evil and base lusts shamelessly, and were not ashamed of their cheap deeds, so it was necessary to punish them with captivity.
(3) The violence of the destruction (vv. 13-17)

13- I will surely consume them, saith the LORD: there shall be no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf shall fade; and the things that I have given them shall pass away from them. 14- Why do we sit still? assemble yourselves, and let us enter into the defenced cities, and let us be silent there: for the LORD our God hath put us to silence, and given us water of gall to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD. 15- We looked for peace, but no good came; and for a time of health, and behold trouble! 16- The snorting of his horses was heard from Dan: the whole land trembled at the sound of the neighing of his strong ones; for they are come, and have devoured the land, and all that is in it; the city, and those that dwell therein. 17- For, behold, I will send serpents, cockatrices, among you, which will not be charmed, and they shall bite you, saith the LORD.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: The vine: the grapevine, that is, the tree of the grape.

Because of the multitude of the sins of His people, God decided to drive them out of their land and kill them at the hand of the Babylonians, as the grapes are gathered from the vine and the fruits of the fig from its tree, and His gifts to them are taken from them, and this is because they did not gather around God and worship Him, but worshiped idols and walked in their evil lusts.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Gall: bitter, and it is often the colocynth plant.

The Jews were afraid when they heard of the attack of the armies of Babylon, so they hurried to their fortified cities to take refuge in them, and sat in fear and silence, and they had no strength to fight the enemies and defend themselves, but in despair they fell silent awaiting death, and God left them in despair and silence because they did not seek Him.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: The Jews expected peace and healing to come to them from their hard distress, as their prophets deceived them, but sadly they found war instead of peace, and instead of healing, ruin and calamities and killing, because they relied on the lie of their prophets and refused to obey God through the mouth of Jeremiah.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Snorting or neighing: the sounds of horses.
Dan lies north of Jerusalem, and from there the armies of Babylon attacked with their armed horsemen and the strong sounds of the horses, and destroyed Jerusalem and Judea.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Which will not be charmed: the one who specializes in gathering snakes cannot gather them by using the charm, that is, the works of demons.
Cockatrices: a very poisonous kind of snake.

God makes clear the strength of the Babylonians, which the Jews cannot resist, and compares it to snakes that bite them with their venom, and it is impossible to resist or repel these snakes by any of the ways of the sorcerers who gather snakes.

When you hear the threats of God against the wicked, hasten to repentance and you will save your soul and regain your peace whatever afflictions surround you, and trust in the tenderness of God who seeks your salvation by gentleness or by warning. (4) The prophet's grief (vv. 18-22)

18- When I would comfort myself against sorrow, my heart is faint in me. 19- Behold the voice of the cry of the daughter of my people because of them that dwell in a far country: Is not the LORD in Zion? is not her king in her? Why have they provoked me to anger with their graven images, and with strange vanities?

20- The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved. 21- For the hurt of the daughter of my people am I hurt; I am black; astonishment hath taken hold on me. 22- Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Faint: sick.

When the prophet saw all the ruin that would come upon the kingdom of Judah, he was very grieved and his heart was pained, and he expressed that by declaring his need for someone to lift from him this grief for the destruction of his people.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Their graven images: statues of the pagan gods.

The prophet expresses the sufferings of his people who will be taken captive to far countries and cry out from the humiliation of slavery, and he asks: where is God, the King of the Jews, who protects them? Why did He leave them to captivity and humiliation? .. And God answers him, I left them because they left Me by their worship of idols.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: The farmer waits for the time of harvest, which is the months of April and May, to rejoice in gathering his crops.

And here he expresses the waiting of the people of God for Him to deliver them from the Babylonians; the months of harvest passed and the Babylonian devastation of the kingdom of Judah was still continuing, so the people said to themselves, perhaps He will deliver us in the summer at the gathering of the summer crops in the months of July and August, but sadly God did not deliver them, because they did not repent of their sins, so all this ruin came upon them.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: The prophet returns and expresses the sorrows of his heart as a father of this people, as he sees their humiliation and suffers and grieves within, and even marvels at the total ruin that came upon them and upon the temple of God, although he knows that all this is because of their evils, but he cannot stop his feelings as a human being, and his suffering for them.

entries.section: (5) Rejected His house and His people

paragraphs.text: Balm: a tree more than four meters high that gives a fragrant scent, and if its stem is struck with a sharp tool a sticky liquid like milk comes out of it, which quickly hardens, and it is used as an ointment for the treatment of diseases, and it was costly; it is what is called the balsam plant.
Gilead: a region located east of the river Jordan and extending to the land of the Arabs.

When the prophet sees many wounded among his people and severe humiliation, he cries out asking for medicine and a physician to rescue them, and gives an example of medicines, the balsam plant, famous for the treatment of many diseases, so that it heals the wounds of many and then their wounds are bound up until they heal. By the physician and the medicine he means not only material medicine but rather spiritual medicine, that is, he appeals to God to lead His people to repentance and forgive them and lift His wrath from them.

May you feel for those far from God and for the suffering and pray for them, and seek to bring them back to the Church so that they find rest from their sins and troubles, knowing that your prayer profits them greatly and God rejoices in them. Lying and idol worship are the cause of Jerusalem's destruction

In his grief over his people Jeremiah began to weep for them, and even wished to keep weeping without ceasing, wishing that his head were turned into water and his eyes into a fountain, so that he might weep continually for those of his people who perish because of their evil. He calls Jerusalem “the daughter of my people,” since her natural position is to be the bride of God, but she turned aside into evil, therefore her sons will perish.
A lodging place of wayfaring men: an inn.

Since the prophet could not bear the sight of his people sunk in sin and about to perish, he wished to go far away into the wilderness and find a place to dwell, so as not to see the adultery spread among his people, whether bodily adultery, or spiritual adultery by the worship of idols and betrayal of God.

Your tears for your sins, or for the sins of others, are very precious to God, because they mean your love for God and for others, and your repentance and your rejection of evil. So let your feelings flow during prayer, and confess your sins every day before God, and pray for those who sin around you.
Their bow: the bow used in war to shoot arrows.

He compares the tongues of his people to bows that shoot arrows in war, as an expression of the sharpness of their speech and their evil and their falling into lying, with which they wound the feelings of those around them and trouble them. They felt that lying gives them strength and material gain, so they persisted in it and refused to repent.
Will utterly supplant: the heel is the back of a person's foot, and to supplant means to pursue him and follow his heels in order to make him fall and achieve one's personal gains.
Slander: spreading false words about a certain person among others.

He alerts the people to the lack of sincerity that has spread among them and the abundance of lying, so that a person cannot trust his brother, for all have become deceivers. Also each one follows the heels of the other in selfishness and looks for his own interest even at the expense of others, and stirs up rumors and false accusations against the innocent to achieve his gains.
Deceive: he deceives him, exploiting his unawareness.

It shows their persistence in lying and deceit: one exploits the other's trust in him, deceives him and attacks him, and plans plots in which he toils to accomplish his evils. And instead of toiling to acquire virtues, he toils many times over to acquire evil.

Give up your rights, and drive away evil thoughts, and do not be led by the provocations that meet you, so that you keep your peace and direct your energy to positive work, that is, drawing near to God and loving others, and so achieve benefit for yourself and for those around you.

He rebukes his people, showing their plunging into lying, and says to them that they dwelt “in the midst of deceit,” and since they plunged into evil they thereby refused to know God, for to know sin is to drive God out of the heart, and the opposite is true: to know God drives out sin.

Since God sees their insistence on lying and deceit, He finds no means of rescuing them except to allow their discipline through the Babylonian attack, that perhaps they will repent. And He addresses Jerusalem in fatherhood, calling her the daughter of His people, perhaps to stir her love toward Him. For affliction tests a person and shows him the result of his sin, so he repents and is purified from it.

He compares their lying tongue to an arrow that kills others, because it speaks words of love to the friend and at the same time plots against him to kill him or exploit him, as Judas Iscariot did when he betrayed Christ to death with a kiss.

God makes them witnesses against themselves, and indeed He calls the whole world to witness that His people who insist on lying deserve punishment and vengeance for their evil. He does not take vengeance on His children whom He loves, but He hates their evils and takes vengeance on them by afflictions, showing their hideousness so that His children hate them.

The prophet Jeremiah shows his grief over Jerusalem and the land of Judea around her because of the ruin coming upon them at the hands of the Babylonians, who burned them, so they turned into a deserted land through which no man passes and no cattle graze, and even the birds keep away from it because it has become a ruin. He proclaims this prophecy, not only that his heart may ache, but that perhaps he may move the hearts of his people, so that they fear the destruction coming upon them and return to God.
Dragons: an animal larger than the fox and smaller than the wolf that always howls, characterized by deceit and cunning, and lives in deserted places.
He continues the description of Jerusalem and Judea and says that they will become heaps of stones and dust, and wild animals such as jackals will spread in them, and no man will dwell in them.

God asks, searching for a spiritual man whom He loves, to whom He reveals His wisdom concerning the affliction that He will allow on the kingdom of Judah, so that he understands and declares the wisdom of God to others, that perhaps they will repent. And this wise and spiritual man is the prophet Jeremiah, and a small number of those who lived with God in the midst of the evils of the kingdom of Judah.
God declares the reason for the affliction, which is the rejection by His people of His commandments and His law, and their being led after idols and evil lusts.

You can become wise and understand God's purposes in the events that pass over you if you walk in humility before Him, and always seek His guidance, and live a life of repentance and purity. And when you receive this wisdom you stand firm in faith and call others to enjoy fellowship with God and to be saved from evil.

Baalim: the plural of Baal, a pagan god of the Canaanites called the god of fertility and farms, who spread in their various lands and each city called him by its own name, such as Baal-peor. And since the Jews lived among the Canaanites they also worshiped the Baalim.

God continues the reason for the ruin coming upon them, which is their stubbornness, that is, their insistence on evil and their holding fast to the worship of idols, the most famous of which is the worship of the Baalim that they received from their fathers; that is, the people of God rejected Him through the years and worshiped idols, so they deserved this discipline.
Wormwood: a plant that grows in Palestine, whose juice is bitter and poisonous.

God declares His power and calls Himself the LORD of hosts, and declares His special attachment to His people, saying the God of Israel, that is, that He is the powerful and loving God who will discipline His people; and He borrows the names of hated plants that grow in Palestine whose juice is bitter and poisonous, as an indication of the severity of His discipline.

When the Babylonians attack, they will not only destroy the kingdom of Judah, but will transfer the people and scatter them in the world to abolish their nationality and belonging, after they kill many of them by weakening and frightening them.
Mourning women: women who specialize in stirring the feelings of the grieving at the passing of their loved ones, who cry out with words that move hearts and make everyone weep.
Cunning women: women distinguished in understanding, intellect and discernment of matters.

The prophet calls for weeping over Jerusalem and for the proclaiming of words of grief, that is, a lament over her, using those who specialize in that, who are the mourning women and the cunning women, so as to move the feelings of all to weep over her, that perhaps this will bring them back to God in repentance.
Zion: its meaning is fortress, and its name is applied to the mountain on which Jerusalem was built, so what is meant by Zion is Jerusalem.
God shows the grief of His people when the army of Babylon attacked them, so they fled before them in shame, and began to lament their condition in sorrow.

He calls the women of the Jews to lament Jerusalem and teach their daughters how to grieve over her, because the army of Babylon has attacked their houses, so they leaped from the windows, and killed those in the houses, and likewise the children who play around the houses and the young men who work and move about in the squares, that is, death has attacked everyone.

He expresses the multitude of the slain by saying that their corpses will be cast on the fields like the dung of man or beast, or like a handful of the harvest that the farmer gathers, which falls from him behind him, and being occupied with gathering the harvest he does not care about the little that falls. So there will be many slain and no one will gather their corpses when Babylon attacks.
May you weep over your sins that caused you many pains, so that you do not repeat them, and guard against them afterwards, and ask God's forgiveness, and so you obtain many divine mercies.

God warns His people not to rely on their wisdom, or their strength, or their riches, for all are passing human things, but to rely on God with humility, and He will protect them; for what did their wisdom and strength and riches profit them before the Babylonian attack?..! Of course they profited nothing because of their sins and their distance from God.
He makes clear that glory and boasting are in knowing God and living with Him, so God protects him and fills him with peace and delivers him from all evil and rejoices in him.

Thank God for all His gifts, for they are from Him and not from you, and seek Him before every work, and He will be with you, and your reliance on Him and your enjoyment of fellowship with Him will increase.

God declares that He will soon punish the kingdom of Judah for their evil, and though they are circumcised in the flesh, their hearts are still full of evil; and after that He will punish the pagan Gentiles, uncircumcised in the flesh, for their evil, for the reason for punishment and discipline is always sin. And God is long-suffering toward the wicked, that perhaps they will take warning from the discipline of other wicked people and return to Him.

Egypt: it was the first empire in the world, and after the rise of the Assyrian kingdom in its place it was still strong, and the Jews thought that resorting to it would deliver them from any evil. Judah: the kingdom of Judah, that is, the southern kingdom of the Jews.
Edom: the descendants of Esau who live in the mountains of Seir.
The children of Ammon: the descendants of Lot, who are neighbors of the Jews.
Moab: the descendants of Lot, who are also neighbors of the Jews.

That are in the utmost corners: in ancient times men used to cut their hair on all sides of their heads and leave a circle of hair on top of their heads to please some pagan gods, which means that they are followers of this pagan god.

God declares His wrath against the pagan nations such as Egypt, Edom, the children of Ammon and Moab because of the inclinations of their evil hearts, and likewise against the Jews because of their evil although they are circumcised in the flesh.

The appearance of your life in the Church and your having good outward qualities is not enough for the salvation of your soul. So do not care about people's opinion, but purify your heart by repentance to live with God and enjoy His salvation. Returning to God
The way of the heathen: the worship of idols.

The signs of heaven: the movements of the planets and the sun in a great and marvelous manner, so that you worship them. God warns His people against being led into the worship of idols like the surrounding nations, and against fearing their authority, and among these worships is the worship of the planets and the sky.
The customs of the people: the pagan worships of the nations.
The forest: the desert and the desolate place.
The axe: the hammer.

God alerts them that what the nations worship of idols is nothing but pieces of wood from a tree cut down from the desert, or any place, which the carpenter then turned into a statue using the axe and the tools of carpentry.

He shows the weakness of these statues in that they are adorned with precious metals of silver and gold, and they give them splendor and glory, and so that they do not break easily they fasten them with nails, and strike on them with hammers, that is, mallets, until they become a statue of any person.

The palm tree: the scarecrow, which is two crossed pieces of wood on which a robe is hung that the wind moves, so the birds think it is a person and fly away and keep off the field and do not harm the crop.

A cucumber field: a field planted with cucumbers (gourds). God makes clear the weakness of these statues, and compares them to the scarecrow that farmers place in their fields to drive away the harmful birds that eat their fruits, for this statue is like the scarecrow, merely a sight with no life in it, and these pagan gods are helpless and cannot walk, so those who worship them carry them, and consequently they are worthless, they harm no one and do no good to anyone.
On the other hand the prophet Jeremiah declares that God is above all these pagan gods and there is no room for comparison with Him in might and power.
To thee doth it appertain: glory and fear and reverence are fitting for You.
Jeremiah declares that God is the King of all the peoples of the world, and not the pagan gods, and He deserves fear and respect.
Brutish: they have become ignorant.
The doctrine of vanities: the vain pagan worships with all their customs and rites.
Everyone who worships idols is ignorant and his worship is vain, because he worships a piece of wood made by human hands and leaves God, the true God.
Hammer: hammers are used for beating and shaping metals such as silver and gold.
Tarshish: a city in Spain at the end of the Mediterranean Sea, famous for trade, and considered the end of the known world at that time.
Uphaz: also called Ophir, a place in the south of the Arabian Peninsula near Yemen, famous for the production of gold.
Blue: cloth of a blue color.
Purple: dark red cloth.
Cunning men: the specialized craftsmen.
He declares that the greatness of these statues is due to their being covered with silver and gold and dressed in the garments of the great, of blue and red colors.
Jeremiah declares the great attributes of God, which are:
1- A true God.
2- A living God.
3- A God who reigns forever.
4- A mighty God, whose wrath destroys all the wicked.
If God is great to this degree, then the pagan gods, who did not create the heavens and the earth and did not do anything, since they are mere statues, will pass away, but God will remain.
God is the Creator of the whole world, both the earth and the heavens and all who dwell and live in them.

He declares that God is the Controller of all, who moves the clouds, which are a quantity of evaporated water, and moves them from the end of the earth to its ends, and directs the winds from place to place, for they go out by the command of God, so He makes this clear by saying that they come out of His treasures, that is, by His command and from Him.

The ignorance of every man appeared because of his reliance on his personal knowledge, and indeed everyone who relied on the pagan gods felt embarrassment and shame, because they will not profit him in the time of affliction.
The vanity and weakness of the pagan gods appears in that when God punishes the pagans their gods do not profit them, but are shattered and perish with them.

He declares that God is the God of Jacob, that is, Israel, and He is not like these weak pagan gods but is the Creator and Former of all that exists, and He is King over His people Israel, to whom He gives for their faith in Him the eternal inheritance, and He expresses His kingship by the scepter of the king, and then in the end He declares His power by describing Himself as the LORD of hosts; and by this He calls the people of God to keep away from the worship of vain idols and to hold fast to the worship of the powerful God who lives forever, who gives them the Kingdom of Heaven.

Everything to which people attach themselves, whether money, or position, or relationships ... all of them are passing things, so do not be occupied with them, but let your heart cling to God, who fills you with peace and in the end gives you eternal life with Him.
Thy wares: the belongings of each individual that he carries on his shoulder in a bundle to go into captivity.

God calls to Jerusalem, besieged by the army of Babylon, that each one of her inhabitants gather his own belongings, because they will be taken captive and driven out from Jerusalem to the lands of the kingdom of Babylon.

God declares that He will strike the inhabitants of the land of the kingdom of Judah by the armies of Babylon, which will strike them with stones by slings, and with all weapons such as arrows and spears, that perhaps when they feel this calamity they will return to God and repent of their sins that caused them this affliction.

Jerusalem cries out because she has been ruined by Babylon, so she is crushed and destroyed and struck with blows that have no cure, and she has nothing before her but to bear this ruin, and understand God's purpose and repent.
My cords: the ropes tied to the cloth of the tent and ending in the stake fixed in the ground; the longer these ropes are, the wider the shade under the tent.
My curtains: pieces of cloth that together make the tent.
He compares Jerusalem to a tent, so that when the army of Babylon attacks her this tent is ruined and torn down and its ropes cut, and her sons flee from her and there is no one to defend her.
Dragons: an animal smaller than the wolf and larger than the fox, which devours whoever meets it.

He makes clear the attack of Babylon coming from the north by the cry of the army that destroyed Jerusalem and Judea and made them a ruin without inhabitant, so wild beasts such as jackals dwelt in them.

Pay attention to God's warnings so that you repent of your sins, and keep away from evil, and prepare for eternal life, and guard against the attacks of the devil by the holy life in the Church, so that you live in security and grow in the way of God.
Jeremiah declares on behalf of the people of God his weakness as a man who cannot know the way of eternal life except with the help of God.

He also declares his repentance and his need for punishment as a discipline from God so that he returns to Him, which is the discipline of a father for his son without destroying him, that is, discipline with His mercy. What is meant by judgment is the fatherly love and mercy, while anger means the punishment for the destruction of the wicked.

If God has allowed the Gentiles in the form of Babylon to discipline the people of God that they may repent, He will afterwards punish them with severe wrath to destroy them, because they insist on rejecting God and faith in Him. For God's discipline of His children is so that they repent, while His wrath on the wicked nations is for their destruction.

I thank You, O Lord, because You are tender to me even in Your punishment, to call me to repentance. So remove by discipline every inclination within me toward evil, that I may know You and love You, and advance in Your way to the Kingdom.
The covenant with God
God calls His people in the kingdom of Judah, through Jeremiah, to renew the covenant with God; and whoever refuses this covenant is cursed, that is, deprived of God's blessings.
Iron furnace: a furnace that reaches a very high temperature, above 1500 degrees Fahrenheit, to melt iron.

God reminds His people of the covenant He made with them through Moses, when He brought them out of the land of Egypt and saved them from the harsh humiliation of slavery, whose hardship He likens to an iron furnace, and He commanded them to obey His commandments, so that He would be their God and shepherd them, and they would become His people.

God's promise in His covenant with His people was to give them a land full of good things, which is expressed by saying that it flows with milk and honey, namely the fertile land of Canaan, which God gave to His people after they crossed the wilderness of Sinai. Remarkably, He says “as it is this day” while they were already dwelling in Canaan; so the land full of good things can only mean the heavenly Jerusalem, full of the spiritual blessings that He gives to His children who keep His commandments.

Jeremiah answered on behalf of the people who fear God, who are sadly very few, and said Amen, that is, he declared his agreement with this covenant, to keep God's commandments and so receive His eternal blessings.
God asked Jeremiah to proclaim in Jerusalem and Judea that God calls His people to renew the covenant with Him.
God reminds His people that He had repeatedly called them to obey His commandments early, from the time they were in Egypt until the days of Jeremiah.
God shows that the cause of the afflictions His people are going through is their refusal to obey His commandments, their abandoning His covenant, and their being swept along by their evil desires.

God, in His fatherhood, seeks you so that you may return to Him, and reminds you of your sonship to Him, which opens for you the doors of divine blessings. So remember at the beginning of every day that you were born of God in the sacrament of Baptism, so that you may enjoy fellowship with Him and incline to doing good at all times.

entries.section: (2) The results of breaking the covenant

paragraphs.text: Conspiracy: a plot, a coup and a rebellion against the leader of the people, who is God. God showed Jeremiah that there was a rebellion among the people and that they refused to submit to God, their leader.

entries.section: (2) The results of breaking the covenant

paragraphs.text: God shows the details of this conspiracy as follows:
1- The people's return to the sins of their fathers, which are the various evil desires.
2- The worship of idols.
3- The breaking of their covenant of allegiance, sonship and obedience to God's commandments.

entries.section: (2) The results of breaking the covenant

paragraphs.text: As a result of the people's breaking their covenant with God, they deprive themselves of His care and protection, and so they are exposed to a great affliction, namely the Babylonian invasion and the captivity; and when they call on God, He will not answer them because of their immersion in evil and the worship of idols.

entries.section: (2) The results of breaking the covenant

paragraphs.text: The inhabitants of Jerusalem and Judea will take refuge in the pagan gods to save them from the attack of Babylon, but these will do nothing for them, because they are merely statues.

entries.section: (2) The results of breaking the covenant

paragraphs.text: God declares with sorrow how deeply they were immersed in the worship of idols, for they made a god for every city, indeed for every street of Jerusalem, and they made altars for the pagan gods in these streets; and the weakness and shame of these gods appeared when they asked for their help and the gods could do nothing.

entries.section: (2) The results of breaking the covenant

paragraphs.text: God speaks to His prophet Jeremiah, showing how firmly His people cling to evil, and tells him not to pray for them, for prayer will not profit them because they have not repented.

If you meet with hard afflictions, examine yourself, lest you yourself be the cause of your distance from God or of your immersion in some troublesome sin, so that you may repent and be delivered from your troubles.

Although God's people have rejected His covenant, and no prayer on their behalf can any longer profit them, He loves them as His bride and calls her “my beloved.” God is astonished at their doing evil in His house and at their disobedience to His commandments and laws; their worship became superficial, so they were deprived of God's blessings, which are expressed by the holy flesh that God sanctifies for His house when they offer their sacrifices and eat of their flesh. But now the holy flesh has become ordinary flesh, which they eat with lust, and this made them lose the blessing; their delight has become the doing of evil and not the worship of God.

God cared for His people and shepherded them and gave them peace and tranquility when they kept His commandments and had spiritual fruits, which are the various virtues. Therefore He likened them to a green olive tree, that is, one full of life, with fruit upon it, that is, olives containing oil, which signifies the work of the Holy Spirit. But when they rejected His covenant, He allowed the armies of Babylon to attack them and burn their city Jerusalem; so they attacked it with noise and shouting and broke its branches after they had demolished it.

God allowed affliction and evil to come upon Jerusalem and Judea because they had done many evils. For although God is the planter of this olive tree, He left it to be broken and burned, since their evils came upon them because of their provoking Him, and the result was their ruin through God's abandoning them. Their worship of foreign gods, chiefly the worship of Baal, is the cause of their disaster.

Remember that your natural place is the bosom of God, and you will live in tranquility, your life will be filled with virtues, and you will protect yourself from the wars of the demons, because you are under God's protection.
God made Jeremiah know what would happen to the kingdom of Judah, and He also made him know their plots against him and their attempt to kill him because of his rebuking them.
Domesticated: tame, raised in private houses and pens.

Jeremiah complains to God that he lived in familiarity with his people and in fatherly love, like the lamb that they raise in their houses, yet they treacherously rose against him to slaughter and kill him. He also likens himself to a tree that they try to uproot together with its fruit, that is, they kill him and he becomes one of the dead. All this is because he loves them and rebukes them so that they may return to God by repentance. This is a clear prophecy about Christ, for Jeremiah is a type of Him, because Christ preached to them His Kingdom and called them to repentance, and they rose against Him and crucified Him, but by His death He saved us from our sins.
I have revealed my cause: I have presented my complaint.

He calls upon God, who knows the hearts of men and the evil or good they hide in them, to take vengeance for their evils and discipline them with His punishment, that perhaps they may repent. For he does not ask for vengeance upon them out of anger against them, but for their discipline, that they may repent, because they are his children. He has presented his complaint to God, who is able to do all things; therefore he calls Him the Lord of hosts.
Anathoth: a nearby city lying north of Jerusalem, in which Jeremiah was born and raised.

Everyone rose against Jeremiah because he rebuked them, even the people of his own town Anathoth, who tried to prevent him from prophesying and proclaiming the voice of God, and threatened to kill him if he did this.

God declares that He will punish the kingdom of Judah: the strong young men will die by the sword of the army of Babylon, while the daughters, who represent the weak among the people, will die of hunger as a result of the siege of Jerusalem. All this is because of their refusal to hear the voice of God from the mouth of Jeremiah.

God declares that He will punish the city of Anathoth with a severe punishment, annihilating and destroying it, because it should have been the first to hear the words of their prophet Jeremiah, since he was from it.
If you fall into affliction, present your complaint to God before any human being, for He loves you more than all, and at the same time is able to rescue you from all people.
The temporary success of the wicked and then their destruction

entries.section: (1) The temporary success of the wicked

paragraphs.text: Plead with You: become an adversary to You.

Jeremiah dares to discuss with God the success of the wicked, because he is weary of their cruelty and their abuse toward him. But he begins to speak with humility, saying that God is righteous and holy and too high for him to stand before as an adversary and argue with, for he is a lowly man; yet he asks in order to learn what is God's wisdom in the governance of mankind. For his mind does not understand why the wicked prosper in their material lives and wield authority and abuse the children of God; indeed, through their confidence in their authority and their evil they have become secure and sure of their ability to abuse the righteous. Here he repeats the words of the Psalm (Ps 119:137).

entries.section: (1) The temporary success of the wicked

paragraphs.text: Jeremiah traced the wicked back to God's good works toward them, for it is He who gave them blessings represented by material goods and fruits, but sadly they used them for evil and forsook God. In addition they fell into the sin of hypocrisy, for they spoke of God and offered worship with the mouth, but they rejected God from within, which the verse expresses by “their kidneys,” the plural of kidney.

Some think that when King Josiah, who took care to build the temple, remove the idols and spread the word of God, was killed in his battle with Pharaoh Necho, king of Egypt, the wicked who worship idols rejoiced over him and abused all the righteous, Jeremiah first among them; so from the depth of affliction Jeremiah uttered these words, crying to God to rescue him from their hands.

entries.section: (1) The temporary success of the wicked

paragraphs.text: Jeremiah reminds God that he is one of His own, for God knows Jeremiah's heart, his faith and his life with Him, so that He may rescue him from the wicked and then discipline them so that they may repent. He likens them to sheep that God prepares for slaughter and announces to them that He will destroy them, that perhaps they may fear and repent; so he asks God's help to lift the abuses of the wicked from him and to frighten them with destruction at the hand of Babylon, so that they may return to God. For being set apart for slaughter, or being appointed for killing, does not mean that they are slaughtered or killed, but that they are prepared for killing, so that when they see death coming upon them they may repent and leave their evils.

entries.section: (1) The temporary success of the wicked

paragraphs.text: Jeremiah likens the land to a sorrowful woman weeping over what has happened to her, for her people, that is, the crops sown in her, have withered, food has become scarce and hunger has increased, besides the death of the beasts and the birds. All this is from God's anger against the wicked Jews who dwell in the kingdom of Judah, who worshiped idols and abandoned the worship of God and persisted in their unclean desires, and in pride made light of the divine wrath coming upon them, which was meant to lead them to repent, and said, “God does not see our last end,” that is, He does not know our fate, instead of letting the affliction lead them to repentance so that they might have a good end with God.

Some of the Fathers see that the land that mourns means the angel responsible for the land of Judah, who weeps over their evils and their making light of the divine wrath, because every kingdom has an angel who intercedes for it before God.

Do not be disturbed by the success of the wicked, their authority, their threats, and their contempt for your faithfulness and purity, but persevere in your striving, confident that God is with you and supports you and will gladden your heart in the end, when all the greatness of the wicked passes away and they are cast into eternal torment.

God reproaches Jeremiah for his weakness and his not enduring the abuses of the wicked, and makes clear that He allowed him afflictions in proportion to his spiritual stature, but that there are greater afflictions that He did not allow him. He likens his affliction to a race in running with a group of men; this is what happened with Jeremiah in his not enduring the wicked. But if he entered a race running with horses, like his entering into direct war with the demons, this would be far harder than enduring the abuses of the wicked around him.

He gives another comparison for the abuses that happen to Jeremiah: he is in a land of peace, that is, an easy valley, yet he was not able to walk in it but fell and sprawled on his face; so how will he walk in the Jordan during its flooding? He will not be able to cross it because of its depth and will surely drown. So God assures him that He allowed him trials within his capacity, and that He is with him, supporting him in them, so he should not be disturbed.
They have called a multitude after you: they have said evil words against you and rebuked you to prevent you from prophesying.

God makes clear to Jeremiah that He feels with him and with all that he suffers, for He knows that the people of his city Anathoth, that is, his brothers and relatives, have forsaken him and stood against him and tried to prevent him from proclaiming the word of God. He warns him not to entrust himself to them even if they speak kind words to him, for they are wicked and treacherous, and he must be on guard against them.

Be reassured that God does not allow you a trial beyond your strength; He feels all your suffering, sympathizes with you, supports you and protects you from the plots of the wicked. He is your God who loves you and protects you and brings you out of all afflictions and gives you consolations, and then the glories of the Kingdom.

entries.section: (3) The evils of the Jews and their shepherds

paragraphs.text: Because of the evils of the kingdom of Judah, God was compelled to abandon them and to allow them to be killed and taken captive by Babylon. But His fatherhood made Him grieve over them and call them “my house, my heritage and my beloved.” He wished that they would remain in His worship and enjoy His care, and so receive their eternal inheritance that He had prepared for them.

If only you would remember God's love toward you and His longing to take you into His embrace, and that you are the temple of God and set apart for Him, so that you may refuse sin however dear it is to your heart and however accustomed you are to it or however much people encourage you in it. Do not wound God's feelings, but refuse sin for His sake, lest you deprive yourself of His love and be exposed to eternal destruction.

entries.section: (3) The evils of the Jews and their shepherds

paragraphs.text: With sorrow God likens His people to a lion standing against Him, using the abilities He gave it to defy Him by its evils and its worship of idols. And He made the holy Promised Land a wasteland, and all holiness departed from it, so He called it rugged. And instead of uttering praise to God, it murmured against Him and spoke evil words against Him and provoked Him by its sins. Because of all this evil God hated it, that is, hated its sins, and was compelled to abandon it and to discipline it, that perhaps it might repent and return to Him.

entries.section: (3) The evils of the Jews and their shepherds

paragraphs.text: He continues to show His people's defiance of Him and makes clear their violence, cruelty and persistence in evil, likening them to one of the birds of prey that swoop down on their prey and tear its flesh; so God's people abused Him and defiled His temple and His holy city Jerusalem with idols.
He likens them also to the hyena, for its cruelty and its preying on other animals, just as every man wrongs his companion.
Therefore God allowed the army of Babylon to besiege Jerusalem and swoop down on it and destroy it, like the birds of prey that swoop down on their prey.

And He likens the Jews, the inhabitants of Jerusalem and Judea, to the beasts of the field, which the many wild beasts easily devour, that is, the armies of Babylon, which kill and destroy the kingdom of Judah.

entries.section: (3) The evils of the Jews and their shepherds

paragraphs.text: God grieves because the shepherds of His people, that is, the kings, rulers, priests and false prophets, have led His people astray; so God abandoned them and they were exposed to ruin and destruction at the hand of Babylon, even though they are His people, set apart for life with Him, whom God desires and whom He wished to live with Him.

entries.section: (3) The evils of the Jews and their shepherds

paragraphs.text: They have made it desolate: He continues His speech from the previous verse, that the shepherds made Jerusalem and Judea desolate by turning the people away from God and not teaching the truth, so that it was attacked and its land laid waste. Being desolate it mourns unto Me: the people mourn on God's shoulder, and in another translation “they sob before Me,” after it became desolate; but the weeping of the shepherds and the people over the desolation of the kingdom of Judah was sadly not repentance, and they did not return to God with right faith, but was merely being moved by the calamity that had happened. The whole land is made desolate, because no man lays it to heart: no one put God in his heart and no one repented, so the desolation and the captivity continued for seventy years.

The shepherds did not do their duty and turned the people away from God, so the kingdom of Judah was laid waste; and when it was laid waste, they wept over it, but not with the weeping of repentance and return to God.

entries.section: (3) The evils of the Jews and their shepherds

paragraphs.text: High places: the plural of “height,” that is, a hill or an elevated place.

The army of Babylon attacked the kingdom of Judah and laid waste the valleys and the high places, which are where the Jews had built temples for idols; they demolished and plundered everything precious in them and killed with the sword whomever they met. Thus all the Jews were in fear and terror, because everyone was exposed to killing, plunder and destruction. And he calls “the sword of Babylon” “the sword of the LORD,” since God is the One who allowed Babylon to discipline His people, that they might repent and return to their first faith.

entries.section: (3) The evils of the Jews and their shepherds

paragraphs.text: God withheld the blessing from His children dwelling in Jerusalem and Judea, so that when they sowed their fields they did not yield the required fruits but very poor crops, expressed by thorns, that is, the lack of blessing, just as the earth gave Adam of old thorns and thistles instead of the leafy plants full of fruit that were in Paradise. So their labor in farming or industry or any craft was of no avail, and they were put to shame at not obtaining fruits and produce from their labor. This was because of God's fierce anger against them, which He showed them with the aim of calling them to repentance.

If some of your work is hindered, or you enter into material afflictions or problems that have no solution by any human means, ask yourself: is God pleased with you? And if you are in a relationship with Him, are you growing spiritually, or have you left your first love and the service you used to serve? God loves you and seeks you by every way so that you may return to His embrace.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Touch: assault.
The inheritance which I have caused My people Israel to inherit: the land of Canaan, that is, the Promised Land.

This is a prophecy about the nations that live around the people of God, whether near or far, whom God allowed to assault and lay waste the land of His people, such as Assyria and Babylon. So God prophesies against them by the mouth of Jeremiah that He will lay them waste as He laid waste the kingdom of Israel and will lay waste the kingdom of Judah.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Then God prophesies concerning His people that after they are plucked from their land, taken captive and their cities laid waste, He will have mercy on them and bring them back again from captivity, so that they build their cities and offer the worship of God in His temple in Jerusalem.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: As for the nations that taught God's people the worship of idols, the most famous of which is the worship of Baal and swearing by him, if these believe in God and repent and leave their sins, God will have mercy on them and will again build them up after having laid them waste. This is what happened when the Gentiles believed in Christianity, and they became living stones in the Church, built up in the spiritual building, walking in the way of God and calling upon His name.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: But the pagan nations that persist in their evils, God will lay waste and destroy, and they will not be built again. This is a type of the eternal destruction of the wicked who persist in their sins.

God is merciful and does not desire the destruction of mankind, even of those who defy Him; so be confident that He loves you whatever evils you have done, and return to Him, and He will wash you from your sins and build you up, and you will become great and pure and fit for the Kingdom of Heaven that He has prepared for you.
The fruits of pride and evil desires (1) The linen girdle (vv. 1-11:)

1- Thus saith the LORD unto me, Go and get thee a linen girdle, and put it upon thy loins, and put it not in water. 2- So I got a girdle according to the word of the LORD, and put it on my loins. 3- And the word of the LORD came unto me the second time, saying, 4- Take the girdle that thou hast got, which is upon thy loins, and arise, go to Euphrates, and hide it there in a hole of the rock. 5- So I went, and hid it by Euphrates, as the LORD commanded me. 6- And it came to pass after many days, that the LORD said unto me, Arise, go to Euphrates, and take the girdle from thence, which I commanded thee to hide there.

7- Then I went to Euphrates, and digged, and took the girdle from the place where I had hid it: and, behold, the girdle was marred, it was profitable for nothing. 8- Then the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 9- Thus saith the LORD, After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem. 10- This evil people, which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the imagination of their heart, and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.

11- For as the girdle cleaveth to the loins of a man, so have I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah, saith the LORD; that they might be unto me for a people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory: but they would not hear.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Girdle: the undergarment worn around the waist that covers the thighs.

God wanted to show the pride of His people, which caused them the affliction of captivity, so He gave them this parable. He asked Jeremiah to buy himself a linen girdle, which is a symbol of purity and was the clothing of the priests; that is, God gave His people purity and a life of righteousness, but they rejected them. And He asked him not to wash it in water, since it was new and did not need this washing; this signifies that God clothed them with righteousness and did not leave them in need of anything. In addition, washing in water makes the girdle lose its firmness, so that it becomes slack and does not do its work well in covering the body tightly; that is, God kept them from every weakness.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Hide it: bury it.

God asked Jeremiah to take the new linen girdle that he had bought. This signifies the righteousness that God's people obtained and which clung to them as clothes cling to the body, and his buying it means that he took care to acquire it and God granted it to him. He took this girdle and traveled to the river Euphrates in Iraq, a long distance of about 350 miles from Jerusalem, and buried this girdle in a hole of the rock and covered it with earth.
