This signifies Babylon's humiliation of God's people and their captivity there, because they had spoiled the righteousness of God given to them through their pride and their worship of idols.

The rock signifies their human strength and their reliance on their pride and stubbornness. Jeremiah traveled the first time to the Euphrates and back, 700 miles, and the second time, in the following verses, he also traveled to the Euphrates, about 700 miles again; so he traveled 1,400 miles to show the hardship that God's people would meet in captivity, when they were transported from their cities to the land of Babylon.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: After many days: after a period that may have been several months.

After a period God asked Jeremiah to travel to the Euphrates and take out the linen girdle that he had buried in the hole of the rock. He did as the LORD commanded him, and dug and took out the buried girdle, and found it spoiled, not fit to be worn or used for anything. This signifies the loss of the dignity and righteousness of God's people when they worshiped idols and were proud, so they lost their holiness, their dignity and their nationhood, and Babylon scattered them in the lands of its kingdom, because they had forsaken God.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: God declared His purpose in this parable, that He would mar the pride of His people dwelling in the kingdom of Judah and its capital Jerusalem by the Babylonian captivity.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: And just as the linen girdle was spoiled, so the dignity of God's people will be spoiled, because they worshiped idols and relied on them in pride.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: God rebukes His people with sorrow, showing His great love for them, for He had caused them to cleave to Himself as a people of their own, bringing them out of the land of Egypt, keeping them in the wilderness, bringing them into the Promised Land and dwelling in their midst, as is shown by the parable of the girdle that cleaves to the body; but sadly they rejected God and were spoiled and entered into humiliation at the hand of Babylon.

Pride is the root of all evils. So if you sin, return to God with humility, lowliness and repentance, and do not lean on your abilities and intelligence, but confess your fault before God and apologize to others, and He will forgive you and lift every affliction from you, and you will regain your peace.
(2) The bottle of wine (vv. 12-14:)

12- Therefore thou shalt speak unto them this word; Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Every bottle shall be filled with wine: and they shall say unto thee, Do we not certainly know that every bottle shall be filled with wine? 13- Then shalt thou say unto them, Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, even the kings that sit upon David's throne, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, with drunkenness.
14- And I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together, saith the LORD: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Bottle: a vessel of skin in which wine or liquids are put.

The second parable that God gives His people so that they may repent is that every bottle shall be filled with wine. They were accustomed to filling their bottles with wine and keeping it and drinking from it in their houses, so God chose this parable, familiar in their life; and they answered Jeremiah when he said this to them that he had added little, because we know that every bottle we fill with wine we keep in our houses. Thus they understood only the literal meaning, because they were superficial and proud and had no spiritual understanding, so they did not understand that their lives had been filled, like the bottle, with the desires into which they had plunged, and with which they were drunk, that is, they had lost their minds and discernment, and had become like animals in their lusts, and worshiped statues and forsook God, the true God.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Since they did not understand the meaning of the parable, God explained it to them by the mouth of Jeremiah: that God had left them to their desires and abandoned them because of their pride, the people and their leaders, the kings, prophets and priests, who had lost their discernment like drunkards.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Because of their immersion in desires and their rejection of God, He allows Babylon to dash them, great and small, and God does not have mercy on them because they persist in their sins.

Beware of too many occupations, for they will gradually draw you away from God and then quietly lead you into sin without your noticing, until you are immersed in it because you have left God and lost your protection. Hold to a spiritual rule in your prayers and your readings every day, in addition to your confession and your Communion; by these four you will find your way of salvation in the midst of the world.
(3) Pride leads Jerusalem astray (vv. 15-21:)

15- Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the LORD hath spoken. 16- Give glory to the LORD your God, before he cause darkness, and before your feet stumble upon the dark mountains, and, while ye look for light, he turn it into the shadow of death, and make it gross darkness.

17- But if ye will not hear it, my soul shall weep in secret places for your pride; and mine eye shall weep sore, and run down with tears, because the LORD's flock is carried away captive. 18- Say unto the king and to the queen, Humble yourselves, sit down: for your principalities shall come down, even the crown of your glory. 19- The cities of the south shall be shut up, and none shall open them: Judah shall be carried away captive all of it, it shall be wholly carried away captive. 20- Lift up your eyes, and behold them that come from the north: where is the flock that was given thee, thy beautiful flock?
21- What wilt thou say when he shall punish thee? for thou hast taught them to be captains, and as chief over thee: shall not sorrows take thee, as a woman in travail?

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Jeremiah calls his people to humble themselves and so to listen attentively to the word of God, who calls them to repentance; and if they reject His voice, destruction will come upon them.

When you read the Holy Bible or listen to a sermon, be humble and let the word of God keep you, judge you and guide you, so that you understand God's word and His message to you, and your life is changed, and you rescue yourself from destruction and obtain the mercy of God.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Jeremiah calls them to worship God, glorify His name and thank Him for His kindnesses, so that they do not ascribe glory to themselves or to the pagan gods.

And if they do not glorify God, they will stray further from the way of God, lost in their pride, which he likens to mountains; and because their pride leads them astray, he calls them the dark mountains, that is, their hideous pride, which hides from them the sight of God and the hearing of His voice. While they wait for guidance and rescue from their afflictions, their straying and immersion in base desires and the worship of idols increase, so they advance toward their destruction from a straying that he calls “gross darkness,” and their drawing near to destruction he calls “the shadow of death.” All this is the result of pride; for when they relied on their intelligence and their formal worship, and thought it a light that would guide them, they did not find it, but walked toward the destruction that was accomplished at the hand of Babylon.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Jeremiah warns them that if they do not listen to the voice of God and repent, destruction will befall them at the hand of Babylon, and because of this expected destruction Jeremiah will weep for them; and because no one understands the word of God, he will weep in secret places, because he is certain that the people of God, that is, His flock, will be taken captive to Babylon and many of them will be killed.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Then God asks Jeremiah to address his words to the young king Jehoiachin and to his mother the queen, who was involved in the administration of government, that they humble themselves and repent, because after a little while the king would be taken captive and the crown would be taken from his head, he and his mother, and they would carry him to Babylon; and this was done in 598 B.C.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: When the Babylonians attacked, they besieged Jerusalem and cut it off from the other southern cities of Judah, so that these could not come to its aid.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: God addresses Jerusalem as a woman and says to her: Behold the armies of Babylon coming from the north to attack you and take your people captive, whom He calls the flock of your glory, since you relied on these children of yours; so where are they? The Babylonians have taken possession of your cities and seized your great men and sent them to Babylon.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Then God calls to Jerusalem and says to her: What will you do when the armies of Babylon punish her with destruction, devastation, killing and captivity? And at her surrender, rulers from Babylon will be set over her to humiliate her and all who remain in her, as a woman in travail suffers when the hour of her delivery draws near.
(4) The fruits of Jerusalem's evils (vv. 22-27:)

22- And if thou say in thine heart, Wherefore come these things upon me? For the greatness of thine iniquity are thy skirts discovered, and thy heels made bare. 23- Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil. 24- Therefore will I scatter them as the stubble that passeth away by the wind of the wilderness. 25- This is thy lot, the portion of thy measures from me, saith the LORD; because thou hast forgotten me, and trusted in falsehood. 26- Therefore will I discover thy skirts upon thy face, that thy shame may appear. 27- I have seen thine adulteries, and thy neighings, the lewdness of thy whoredom, and thine abominations on the hills in the fields. Woe unto thee, O Jerusalem! wilt thou not be made clean? when shall it once be?

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Discovered: torn.
Thy skirts: the hems of your garment.
By violence: against your will.
Thy heels: the feet from behind.

Jerusalem asks, after the Babylonians have destroyed her, saying: Why has this destruction come upon me? And God answers her, saying: Because of your evil desires the Babylonians struck you, which is expressed by the lifting of the skirts of the garment, so that Jerusalem's nakedness appears, that is, she becomes desolate; and this devastation was accomplished against your will, because the power of Babylon was great. This also points to Jerusalem's depravity and her adultery after pagan worship, so he uses these expressions, which show that she walked in the way of adultery and so was laid waste at the hand of Babylon, like a woman whose nakedness was exposed in adultery; likewise she was laid waste as a city with everything in her.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: The Ethiopian: the Abyssinian, black in color.
His spots: the black dots and the stripes on the skin of the leopard.

People are accustomed to say that the wicked man will not change his evil once he is used to it, and cannot leave evil, like the black African who cannot change his skin and make it another color, and likewise the leopard cannot change its striped skin full of black dots. But God opens the door of His mercies and calls His people to leave their evils, and God will lift from them all these afflictions of which He spoke, that is, the captivity and what follows it.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: But if the people of God persist in their evil, God will scatter them as the wind scatters the stubble in the empty desert; so He will scatter them in the kingdom of Babylon and take them far from their land.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Of thy measures: from “measure,” a vessel used to gauge volumes, such as the liter.

God says that the portion of Jerusalem and Judea is captivity and scattering, and God allows Babylon to do this as a punishment for His people for a certain period until they repent, and then He brings them back from captivity; and the cause of these evils is Jerusalem's trust in the false pagan gods.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: God repeats that He will allow the devastation of Jerusalem, which He likens to the uncovering of a woman's nakedness by lifting the skirt of her garment, so that her face is covered and her nakedness appears, that is, Jerusalem loses all understanding and sight and becomes desolate.

entries.section: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

paragraphs.text: Thine adulteries: the various kinds of adultery in which you walked.
Thy neighings: the sound of the horse.
The hills: the mounds.
Thine abominations: the statues of the pagan gods, which God hates.

God shows the cause of Jerusalem's devastation, namely her immersion in adultery after foreign gods and her running like the animal, which He represents by the neighing, after the desires of adultery, whether physical adultery or attachment to the worship of idols; and adultery was committed on the hills and in the fields, where they offered this adultery as worship of idols and as immersion in their desires. And God marvels at Jerusalem's persistence in adultery and her distance from Him, and calls to her in sorrow: How long will you refuse purity and the pure life with God?

If you fall into evil, return quickly to God in repentance and do not reject His voice that calls you, lest you enter into many afflictions and He forsake you and you hasten to your own destruction. He loves you, so do not harden your heart or reject His love.
The drought

The LORD spoke to Jeremiah about a drought that would come upon the kingdom of Judah, that it might lead them to repentance; this was the drought that occurred in the days of King Jehoiakim, before the armies of Babylon attacked and took them captive.
Judah mourneth: He portrays the kingdom of Judah as a woman weeping because of the lack of water, thirst, the drying up of the crops and the death of the beasts.

The gates thereof languish: the cities of Judah suffered thirst and hunger and their sons went out from them, so the gates no longer had value in protecting or fortifying those in the city, as a flower withers and becomes useless. They are black unto the ground: the affliction on the people of Judah increased, so they were in great sorrow and bowed their heads to the ground, and their strength weakened, so they fell to the ground from thirst and hunger.
The cry of Jerusalem is gone up: from the severity of thirst and hunger the people cried out everywhere.
Their little ones: their servants, those who work for them.
Pits: pools and gatherings of water.

The rich and the great sent those who work for them, or their servants, with vessels to fill them with water from any place, but they found all the gatherings of water dried up, so they returned in shame and disgrace to these great men, and from the intensity of shame they covered their heads and bowed them to the ground.

Not only did the great suffer from thirst, but also the poor, who are the farmers working the land, because it was cracked from dryness and the lack of rain, so they were ashamed, and therefore covered their heads.
The hind: the female deer, a kind of swift-running gazelle.
Grass: the grasses and herbs.

The hind left her natural place, which is the forests, because the earth dried up and the plants died; and when she found her young she found no water for them to drink or food of grass for them to eat, so she left them to die and went to look for water and food.
The wild asses: the wild donkey.
Dragons: predatory animals, larger than the fox and smaller than the wolf.

The wild donkey found no food, so it went up on the hills and the plateaus to search for food, and from running it grew tired and breathed with difficulty and needed to snuff up the wind lest it die of weakness, hunger and thirst, like the jackals that run and pant; and from the leanness of the wild asses their sight failed.

Your distance from the source of the waters of grace, that is, the Holy Spirit working in the Church, weakens your spirit and exposes you to many troubles, so that you almost die and become an easy prey for Satan, falling into many sins. So submit to Him, hold to His commandments and abide in His Church, and you will regain your strength.

The prophet Jeremiah bears the sins of his people and offers this prayer, confessing on their behalf and on behalf of his own weakness that they have sinned against God and their iniquities are many, which testify that they are wicked and deserve punishment such as this drought; but their hope is in the love of God, who has mercy on them, because His name is called upon them, for they are His people, so with the boldness of a son he asks God's mercy.

God is your heavenly Father; He rejoices in your taking refuge in Him, so ask Him earnestly to have mercy on you, support you, rescue you from every affliction and give you repentance. Trust in your sonship to Him, so that you speak to Him with the boldness of sons; and if He does not answer quickly, know that He is concerned with your prayer and will rescue you in the end.

He pleads with God and says to Him: Why have You left us in the drought and humiliation and become like a stranger to us, like a traveler who lodges in the desert? He asks Him to enter their cities and rescue them, because they are His people and He is their only hope in their afflictions.

He continues to ask God to rescue them and says: Why do You stand silent and not stretch out Your hand to have mercy on us, as if You were bewildered and did not know how to rescue us, though You are mighty and able to do all things? You are in our midst and are our God, so do not leave us in our affliction but rescue us.

God was grieved at His people's lack of steadfastness in living with Him and worshiping in Jerusalem, for they moved about in many places on the hills and in the fields to worship the idols that they had set up there... Therefore He calls them “this people” and not “My people,” and even threatens them that He sees their sins and will punish them for them.

In the face of the persistence of God's people in their sins, the prophet's prayers or any intercession will not profit them; therefore God says to him with sorrow: Do not pray for them, because they have not yet repented, and I will not lift from them the punishment that I have allowed, that perhaps they may repent.

God also decides, as a result of His people's persistence in the worship of idols and in evil worship, that He rejects their prayers as well as their sacrifices and offerings to Him, because they are without repentance, and He declares that He will punish them with kinds of punishment, which are:
1- The sword, that is, killing, which was accomplished when the armies of Babylon attacked.
2- Famine, which was accomplished in the days of King Jehoiakim, as mentioned in this chapter.
3- Pestilence, by the spread of various diseases among them.

Do not justify your sins, because this makes you persist in them and lose God's forgiveness; rather various afflictions come upon you, which God allows out of His love for you, since by them He calls you to repentance. For if you forget God, God allows you material afflictions because you have become attached to material things, and when you lose your hope in them you return in repentance and feel the importance of spiritual things, so you hold to them and find your way toward eternity.

Jeremiah makes an excuse for his people before God, that the cause of their persistence in evil is the deception of the false prophets, who promised them peace and material comfort and did not direct them to repentance.

God declares that He did not send the false prophets and that all they claim of visions and divination is a lie and vain, worthless talk, so that the people may know the truth about the false prophets through the mouth of Jeremiah and return in repentance to God.

God declares His punishment of these false prophets, that He will allow them to be killed and the rest to suffer from hunger, so that their evil comes upon their own heads; for they prophesied that neither sword nor famine would come, so sword and famine will come first upon them.
Then, after punishing the prophets, God will also punish the people who followed them and rejected God and did not repent, and He will punish them also with the sword and famine.

Do not be careless in your speech, lest you fall into the sin of lying and deceive others, for God is looking at you and is just, and He will punish you because you fell into lying and caused another to stumble; so hasten to repentance and you will obtain His mercies.

God forbade the prophet to pray for the people because they refuse to repent, but His fatherhood makes Him grieve over them, so He calls the prophet to weep continually over them and likens the kingdom of Judah to a virgin, that is, a weak girl, whom the wicked attacked and shattered, and He declares clearly that the blow of Babylon that will fall upon her is a bitter blow, that is, very hard; perhaps the people will hear the words of Jeremiah and cease from their sins.

As a result of Babylon's attack many will be killed and thrown out in the fields, and those who hid in the cities will sicken from hunger, because Babylon besieges their cities and keeps food and drink from them. As for the leaders of the people, the priests and the false prophets, their inability to rescue the people will be revealed, and they will go about the land in bewilderment and helplessness; indeed the Babylonians will carry them to another land, where they will go about in shame and the humiliation of slavery.

The prophet pleads, interceding for his people, and speaks to God to rescue them from this blow, and with the boldness of sonship he rebukes them in love, saying: Why have You rejected Your kingdom Judah and Your city Zion, which is the old name of Jerusalem? Your people still beseech You, asking for healing from this blow and for peace to return to them after this decision. The lie of the prophets has been revealed, who claimed that nothing would befall Jerusalem and Judah since the temple of God was in them, and that the kingdom of Israel was taken captive by Assyria because it was far from Jerusalem; thus they deceived the people and did not lead them to repentance.
Jeremiah confesses on behalf of his people that they have sinned against God and continued in the evils their fathers did.

If you are a father or a mother or a servant, pray for those you shepherd, and prostrate yourself and plead with God for them, offering the tears of repentance for them, because the weakness of your care caused them these sins.
Jeremiah pleads with God for his people, not for their righteousness but for His goodness, and reminds Him of three things to move His heart toward them, which are:

1- God's name, which means His mercy and perfection; for because they are His people who believed in Him, He forgives them and lifts the affliction from them; and this shows the prophet's fatherhood toward his people.

2- The throne of God's glory, which is His temple in which He dwelt and which was filled with the prayers of many godly people through the ages; so although the people are unworthy, God has compassion on them because they repent.
3- God's covenant, which He made with the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; so for the sake of God's mercies and goodness He lifts the afflictions from them.
Showers: heavy rain.
The vanities of the Gentiles: the pagan gods.

The prophet declares his faith that God alone is able to lift the drought by sending down rain, and so rescue His people from hunger and death, while the pagan gods are statues, unable to do anything.
God disciplines His people and supports His prophet
1- A necessary discipline (vv. 1-9)

1- Then said the LORD unto me, Though Moses and Samuel stood before me, yet my mind could not be toward this people: cast them out of my sight, and let them go forth. 2- And it shall come to pass, if they say unto thee, Whither shall we go forth? then thou shalt tell them, Thus saith the LORD; Such as are for death, to death; and such as are for the sword, to the sword; and such as are for the famine, to the famine; and such as are for the captivity, to the captivity. 3- And I will appoint over them four kinds, saith the LORD: the sword to slay, and the dogs to tear, and the fowls of the heaven, and the beasts of the earth, to devour and destroy. 4- And I will cause them to be removed into all kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah king of Judah, for that which he did in Jerusalem. 5- For who shall have pity upon thee, O Jerusalem? or who shall bemoan thee? or who shall go aside to ask how thou doest? 6- Thou hast forsaken me, saith the LORD, thou art gone backward: therefore will I stretch out my hand against thee, and destroy thee; I am weary with repenting. 7- And I will fan them with a fan in the gates of the land; I will bereave them of children, I will destroy my people, since they return not from their ways. 8- Their widows are increased to me above the sand of the seas: I have brought upon them against the mother of the young men a spoiler at noonday: I have caused him to fall upon it suddenly, and terrors upon the city. 9- She that hath borne seven languisheth: she hath given up the ghost; her sun is gone down while it was yet day: she hath been ashamed and confounded: and the residue of them will I deliver to the sword before their enemies, saith the LORD.

As a result of the people's persistence in their sins, God forbids Jeremiah to pray for them; and lest he think it is because of his own weakness or sins, He says to him that not even the great prophets among God's people, such as Moses, who interceded for his people lest God destroy them (Ex 32:11-14), and such as Samuel (1 Sam 7:5-11), could help. This is an encouragement to Jeremiah, of whom the Holy Bible records that he is a constant intercessor for the children of God (2 Macc 15). And God decides that He must cast His people away and drive them out of their cities as a discipline for their sins, that perhaps they may repent.

Beware of losing the intercession of the saints for you through your persistence in sin and your justifying it, so that your guardian angel grieves over you. Whatever your faults, do not despair or grieve, but offer repentance before your father of confession, and God will receive you.
God says to Jeremiah: If they ask you, “Where shall we go when we go out from our cities?” you will declare to them God's decree, which appears in:
1- Death by the sword and by every means.
2- Sickness because of hunger, which may lead to death.
3- Captivity as slaves in the kingdom of Babylon.
God affirms His severe punishment of them because of their persistence in sin, and this punishment appears in:
1- Death by the sword, which means their destruction because of their lack of repentance.
2- The dogs dragging their corpses after their death, a symbol of their humiliation because of their sins.
3- The birds of prey eating their corpses, a symbol of the demons who attack them with evil thoughts and pagan worship.
4- The beasts eating their corpses, a symbol of the evil desires that destroy their lives.

In addition to the previous punishments, God strikes them with anxiety when Babylon takes them captive and carries them to scattered lands in its kingdom. All this is because of their persistence in the evils in which King Manasseh excelled, who was the most wicked of the kings of the kingdom of Judah and reigned for a long time, and introduced the worship of idols into his kingdom, and depravity spread in his days; so the Jews continued in these sins in the days of Jeremiah.

Jerusalem will be in a state of great misery after Babylon destroys her, and she will find none among her neighbors to have pity on her and help her, nor among the cities of Judah, because they will have been destroyed like her; and God will not rescue her because she rebelled against Him and disobeyed His word.

Because Jerusalem and the kingdom of Judah forsook God and life with Him and replaced Him with the worship of idols, God allows this punishment to come upon her, and God declares His weariness with her false repentance, for she is not sincere in her worship and pretends repentance and regret, while persisting in evil.
Fan: a wooden stick with five fingers used to separate the grain from the chaff, so that the chaff flies away with the wind, far from the grain.
The gates of the land: the whole world.
I will bereave: I will kill the sons of My people.

God threatens His people that He will scatter them in the cities of the world by means of Babylon, which reigns over the world and carries them to various lands subject to it; and He likens this to the farmer who winnows the chaff to remove it and separate it from the grains of wheat or barley. He adds also that He will kill the sons of the kingdom of Judah, so that she becomes like the bereaved mother, that is, one who has lost her children.

Terrors: the plural of “terror,” something very frightening. God declares that He will kill many of the men of Judah, so that the number of widows increases to the point that it becomes difficult to count them, as it is impossible to count the sand of the seas; and death will fall suddenly upon the mother who has young sons and kill her sons, causing her great terror and fear. This is what happened at the hand of Babylon, which killed the young men and left their mothers without sons.

He continues His speech about the mothers of the kingdom of Judah who lost their young sons in the war, and likens her to a woman who in her weakness has become like a languishing woman because she lost all her sons, even if they were many and reached seven sons; that is, the Jewish nation lost all her men and surrendered to sorrow and fell into an affliction expressed by darkness, though she is not old, but she lost her vitality as the day loses its light and the night comes with its darkness. And she was in shame, disgrace, humiliation and weakness because of the death of the men who were her support. So she is a type of the soul that grew careless and persisted in sin and so became helpless and unable to face life. All this God says through Jeremiah to warn His people, that they may return from their depravity, desires and pagan worship, and repent, and God will receive them.

Jeremiah began to prophesy when he was young, in the midst of a wicked generation, and he rebuked the people to repent, and likewise their leaders, whether priests or prophets or rulers; and only a very small number accepted his word and repented, among them his disciple the prophet Baruch, who recorded the prophecies of his teacher. As for the rest of the people, they felt distress at Jeremiah's words, indeed they considered him an agent of Babylon when he called them to submit to the Babylonian captivity and not to take refuge in Egypt; so they stood as adversaries to him and resisted him and contended with him, and even tried many times to kill him. Yet there were no material dealings between him and them: he had not lent to them, nor borrowed anything from them, for these material dealings are what cause disputes among men; he demanded no debt and no one demanded debts from him, but everyone cursed him because he rebuked them and spoke to them about the future, which was an injustice to them and not good news like the false prophets; and his contention was with all the inhabitants of the land of the kingdom of Judah, that is, all his people.

This verse shows Jeremiah's distress at the people's resistance to his prophecies, so that he calls to his mother according to the flesh. He is in pain and the closest person to him is his mother, to whom he declares the extent of his inner pain because of his service to them.
Do not give up proclaiming the truth as long as God has guided you to it, even if people reject your word, and bear their abuses, because they resist you in ignorance, and pray for them.

God answers Jeremiah, who is suffering from his people's abuses toward him, and promises him that He will free him from the chains of the prison into which he was thrown and from the chains of the inner pains that he suffers because of his people's persecution of him.

Then He reassures him, because he said to himself: If my own people persecute me like this, what will the Babylonian enemies do to me? And God answers him that He will make the enemies treat him well, indeed that they will entreat him to do what he wishes. This is what actually happened, for the Babylonians honored him and left him free to stay in Jerusalem or go to Babylon. And what is meant by the time of evil and affliction is the time of Babylon's attack on the kingdom of Judah.

The LORD speaks to His people by the mouth of Jeremiah and says to him: If you think that you are strong like iron, can you break the iron and the brass that come from the north, that is, the kingdom of Babylon? Of course not; rather Babylon will defeat you and destroy you.

Thy borders: your boundaries. God continues His speech to His people, who will be defeated before Babylon, and says to them that Babylon will plunder all your wealth and everything in your treasures of gold or silver or precious possessions, and will occupy your land to all your borders, because you have sinned greatly against God. So the enemy takes all your possessions without price, not in exchange for anything but because of your sins.

And after Babylon plunders all the possessions of the kingdom of Judah, it will seize the rich, the great men and the young men, and send them as slaves to Babylon and all the cities of its kingdom, because on account of their sins the fire of God's anger was kindled against it.

Be humble and rely on God, and do not rely on your own strength in resisting whoever wrongs you; all your wealth, relationships and position will not profit you if you do not keep God's commandments. So return to Him in repentance and trust in Him, and He will keep you from all evil.
When the afflictions, insults and threats from the wicked against Jeremiah increased, he pleaded with God, saying:

1- You alone, O God, know the secrets of my heart, and that I love You and love my people and want their salvation. So if the wicked think me a traitor in my own country or harsh toward them, You know that I do all this for their good.
2- He asks God not to forget him and leave him alone in the midst of the persecutors, but to care for him and look after him with His mercies and deliver him from their hands.

3- Jeremiah was weary of the persecution of the false prophets against him, so that he asked God to take vengeance on them, not out of spite and hatred for them but to discipline them, so that they stop their false teachings and repent and no longer wrong him.

4- If Jeremiah declared his distress to his mother over the troubles he was going through, in (v. 10), this does not mean that he wants to die, but he wants to complete his mission and prophesy as God commands him to draw his people to repentance; so he asks God to be longsuffering toward him and not let him die because he declared his pains and his distress at the persecutions, but to support him and give him an opportunity to complete his service.
5- Jeremiah reminded God that he had borne many insults for His sake, so that God would make an excuse for him in his distress at the multitude of pains, and support and strengthen him.

In the midst of all these pains God comforted Jeremiah by letting him taste the sweetness of God's word, and the prophet declares this by saying that God's word is very delightful, so that he hid it in his heart and meditated on it, and it became a great source of joy to him in the midst of pains; and he expresses the depth of his meditation by saying that he ate God's word. He adds that this grace was given to him, namely delighting in God's word, because God's name is called upon him, that is, God gave him the grace of prophecy and brought him into the depths of His word, which is the greatest wealth in the world, while the wealth of his people who persist in evil becomes worthless and is plundered by Babylon; but as for God's word, no one can take it away from Jeremiah, because it is the word of the LORD God of hosts, that is, the mighty God, able to establish His word in His children and protect them by it.
Do not be content with reading the Holy Bible every day, but take care to meditate on its meanings, and choose a verse to memorize and make it an exercise that you apply in your life.

Jeremiah lived in godliness and rejected the councils of the mockers and their vain talk, and sat alone meditating on the word of God and grieving over his people who were far away and over their evil future, that is, their captivity; and his heart was filled with distress, sorrow and anger because of their persistence in evil, and he prayed to deliver them from it.

Jeremiah asks in his distress from the pains and rebukes God, who leaves him with a wounded heart and inner pains because of his people's lack of repentance, in addition to the constant insults and persecutions against him, and he says to Him: Your leaving me is as if You were a false god, who promises His children to rescue them from affliction yet leaves me to pains. Then he rebukes God, likening Him to a spring of water that is not lasting, so that a man comes to it and finds no water, that is, no comfort. Here Jeremiah rebukes God, asking for His quick intervention to rescue him from those who persecute him.

God makes an excuse for Jeremiah in his suffering and his not enduring the persecutions, but He calls him to return to his steadfast faith in Him; then God will restore to him his peace and tranquility, for He appreciates his human weakness but promises him peace and joy if he returns to his reliance on Him. What is meant by Jeremiah's standing before God is the standing of prayer and the feeling of God's constant presence with him, so that his heart is reassured, and then he can speak with courage and declare his prophecies however much the wicked persecute him. And bringing forth the precious from the vile, that is, the good, fat meat from the bones or membranes that are not eaten, means bringing back to God the precious souls that were despised because of their evil. So God encourages the prophet to be strong and complete his service of seeking the repentance of the souls of his people; by this his mouth will be as God's mouth, that is, he declares the divine truth and shows the fatherhood of God, who desires the salvation of all. And by this the people will return to the pure life that Jeremiah lives in faith and leave the worship of idols, and Jeremiah will not return to rebuke them again for their evils.

It may be that what is meant by Jeremiah's not returning to them is that he will not rebuke them again, because the captivity will fall upon them and they will return to Jeremiah asking him to rescue them.

God reassures Jeremiah that although his people persecute him, He will support him and make him strong like the brazen walls that surround cities, which no one can break through; they will continue their persecutions but will not be able to stop his prophecies or weaken him.

Thus the power of God is manifested: although the wicked who persecute Jeremiah are strong, and he describes them as terrible, that is, very strong, God rescues him from their hands, and God's power, which is above all, is revealed.

Return to God in repentance and hold to your faith, and you will receive divine power that supports you, so that no one can overcome you and you are able to continue in the life of purity and the service of God.
Jeremiah's life as an example for the people

God commanded Jeremiah not to marry and therefore not to beget sons and daughters, because the captivity had drawn near and many would be killed and the rest taken as captives, so that Jeremiah would not be exposed to anxiety because his wife and children were killed or taken as slaves far from him, and so that he might be an example to the people and a declaration of the nearness of the captivity when they ask him the reason for his not marrying, that they may believe the truth of what he says and repent of their evils that cause this captivity.
Dung: the waste of man and beast. Lamented: the sad words of lament that are said in the mourning for the dead.

He declares the reason for Jeremiah's not marrying, which is a prophecy that the mothers, daughters and sons of God's people will die by the sword of Babylon or sicken from hunger, and more than this, that no mourning or lament will be made for them and that no one will bury their corpses, but they will be thrown on the face of the ground as dung or eaten by the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth, as a declaration of the humiliation that will befall them at the hand of the Babylonians.

God forbade Jeremiah to attend funerals or the mourning made when a person dies, so that if they ask him he may declare to them what will happen at the captivity, where no mourning will be made at anyone's death, but the corpses will be thrown on the ground and the rest will flee. All this is because God will withhold His peace, kindness and care from His people, that perhaps they may repent.
Cut themselves: wound themselves at the death of their loved ones to please the pagan gods.

Baldness: the nearest of kin to the dead used to shave the hair of his head and beard to please the pagan gods. He affirms that when Babylon attacks, great and small will be killed and the rest will flee, and there will be no opportunity to perform the rites of mourning such as lament, cutting the bodies and shaving the hair to please the pagan gods whom they worshiped, and because the bodies will not be buried at all but will remain thrown on the ground.

In ancient times the comforters did as some do now: they bring food and drink to the house of the dead to share with his family in the funeral meal, but this will not be, for no funerals will be held and the corpses will not even be buried when Babylon attacks. In sum, when Jeremiah does not attend the mournings, he declares to the people that the reason is God's warning to them of the captivity coming upon them, that they may repent.
Likewise God forbade Jeremiah to attend feasts of joy or to share in the food and drink offered in them.

The reason for not attending feasts of joy is that God will bring them to an end when the captivity comes, so that all will be in sorrow and will not hold the feasts of joy that are held after the completion of a marriage or on other occasions.

Look at the lives of the saints to learn from them how to live with God and prepare for your eternity, and then you will not be wearied by the wars of the devil, since you will be strong in God like these saints.

entries.section: (2) Sin is the cause of the captivity

paragraphs.text: The LORD declares to Jeremiah that when he prophesies to them of the captivity coming upon them as a discipline, they will be astonished, because they do not commit sins that deserve this, and they will ask, “What is our sin?” This shows the spiritual blindness that came upon the people because of their immersion in sin and the breaking of their relationship with God, so that they fell into great ignorance and lack of discernment.

entries.section: (2) Sin is the cause of the captivity

paragraphs.text: The LORD asked Jeremiah to answer them that the causes are:
1- The worship of idols and the evils that their fathers did and their forsaking God, so the sons were influenced and learned these sins from their fathers.
2- Their continuing in the sins of their fathers, indeed their increasing in them.
3- Their rejecting the voice of God through the mouth of Jeremiah and their stubbornness against him.

4- When the Babylonians drive them out of their land and carry them to the lands of their kingdom, they will continue in the worship of idols to which they were accustomed, not only by day for fear of the enemies but also by night, because they loved this worship, so they offer it from their hearts out of conviction; and the grace of God will depart from them, and they will suffer material and spiritual wrong because of their persistence in sin.

If you see faults in your parents or in any person, do not judge him, but try to avoid these sins and acquire the opposite virtues, so that you do a positive work and save your soul by the power of Christ.

entries.section: (3) Sin is the cause of the captivity

paragraphs.text: Fishers: catchers of fish.
Hunters: catchers of animals.
Hill: a mound.

God declares that He will discipline His people by sending the Babylonians against them as fishers and hunters, who will catch them and kill them even if they hide in the mountains and hills or the clefts of the rocks; that is, they must perish because of their sins.

entries.section: (3) Sin is the cause of the captivity

paragraphs.text: God is longsuffering, but He sees all the sins of His people, even if they commit them in secret, and in the end He must punish them for them. But even in disciplining them He asks that they repent, so He warns them of His discipline that they may repent, for He is a tender Father who does not desire the destruction of His people.

entries.section: (3) Sin is the cause of the captivity

paragraphs.text: The carcases of their detestable things: the animals slaughtered to the pagan gods.

As a result of God's people's immersion in the worship of idols and their rejection of God, He will punish them with a severe, double punishment fitting their great evil, their provoking God and their defiling the Promised Land with the worship of idols.

entries.section: (3) Sin is the cause of the captivity

paragraphs.text: My strength: my glory and my pride.

The prophet speaks to God in the midst of the afflictions that he meets from his people who are far from God, and trusts in the LORD, his fortress and refuge in afflictions, indeed his glory and his pride. And he prophesies about the Gentiles' faith in Christ, who will declare that their worship of idols is a lie and that the true God is Christ.

entries.section: (3) Sin is the cause of the captivity

paragraphs.text: Then the prophet declares that God will make the Gentiles know His name and His might, so that they believe in Him and leave the pagan gods, and know that He is Jehovah, that is, He is God and there is no other.
Do not be troubled by the resistance of the wicked, for they are weak and will submit to your Christ in the end and will feel His power that is in you; so abide in your faith and pray for them.
Reliance on God, our Savior from sin

He declares that the sin of the tribe of Judah, meaning the whole southern kingdom, is engraved on their hearts; it is written with a pen of iron, that is, a strong one able to engrave in stones, and likewise with the point of a diamond, a strong mineral able to engrave in metals also. In sum, sin is fixed in them and in their heart, that is, in their feelings and inner intentions, and is not merely a slipping into a superficial sin.
Their sin also appears on their altars, that is, the pagan worship and the sacrifices offered on the altars of the idols.
Whilst their children remember: customary speech; as a man remembers his sons, so their talk of the worship of idols had become, which they had grown accustomed to.
Their groves: the plural of “pole,” a tall piece of wood planted in the ground at which worship is offered to the goddess of fertility, one of the pagan goddesses.

Hills: mounds. The tribe of Judah was accustomed to worship idols by setting up altars or poles for them; likewise they offered the worship of idols under the green trees and offered this worship also upon the hills. In sum, this verse declares the spread of pagan worship among God's people everywhere.

Thy borders: your boundaries. God warns His people of destruction and plunder when their enemies attack them and take away their wealth, seizing it from their fortified cities however strong they are, like a towering mountain, because they worshiped idols on these mountains and everywhere.

Thus God's people give up their land and their heritage, so they leave them, that is, disown them, and go into captivity. The real cause of the captivity is not the cruelty of the enemies but the sin of Judah; therefore God allowed the enemies to attack him. And when the captivity took place, God's people went to become slaves serving the Babylonians, and this was God's anger because of the sin of Judah, which kindled God's anger against them, an anger that continues forever if they do not repent of their sins; for God's anger continues against sinners who have not repented and is completed on the Day of Judgment, when they go to eternal torment.

Sin is what separates you from God and deprives you of His blessings and brings every wrath upon you. So do not be deceived by its pleasure, for it passes away and leaves in you a great bitterness; and if you fall, hasten to repentance to rescue yourself, for our God is compassionate and merciful.
(2) Reliance on God (vv. 5-8:)

5- Thus saith the LORD; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the LORD. 6- For he shall be like the heath in the desert, and shall not see when good cometh; but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, in a salt land and not inhabited. 7- Blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD, and whose hope the LORD is. 8- For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green; and shall not be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit.
His arm: his strength, because man works with the arm and his strength is shown by it.
God warns the kingdom of Judah against relying on men and their strength, for these lose God's help and are cursed by Him, because they have turned away from Him and rejected Him.
The heath: a dry plant without fruit that appears in the desert.
The desert: the wilderness.
The parched places: the hot land, that is, one with no plants or fruits, which means the absence of fruit in the man.
A salt land: salty land unfit for cultivation.

God's people relied on men, as when they tried to rely on Egypt to fortify themselves against Assyria and Babylon instead of relying on God, so they became a dry people without fruit like the heath in the desert: when the plants give fruit and good, it does not give, and it dwells in an uninhabited land, like the salt land or the extremely hot one. The meaning is that whoever does not trust in God does not enjoy spiritual fruits in his life and becomes despised by people and loses material blessings as well.
On the contrary, whoever trusts in God receives many blessings in his life, whether spiritual or material.

He likens the man who trusts in God to a tree planted beside a stream of water, which spreads its roots in the ground and finds water sufficient for it, so that it does not suffer from the heat or the drought that comes upon all plants, because it is planted beside the stream of water. The stream of water here means God, on whom His children rely, so they are not troubled by the afflictions of life.

Seek God before every work and you will feel His help, and your heart will no longer be troubled however much afflictions come upon you, because He rescues you from them and is even glorified in you through them.

entries.section: (3) The reward of the righteous and the wicked

paragraphs.text: God warns His children in the kingdom of Judah not to walk in evil with their wicked hearts, lest their heart become desperately wicked, that is, bitter.
Seek God before every work and you will feel His help, and your heart will no longer be troubled however much afflictions come upon you.

entries.section: (3) The reward of the righteous and the wicked

paragraphs.text: God declares of Himself that He is the One who knows the secrets of hearts, and therefore He punishes His wicked people with captivity, that perhaps they may repent, and rewards His obedient children with peace and joy.

entries.section: (3) The reward of the righteous and the wicked

paragraphs.text: The partridge: a wild bird with long legs and a red beak that lived in Palestine and laid its eggs in nests on the ground and not on trees.

The partridge used to sit on and sleep upon the eggs of other birds, and when the eggs hatched, it would produce chicks foreign to it that soon left it, so that it gained nothing from all its labor. This bird is like one who gets riches by unlawful means, for they are lost to him afterward, whether by their loss or by his death, so he gains nothing from what he obtained.
It seems that this verse was a proverb that people repeated, and God used it here to forbid the love of money and the acquiring of it by unlawful means such as theft and exploitation.

entries.section: (3) The reward of the righteous and the wicked

paragraphs.text: On the other side, God declares that His holy place in His house is great and high above all the earthly things with which the people of the world are occupied and in which they waste their lives.

entries.section: (3) The reward of the righteous and the wicked

paragraphs.text: Whoever forsakes the holy God loses his purity and exaltation and loses his eternal heavenly place, and his life clings to the dust from which he was taken, so he is written in it, that is, he dies and his life ends in passing earthly things. And Jeremiah directs the attention of God's people to the fact that their hope is God, that they may come out of their material afflictions and their preoccupation with sin and earthly things, for He is the fountain of true living water, and not riches and money.

Do not forget that you are a child of heaven, because your Father is heavenly; so do not be occupied with passing material things and do not be troubled by the afflictions of life, because God is able to rescue you from them, and you will remain like Him at all times.

Jeremiah speaks as a servant on behalf of his people, declaring that he is a sinner in need of God's healing, and with humility also declares his personal need for healing, and in this way he is an example to his people in returning to God by repentance. He asks God to heal him from the wounds of sin and rescue him from all his troubles, so that he may continue to praise God and enjoy constant prayer with Him.

At the time when Jeremiah offers repentance before God, the people deny the existence of God and His work, and say of Him that He does not carry out His word and does not punish the one who sins; indeed they mock and say, “Where is the word of the LORD? let it come now,” if it is true.
I have not withdrawn: I have not abandoned my place as a shepherd of the people.

But Jeremiah was not affected by the words of the people who doubted God's work, and continued to shepherd his people and warn them to repent; and in all this he follows God and takes refuge in Him, for God is his leader in all his service. And in the spirit of fatherhood he did not wish that God's wrath should come upon his people to punish them for their sins, that they might know that His word is true and so answer their mockery.

But he wishes that God would be longsuffering until his people repent, and God bears witness against himself that he asked in his prayers to God for repentance for his people, besides that God knows his heart and feelings and fatherhood toward the people.
Jeremiah asks for himself and for all the people God's tenderness and mercy, that He not repay them for their sins with fear and affliction, because He is their refuge in all their afflictions.
The day of evil: the day of affliction.

In faith he asks the help of God, who reassures him, and at the same time frightens his enemies and defeats them and crushes them before him; so even if affliction comes upon him from the enemies, God is able to deliver him from their hands and crush them. This was fulfilled in God's keeping Jeremiah in the faith throughout his life, while those of the people who troubled him were terrified before Babylon, and the Babylonians too, their kingdom passed away after years at the hand of the kingdom of the Medes and Persians.

Be confident in the power of your God, who protects you however much the wars of the demons rise against you and however much you fall; He is able to raise you up and defeat them before you, and even to gladden your heart with His consolations until you obtain glory in the Kingdom of Heaven.
(5) Breaking the Sabbath (vv. 19-27:)

19- Thus said the LORD unto me; Go and stand in the gate of the children of the people, whereby the kings of Judah come in, and by the which they go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem; 20- And say unto them, Hear ye the word of the LORD, ye kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, that enter in by these gates: 21- Thus saith the LORD; Take heed to yourselves, and bear no burden on the sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem; 22- Neither carry forth a burden out of your houses on the sabbath day, neither do ye any work, but hallow ye the sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers. 23- But they obeyed not, neither inclined their ear, but made their neck stiff, that they might not hear, nor receive instruction. 24- And it shall come to pass, if ye diligently hearken unto me, saith the LORD, to bring in no burden through the gates of this city on the sabbath day, but hallow the sabbath day, to do no work therein;

25- Then shall there enter into the gates of this city kings and princes sitting upon the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses, they, and their princes, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: and this city shall remain for ever.

26- And they shall come from the cities of Judah, and from the places about Jerusalem, and from the land of Benjamin, and from the plain, and from the mountains, and from the south, bringing burnt offerings, and sacrifices, and meat offerings, and incense, and bringing sacrifices of praise, unto the house of the LORD.

27- But if ye will not hearken unto me to hallow the sabbath day, and not to bear a burden, even entering in at the gates of Jerusalem on the sabbath day; then will I kindle a fire in the gates thereof, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem, and it shall not be quenched.

God asked Jeremiah to stand in the gate by which the kings of Judah, that is, the leaders of the people, and most of the people enter, for it is one of the gates of Jerusalem by which many enter, and it may be the Benjamin Gate; and He means that he should declare the following word to all the people, since they all pass, entering or leaving Jerusalem, by this gate and all the other gates, because the city of Jerusalem had many gates. The spiritual meaning of this is that we should declare the word of God to all who are around us and not to some only, and call everyone to be bound to the Church.

God's command through Jeremiah is not to work on the Sabbath day, whether by carrying goods from outside Jerusalem into it, that is, buying these goods, or by carrying loads from their houses to sell outside Jerusalem, but to hallow the Sabbath day and set it apart for the worship of God.

God declares with regret that His people refused to obey the commandment to keep the Sabbath, and their hearts were hard, so they were empty of every feeling of sonship toward God; and their disobedience is shown by the stiffness of their necks, as the unruly, rebellious animal refuses to have the yoke put on its neck and to submit to its owner; indeed they also murmured against God's discipline of them and did not understand that this was because of their sins.

He declares the blessings of obeying the commandment to keep the Sabbath in order to encourage them to keep it: that if they obey they will have great kings riding in chariots and on horses who will rule them, and they will live in peace and security; indeed He promises them not only rest in the earthly Jerusalem but also in the heavenly Jerusalem forever in the Kingdom of Heaven if they keep His commandments.

He completes the blessings that come from their obeying His commandments, that the Jews will come from every place, and He mentions here six regions to declare that from every place the believers will come and offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and holy worship to God.
And on the contrary, if they do not obey God's commandment, God allows the enemies, who are the Babylonians, to destroy Jerusalem and burn its gates and all its palaces.
Take care to obey the commandments of God, for they keep you from every evil, and you enjoy God's care for you and fellowship with Him on earth and then glories in heaven.
The potter and the plot against Jeremiah
Arise: it means hastening to carry out the command. It signifies the resurrection with Christ.

Go down: the potters most often made their workshops in the valleys to find clay suitable for their work, so He said to him, “go down,” that is, go down to the low valley. Going down signifies humility. God commanded Jeremiah to go to the potter's house, that is, one who works in making pottery, to hear the word of God, who provides an illustration for His word, namely the making of pottery.
And for a man to be able to hear the voice of God, he must be with Him, so that his life is renewed and he is able to be humble and hear and understand the word of God.
The wheels: the device on which the clay is shaped to make the pottery vessels.

When Jeremiah went to the potter's house he found him making a clay vessel on the wheel, and then he noticed that the vessel was marred; and it does not say that the potter marred it, because the potter signifies God and the clay vessel signifies men, who spoil their lives themselves by their distance from God. But God in His love reshapes the clay again and mends the vessel that was marred; for although it was marred, it is still in His hands, and if they repent and return to Him He renews their nature and makes them vessels of honor according to His good pleasure and what seems good to Him, as He renewed the human race by His redemption through the sacrament of Baptism.

When Jeremiah saw the potter's work as an illustration, God said to him: I am able, like this potter, to reshape you after you have spoiled your lives by sin, and to renew you. So He gives hope to His people that they may repent and return to Him, and He will restore them to their first sonship to Him and their pure life.

Trust in the power of God, who is able to renew your life however many or repeated your sins, for He is your Father who loves you and you are always in His hands; so return to Him in repentance and ask His help, and He will mend your life.

God declares His plan in dealing with men: if He finds them in an evil way of life, He decides that He will destroy them and pluck them up like trees, that is, kill them. This is not a final decision but a declaration of His anger at their evils, that perhaps they may repent and be delivered from this anger; and this shows the love of God, who wants all to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth, and does not desire the destruction of anyone.
If this nation turns from its evil way of life and repents, God does not punish it; for what is meant by the evil that God would have brought upon it is its punishment.
The other case is that God promises the nation good, building up and blessings, and what is meant by planting is steadfastness, as the tree is fixed in the ground.
“In My sight:” any evil that a man does is against God and a defiance of Him.

“I will repent:” God speaks in human terms, which is to go back on what was decided; but in truth God knows everything before it is, and does not repent of anything, but He knows that He did not give them good because of their evils. So God's use of these words is like a grown person's use of words suited to children when he talks with them, not because he does not know the language of grown-ups but so as to be understood by the children.
If this nation leaves God and does sins before Him and refuses to obey His commandments, God does not do good to it and does not give it blessings.

Every wrong you do to others is directed against God, because all men are His image, and even if the sin is in your thought and in your heart, it is a defiance of God. Return to Him in repentance, for He is ready to forget all your sins.
Amend your ways: walk in the way of God and keep away from the ways of evil.
God warns His people of punishment for their sins, for divine decrees have been issued to punish them, that perhaps they may fear and return to Him, and He will lift this punishment from them.

Sadly, God's people answered Him badly, for they made light of His word and considered it vain, that is, worthless, and insisted on persisting in their evil thoughts and deeds; that is, they refused repentance and continued in sin.

God marvels at His people's rejection of His word, and the peoples of the world bear witness against them, who obey their pagan gods, whereas God's people, who ought to have been loving and clinging to Him, rejected Him and persisted in their evil; and He likens them to the virgin who has only her bridegroom, because she is not bound to any other man.

God rebukes His people that He loved them and gave them water in the form of snow on the tops of the rocks in the high mountains such as Lebanon, and when the snow melts it turns into flowing water that runs continually and waters man, animal and plant. So God gives them His heavenly blessings; why then do they not worship Him and thank Him? Why did they turn to the worship of idols?
The ancient paths: the ways of the fathers who lived with God and kept His commandments.
Paths: winding roads in the desert between the mountains, which are hard to travel.

Not cast up: a hard way that cannot be walked, which is the way of the worship of idols and evil. God continues His rebuke of His people, who neglected His blessings and forgot God's favors to them, who brought them out by a wondrous power from the land of Egypt and kept them in the wilderness of Sinai and fed them from heaven and gave them to drink from the rock. They left God, the Maker of good things, and went to burn incense to vanity, that is, the worship of idols, and the wicked caused the rest of the people to stumble, so they turned away from the straight ways of the fathers and walked in rugged ways that destroy them, which are the ways of the worship of idols.
Wag his head: shakes his head in mockery and grief.
I will show them the back: I will abandon them.
As a result of God's people's persistence in sin, God warns them of these punishments that they may repent, which are:

1- Their cities will be demolished and their land will become desolate, and this was accomplished at the hand of Babylon; this signifies the loss of the possessions and desires to which the wicked man clings, and no one dwells in them, but there is heard in them the hissing of the winds, that is, their strong sound that moves with force because there are no walls or buildings.

2- Every man who passes by these ruined cities, which perished because of their evils, will be astonished and mock. This signifies the demons' mockery of us when we persist in evil, so that we are cast into eternal torment.

3- The inhabitants of Judah will be scattered like those pursued by a hot, violent wind, which is the east wind, and they flee lest they be suffocated by its heat; this signifies the cruelty of the wars of the demons that strike those who are far from God and the careless, scattering them and destroying them.

4- The hardest punishment is God's abandoning them, so that He turns away His face, that is, His care for them, and leaves them to suffer afflictions because they rejected following Him and insist on that, so the afflictions are very severe upon them; and this signifies eternal torment.

When you see afflictions come upon you or upon others, know that they are warnings from God so that you turn from your sins, and when you ask God's help your eyes are opened and you see His blessings and thank Him, and your soul lives in you.
Shall not perish: shall not depart.
Smite him with the tongue: catch him in a word that condemns him, and punish him and kill him.

The people resisted the prophet Jeremiah because he prophesied the devastation of Jerusalem and their destruction, and they said that he was not a prophet because the word of God does not depart from the prophet, whereas Jeremiah does not speak the word of God but evil against the people; likewise he is not wise and has neither the Law nor counsel. Then they tried to catch him in a wrong word that he would say so that they could punish him for it, and thereby declare his words void so that no one would listen to him; that is, when they think his words are wrong by catching words against him, they make the people doubt him and not listen to his words. And in this they are not resisting Jeremiah only but rather God who sent him, and they reject His word.
Jeremiah calls on God for help to defend him against those who stand as adversaries to him and resist him, so that He hears their slanders and answers them.
Jeremiah marvels that his people answered his love with evil, for he stood before God asking mercy for his people, but they repaid his goodness with evil and wanted to kill him.
Bereaved: mothers whose children have died.

In the spirit of prophecy Jeremiah speaks of what will happen to his people, and not in a spirit of vengeance for what they say about him and their attempt to take revenge on him, because his fatherhood is clear throughout this book (Jer 14:17) (Jer 9:1) (Jer 8:21). So he prophesies the death of the young men and the men, and the women becoming bereaved and widows.

The people tried to kill Jeremiah by throwing him into a pit or catching him in their nets by trapping him with a word or trying to kill him by anything; therefore God takes vengeance on them by His divine justice, so Babylon attacks them, and cries come from all their houses for the death of many of them.

Jeremiah asks for divine justice for the evils of his people because of their counsel, so that they are punished with destruction. This is not only a prophecy but a declaration to the people, that perhaps they may repent, and he gains their souls because he loves them.

Do not resist the one who rebukes you, for it may be a message from God on his tongue, even if he increases the rebuke and blame; and if his word is wrong, make an excuse for him and do not take vengeance on him or wrong him.
The breaking of the earthen bottle

God asked Jeremiah to buy an earthen water bottle made of pottery and to take with him a group of the priests and elders of the people to be witnesses to the word of God that He would declare before them. Although the priests and elders of the people did not want to hear his word and resisted him, some of them might have been willing to listen, or some agreed so as to catch him in a word.

The valley of the son of Hinnom: a valley lying southeast of Jerusalem into which the carcases of animals were thrown and burned with fire, so the fire was always burning in it, in addition to the throwing in of animal refuse, rubbish and broken earthen vessels. The word “Gehenna” was taken from “the valley of Hinnom” because the fire was always burning in it.

The east gate: a gate of Jerusalem lying to the southeast, also called the Dung Gate, that is, the gate of the refuse of animals, because through it they go out with the remains of animals and the broken earthen vessels to throw them into the valley of the son of Hinnom.

God commanded Jeremiah to take with him the priests, the elders and the bottle, and to go to the Potsherd Gate and go out by it and stand before the valley of the son of Hinnom to declare the word of God there.
His ears shall tingle: the ear hears a very loud sound in it that almost makes it lose its hearing; what is meant is a very hideous report, hard for any ear to hear.

Jeremiah directed his speech not to the people only but to the kings also, for he declares the voice of God with power to all the wicked and fears no one whatever his position, because God seeks the salvation of all.

And God describes Himself as “the LORD of hosts,” declaring His might and ability to carry out the hardest things, and says that He will do something very dreadful at which everyone will be astonished, indeed in its harshness they will not be able to hear it, namely God's forsaking His people and leaving them in the hands of Babylon, that they may crush them and humiliate them because of the multitude of His people's sins and their refusal to repent. All this God declares that perhaps His people may fear Him and turn from their sins, and He will receive them.

Be ready to hear the voice of God and His rebuke at the hand of any person, however small, so that you learn every day and rescue yourself from evil and find a place for yourself in the Kingdom of Heaven.
They have estranged this place: they turned the Promised Land into an unclean land through their worship of idols, so they denied God's ownership and His presence in this place.
Jeremiah summed up the sins of the people in:
1- Forsaking God and His love and fellowship and holding to His commandments.
2- Defiling the land with their evils.
3- The worship of strange idols and the burning of incense to them.
4- The shedding of the blood of the innocent, whom they offered as human sacrifices to please the pagan gods such as (Molech).

5- The building of high places on the elevated sites for the pagan gods such as Baal, and offering human sacrifices to them, namely their sons, whom they burned to please the idols; and all this, of course, God did not command, for He never commanded that human sacrifices be offered to Him. And the story of Isaac was to show the love of Abraham and Isaac for Him, and He did not allow the sacrifice to be carried out.

entries.section: (2) Their discipline and the breaking of the bottle

paragraphs.text: Tophet: a place in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and the meaning of the word is spitting or burning; and in Tophet there was a pit filled with wood in which fire was kindled, so what is meant by Tophet is the valley of the son of Hinnom, or the valley of burning. God declares His anger against the kingdom of Judah, which disobeys Him, and the following comes upon it:

1- Instead of the carcases of animals being thrown in the valley of the son of Hinnom (that is, Tophet), those whom Babylon will kill will be thrown there, and this valley is called the valley of slaughter because of the multitude of the slain who were thrown into it.
2- Because of the multitude of the slain the birds of prey and the beasts attack to eat their corpses.
3- Jerusalem and the kingdom of Judah are laid waste, and everyone who passes by them is astonished and hisses at them, that is, grieves deeply at what has happened to them.
4- A famine occurs so that people are compelled to eat their sons and their friends so as not to die of hunger.

entries.section: (2) Their discipline and the breaking of the bottle

paragraphs.text: After Jeremiah declared the sins of the people and God's discipline of them before the eyes of the priests and elders, he suddenly threw the new earthen bottle into the valley of the son of Hinnom and it was shattered and became small pieces that could not be restored to be a bottle, and he said: Thus will God crush this people, and they will become subject to killing and burning like the valley of the son of Hinnom, because of the multitude of their sins.

entries.section: (2) Their discipline and the breaking of the bottle

paragraphs.text: God's punishment of His people extends to the places where they worshiped idols, namely the roofs of their palaces and houses, which will be defiled by the falling of the slain in them, because the bodies of the dead were unclean in the eyes of the Jews; that is, the places of their idol worship become places of uncleanness, because they forsook God.

God's warnings and rebukes to you, indeed the afflictions that come upon you, are not divine vengeance against you but divine declarations that call you to repentance, that you may return to Him and He lift all His wrath from you.

entries.section: (3) In the court of the LORD's house

paragraphs.text: After Jeremiah prophesied in Tophet, that is, the valley of the son of Hinnom, he entered Jerusalem and stood in the court of the LORD's house, where the people gather for worship, to declare the word of God again.

entries.section: (3) In the court of the LORD's house

paragraphs.text: Jeremiah repeated his words about God's anger and His discipline of Jerusalem and all the villages of Judea in the kingdom of Judah, because the people disobeyed God and refused to submit to His commandments, as the animal stiffens its neck and refuses to bear the yoke and pull the farming implements.
God repeats His word to you many times through those around you so that you repent; so do not be vexed at this but thank Him and submit to Him, and you will find your life.
Pashhur's resistance to Jeremiah

entries.section: (1) Pashhur's trembling over his striking Jeremiah

paragraphs.text: Pashhur the son of Immer: a leading priest in the temple, and the meaning of his name is “fruitful on every side”; chief governor. A chief priest in the house of the LORD.

These words: Jeremiah's words of devastation for Jerusalem and the temple, which he declared in the previous chapter (ch. 19:15).
