The Elamites become very afraid, and Babylon kills many of them.

God sets His throne in Elam, and what is meant by this is Babylon’s dominion over them, because Babylon is the divine instrument in chastening the nations, and God destroys the king and the princes of Elam.

God gives hope to Elam of a return from captivity, not only after the fall of Babylon but also through the faith of the Elamites in Christ. They are mentioned in the second chapter of the book of Acts as being gathered in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost, and they believed in Christ.

Some may think that their bodily strength, their material weapons, the various powers of the world and their possessions may give them success. But let your strength be spiritual, that is, your faith in Christ, who is able to overcome the world, so that you are not troubled by all its changes.
Prophecies about Babylon

Babylon: it is first mentioned in (Gen 10:10), where it was founded by a rebellious person called Nimrod. In it appeared man’s pride and his refusal to submit to God in the attempt to build a tower, so God confused the tongues of those gathered (Gen 11:9). It appeared as a kingdom in the eighteenth century before Christ in the reign of Hammurabi, who laid down the laws known by his name, and in the third century before Christ its greatest power appeared in the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, who seized all the surrounding countries as far as the Mediterranean Sea and triumphed over many kings, establishing his empire.

The Chaldeans: they dwelt in Mesopotamia in the tenth century before Christ, and from them Abraham came out. In this chapter and the next, God speaks in prophecies through Jeremiah against Babylon, and He gave it much speech, equal to all of Jeremiah’s prophecies about the various countries of the world, because Babylon’s evil was greater than that of the other countries. God used it to chasten His people and to chasten the countries of the world, but in the end He must chasten it.

Set up a standard: declare clearly before all, like a standard raised before everyone. Bel: an Akkadian name meaning “the lord”, corresponding in Hebrew to the god Baal; it is also one of the names of the god Merodach, and he was depicted in the form of a great head with a crown on his head and with seven bull’s horns.
Merodach: he was a god of the city of Babylon, and because of its greatness he was considered the king of the gods, and many kings of Babylon were named after him.

God declares His decision for the fall of Babylon and its shattering, despite its exalting itself over all the countries of the world, and declares the weakness of its pagan gods, the most important of which is Merodach, who is also called Bel. Because this decision must be carried out, God commands that it be proclaimed among all the peoples and not concealed from anyone, because Babylon was proud and humbled the whole world.

The reason for the fall of Babylon is the attack of the new empire formed by the union of the two kingdoms of Media and Persia, which dwell to its east and north. They will attack Babylon from the north and ruin it, so that no life remains in it and neither man nor beast can dwell in it, but it becomes deserted.

Nothing of the powers of the world that you rely on will profit you before the divine wrath. Neither its idols, nor its greatness, nor its wealth profited Babylon. So trust in God and humble yourself before Him, and you will find your protection.
[2] The return of Israel from captivity (vv. 4-8:)

4- In those days, and in that time, saith the LORD, the children of Israel shall come, they and the children of Judah together, going and weeping: they shall go, and seek the LORD their God. 5- They shall ask the way to Zion with their faces thitherward, saying, Come, and let us join ourselves to the LORD in a perpetual covenant that shall not be forgotten. 6- My people hath been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray, they have turned them away on the mountains: they have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their restingplace. 7- All that found them have devoured them: and their adversaries said, We offend not, because they have sinned against the LORD, the habitation of justice, even the LORD, the hope of their fathers. 8- Remove out of the midst of Babylon, and go forth out of the land of the Chaldeans, and be as the he goats before the flocks.

God gives good news to His people of its two kingdoms, Israel and Judah, that they will return from captivity through their repentance, their return to God and their weeping over their sins, so that God has compassion on them and brings them back to their land.

Zion: an ancient name of a fortress beside Jerusalem, and what is meant by Zion is all Jerusalem. The people of God return to Jerusalem to build the temple, pray, offer sacrifices, remember their covenants with God, and offer repentance and an everlasting covenant to live with Him.
Restingplace: the place in which the sheep rest and sleep (that is, the fold), and what is meant is the house of God and His city Jerusalem, where they worship God.

God gives the reason for His people’s straying and distance from Him: it is the lack of care of their shepherds for them; rather, because of their corruption they made the people stray far from Him. He expresses this by the mountains and the hills, where they worshiped strange gods upon them and abandoned the worship of God.

Because of the evils of the people of God and their distance from Him, they became prey to the nations, who led them astray and took them captive, whether Assyria, and before it Egypt, and after it Babylon. These enemies of the people of God were instruments of chastening in the hand of God for His people, because they strayed from Him although He is the cause of their righteousness, and they dwell in His house and His city, and He is their hope in all their troubles. But sadly they left Him and became booty for their enemies, each of whom devours them and exploits them.
He goats: male goats.

God calls His people to go out of Babylon after it was struck and Cyrus, the first of the kings of Media and Persia, took the kingdom and permitted them to return to their land. God urges them to go out of Babylon and return to their land. The return of the people of God to Jerusalem and their worship of Him symbolizes the return to God at faith in Christ in the fullness of time. God asks His people to be an example to the rest of the peoples in faith in Christ, like the he goats that go out quickly from the folds and run to the pasture, and the rest of the sheep follow them.

The love of God, His tenderness and His mercy are great toward everyone who repents and returns to Him. So do not delay repentance, however great your sins or the straying you have reached; He still loves you and awaits your repentance to give you salvation and to compensate you for the misery of sin that you suffered from your distance from Him.
[3] The invasion of Babylon (vv. 9-16:)

9- For, lo, I will raise and cause to come up against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the north country: and they shall set themselves in array against her; from thence she shall be taken: their arrows shall be as of a mighty expert man; none shall return in vain. 10- And Chaldea shall be a spoil: all that spoil her shall be satisfied, saith the LORD. 11- Because ye were glad, because ye rejoiced, O ye destroyers of mine heritage, because ye are grown fat as the heifer at grass, and bellow as bulls; 12- Your mother shall be sore confounded; she that bare you shall be ashamed: behold, the hindermost of the nations shall be a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert. 31- Because of the wrath of the LORD it shall not be inhabited, but it shall be wholly desolate: every one that goeth by Babylon shall be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues. 14- Put yourselves in array against Babylon round about: all ye that bend the bow, shoot at her, spare no arrows: for she hath sinned against the LORD. 15- Shout against her round about: she hath given her hand: her foundations are fallen, her walls are thrown down: for it is the vengeance of the LORD: take vengeance upon her; as she hath done, do unto her. 16- Cut off the sower from Babylon, and him that handleth the sickle in the time of harvest: for fear of the oppressing sword they shall turn every one to his people, and they shall flee every one to his own land.

God declares that He is the One responsible for the chastening and ruin of Babylon, so He raises up against it Media and Persia, whom He likens to a sleeper whom God has awakened. That is, God is the Ruler of all, and He chastens Babylon because it wronged and exploited all the peoples of the earth, so He raises up peoples against it to ruin it.

These peoples come from the north, for Media and Persia attacked Babylon from the north. They set themselves in array against it, that is, besieged it. He describes Media and Persia as the mighty man who destroys what is before him and shoots his arrows at his prey, Babylon, so that it falls, and this mighty man does not return until he has achieved his aim, which is the seizure of Babylon. Babylon submitted easily at the beginning of the rule of Media and Persia, but it rebelled again, so they struck it.
The Chaldeans: they are the original inhabitants of Mesopotamia and Babylon.

Media and Persia seize the land of Babylon and take its many spoils, so that Media and Persia are greatly satisfied. Grass (pasture): herbs, and what is meant is the wheat and barley when they are threshed to separate their grain from the chaff.

Heifer: a young cow. God declares the reason for the chastening of Babylon: it gloated over the people of God when it seized its lands and spoils, like a heifer that pulls the threshing sledge to thresh wheat and barley and leaps for joy; that is, Babylon rejoiced in the humiliation of the people of God. He also likens Babylon to a horse that leaps and gives strong sounds, which is neighing, and rejoices; that is, Babylon rejoiced in the destruction of Judah and Israel.

Babylon claimed to be a mother of the peoples and was not so, because it did not have compassion on the peoples of the world but humbled them. So God speaks to these peoples and tells them that your mother Babylon, that is, the one who claimed to be your mother, has fallen into shame and disgrace because it was struck and became a wilderness and a deserted place with no water or life, although it was a fertile land; its springs dried up and it became ruin.
The LORD’s wrath was upon Babylon, so it became deserted, and everyone who passes by it is astonished and hisses, so great is his astonishment at the ruin of Babylon, which was very great.
God calls the soldiers of Media and Persia to shoot many arrows at it and kill those in it, because they rebelled against the LORD.

God continues His speech to the soldiers of Media and Persia, that they shout the shout of victory against it on every side, because it has surrendered and given its hand, so it no longer has strength to resist the soldiers of Media and Persia, who demolished it, removed its foundations and broke its walls. They take vengeance on it because it is the command of the LORD, and by this it receives its recompense: as it did evil to all the peoples, so they do evil to it and shatter it.
Sickle: a curved knife with which they gather the stalks of wheat and barley.

Because Babylon will become deserted and lose its fertility, and there is no one to sow it or reap anything from it, and those in it flee for fear of the sword of Media and Persia that kills the inhabitants of Babylon, those who left their lands when Babylon took them captive return, leave it and go back to their lands to live in security. Though Babylon was the most secure place in the world and a realm of wealth, it became a terror to everyone who stayed in it, so they fled from it.

Whoever deceives God and has no compassion on those around him and wrongs them, God takes vengeance on him, even if after a while. So do not go on in evil or wrongdoing, and return quickly by repentance, and God will have mercy on you.
[4] The punishment of the enemies (vv. 17-20)

17- Israel is a scattered sheep; the lions have driven him away: first the king of Assyria hath devoured him; and last this Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath broken his bones. 18- Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I have punished the king of Assyria. 19- And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead. 20- In those days, and in that time, saith the LORD, the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve.

God likens the enemies of His people to lions, and His people to sheep. When lions attack sheep they eat them as prey and rule them. The first lion is Assyria, which took the kingdom of Israel captive; then after it came the kingdom of Babylon under the leadership of Nebuchadnezzar, which took the kingdom of Judah captive and ruled it, and Israel, harshly, because it seized all the countries that had been subject to Assyria.

Satan, our enemy, takes different forms such as Assyria or Babylon, but he is violent and wants to control us. We cannot escape from his hand unless we hold fast to God. We do not fear the lions as long as we are under God’s protection, and our God is able not only to turn the lions away from us but also to punish them and protect us with a complete protection.
Broken his bones (crushed): I will make bruises in him, that is, severe contusions, and what is meant is: I will humble him and shatter his strength.

God gives good news to His people that He will lift the dominion of Babylon from them and shatter it. As He shattered Assyria at the hand of Babylon, He will shatter Babylon at the hand of Media and Persia. He chastens His people by Assyria and Babylon, but when His people repent, He punishes Assyria and Babylon for their many evils.
Carmel and Bashan: fertile places in Lebanon lying in the portion of Ephraim, which yield many good things.

Gilead: it lies east of the river Jordan and is distinguished by fertility; in it are balsam trees whose sap is a costly medicine. Gilead lies in the portion of the two tribes of Reuben and Manasseh. At the time when God punishes Babylon, He brings His people back to dwell in their land at the beginning of the rule of the kingdom of Media and Persia, so they return to their lands overflowing with milk and honey, that is, many good things.

If the nations around the people of God thought that this people was sinful and that God was punishing it, then when He brings them back to their land full of good things, God declares that He has forgiven their sins and pardoned them because they repented and returned to Him. God rewards His repentant children with abiding, stability and peace.
[5] The destruction of Babylon (vv. 21-32:)

21- Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod: waste and utterly destroy after them, saith the LORD, and do according to all that I have commanded thee. 22- A sound of battle is in the land, and of great destruction. 23- How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken! how is Babylon become a desolation among the nations! 24- I have laid a snare for thee, and thou art also taken, O Babylon, and thou wast not aware: thou art found, and also caught, because thou hast striven against the LORD. 25- The LORD hath opened his armoury, and hath brought forth the weapons of his indignation: for this is the work of the Lord GOD of hosts in the land of the Chaldeans. 26- Come against her from the utmost border, open her storehouses: cast her up as heaps, and destroy her utterly: let nothing of her be left. 27- Slay all her bullocks; let them go down to the slaughter: woe unto them! for their day is come, the time of their visitation. 28- The voice of them that flee and escape out of the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance of his temple. 29- Call together the archers against Babylon: all ye that bend the bow, camp against it round about; let none thereof escape: recompense her according to her work; according to all that she hath done, do unto her: for she hath been proud against the LORD, against the Holy One of Israel. 30- Therefore shall her young men fall in the streets, and all her men of war shall be cut off in that day, saith the LORD. 31- Behold, I am against thee, O thou most proud, saith the Lord GOD of hosts: for thy day is come, the time that I will visit thee. 32- And the most proud shall stumble and fall, and none shall raise him up: and I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all round about him.
Merathaim: it lies south of Babylon, and its meaning is double rebellion.

Pekod: it lies east of Babylon, and its meaning is punishment. Utterly destroy after them: kill. God declares to the enemies of Babylon, that is, Media and Persia, who attack it to ruin it in every part of it, whether in the east or the south, that they are to punish it for its rebellion against God.
The sound of the fighting soldiers and the instruments of war will be heard in Babylon, in addition to the sounds of shattering and destruction that take place in it.

He likens Babylon to the hammer that shatters what it falls upon, for it shattered and seized all the countries of the world around it. Now God punishes it, cutting it off and shattering it at the hand of Media and Persia, and lays waste its buildings.
Snare: a trap. Taken: it fell into the trap and became unable to get out of it.

God permitted the snare for Babylon, which is the attack of Media and Persia on it, and it fell into weakness and did not know how to resist, and Babylon was ruined because it walked in evil and stood as an adversary to God by destroying His people, so it deserved to be punished.

His indignation: His wrath. God likens Himself to a great man who has storehouses from which He brought out the instruments of His wrath, and what is meant is the chastening of Babylon at the hand of Media and Persia. This is His work in the land of Babylon, in which the Chaldeans dwell.

The utmost border: the farthest east in relation to Babylon is the kingdom of Media and Persia. Her storehouses: her granaries; the granaries are the barns in which the grain is gathered after its harvest. Heaps: piles. He asks Media and Persia to attack Babylon and open its treasuries, plunder it and ruin it, so that it becomes ruined hills, and to kill all who are in it.
He required the enemies of Babylon not only to kill the people dwelling in it but also its beasts, to put an end to life in it and to all its good things.

Some of the inhabitants of Babylon fled, who had believed in God as a result of their association with the Jews who were in captivity, and came to Jerusalem, which is Zion, and declared the punishment that came upon Babylon from the God of Israel, and perhaps they declared their faith and joined the people of God.
Proud (she acted insolently): she wronged.

He calls the soldiers of Media and Persia, who are distinguished in shooting arrows with the bow, to aim their arrows at Babylon and kill those in it because it wronged the people of God, Israel. Whoever assaults the people of God assaults God Himself, so God punishes it severely. This is its natural recompense, because it humbled the peoples of the earth, among whom were the people of God. As it punished the peoples, it is punished now.
On the day of the attack of the army of Media and Persia on Babylon, they kill its young men and its fighting soldiers, that is, they put an end to its strength.
The day of the attack of Media and Persia is the day of the punishment of Babylon, which wronged the peoples of the earth.
Wrongdoing Babylon falls and finds no one to raise it, because God commanded its punishment, and God permits them to burn its palaces and houses.

If you have strength and capacities, do not wrong others by them but use them to help the weak and the needy. Know that if you do not have mercy on others, God will not have mercy on you, and in proportion to how you wrong people God will judge you. [6] The punishment of the oppressor (vv. 33-46)

33- Thus saith the LORD of hosts; The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together: and all that took them captives held them fast; they refused to let them go. 34- Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of hosts is his name: he shall throughly plead their cause, that he may give rest to the land, and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon. 35- A sword is upon the Chaldeans, saith the LORD, and upon the inhabitants of Babylon, and upon her princes, and upon her wise men. 36- A sword is upon the liars; and they shall dote: a sword is upon her mighty men; and they shall be dismayed. 37- A sword is upon their horses, and upon their chariots, and upon all the mingled people that are in the midst of her; and they shall become as women: a sword is upon her treasures; and they shall be robbed. 38- A drought is upon her waters; and they shall be dried up: for it is the land of graven images, and they are mad upon their idols. 39- Therefore the wild beasts of the desert with the wild beasts of the islands shall dwell there, and the owls shall dwell therein: and it shall be no more inhabited for ever; neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation. 04- As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof, saith the LORD; so shall no man abide there, neither shall any son of man dwell therein. 41- Behold, a people shall come from the north, and a great nation, and many kings shall be raised up from the coasts of the earth. 42- They shall hold the bow and the lance: they are cruel, and will not shew mercy: their voice shall roar like the sea, and they shall ride upon horses, every one put in array, like a man to the battle, against thee, O daughter of Babylon. 43- The king of Babylon hath heard the report of them, and his hands waxed feeble: anguish took hold of him, and pangs as of a woman in travail. 44- Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan unto the habitation of the strong: but I will make them suddenly run away from her: and who is a chosen man, that I may appoint over her? for who is like me? and who will appoint me the time? and who is that shepherd that will stand before me? 45- Therefore hear ye the counsel of the LORD, that he hath taken against Babylon; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out: surely he shall make their habitation desolate with them. 46- At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved, and the cry is heard among the nations.

God speaks of His poor people in the two kingdoms of Israel and Judah, and how they were subjected to the wrongdoing of Assyria and then Babylon, who led them astray and took them into captivity and did not release them but treated them with violence and cruelty.

The land: what is meant is the land of His people. God declares His responsibility for His people, for He is their Redeemer, that is, their kinsman responsible for them, and at the same time His power is great, for His name is the LORD of hosts. He will examine their case and their plea and the petitions lifted up to Him, and will do them justice, give them rest in their land and punish Babylon, which humbled them.

God declares that Media and Persia will kill the people of Babylon who dwell in it, and also the leaders of the people with the king, in addition to the king’s counselors, who are the wise men of the state.
The liars: the false prophets, the sorcerers and the astrologers. Her mighty men: the commanders of the army.
The sword of Media and Persia will kill the false prophets and the astrologers, who have great standing in the state, and also the commanders of its armies.
Their horses and chariots: its weapons of war. The mingled people: the non-Babylonian inhabitants who support Babylon, that is, its allies.
Her treasures: her good things.

The hand of Media and Persia will stretch out to kill the horses and shatter the war chariots and destroy not only the Babylonians but their allies, and to plunder its spoils of silver, gold, cattle and every precious possession.

The enemies will dry up the river Euphrates, which enters the city from under its great wall, for they will turn the course of the river to form a great pool, so the waters of the river dry up and they storm the city from under its walls. It loses water and its inhabitants nearly die of thirst, and in all this their pagan gods, to which they clung and for which they lost their minds in following, did not rescue them.
Everything of the world’s powers and goods that you rely on is liable to pass away. So thank God for His gifts and trust in Him, and you will live reassured even if what you have is little.
Jackals: a predatory animal whose size is between the wolf and the fox.
Owls (daughters of the ostrich): the ostrich is a large bird that walks on the ground.
The enemies destroy Babylon, so people abandon it and wild beasts and wild animals dwell in it with the ostriches.
Babylon will be ruined like the ruin of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighboring countries, and all people abandon it.

God makes clear that He is the Ruler of all, who punishes Babylon for its evils, using the kingdom of Media and Persia coming from the north of Babylon, and He represents it as a sleeper whom God awakens to attack Babylon.

God shows the strength of the soldiers of Media and Persia, skilled in the use of weapons such as arrows and spears. They will besiege Babylon, standing in one rank around it, united together as one man, and so triumph over it, and at the same time treat it cruelly and ruin it.

If the king of Babylon exalted himself in his strength, now he is in great weakness before the attack of Media and Persia, and he writhes with fear like a woman near to childbirth who writhes in pain. God shows his weakness by the feebleness of his hands, which symbolize his strength, and what is meant is not only the king but all his armies, which have become weak before the enemies.
The swelling of Jordan: when the river Jordan overflows and its waters rush with force.

The armies of Media and Persia attack with force like the rush of the waters of the Jordan in its flood, and attack Babylon, full of good things, which he likens to a perpetual sea, that is, perpetual good things. But the mercy of God appears in His signal to the armies of Media and Persia, so they stop their ruin of Babylon and turn back from it. God is merciful and does not want the destruction of the inhabitants of Babylon but their repentance and abandoning of their worship of idols, and God asks to find a faithful shepherd to appoint over it to lead it to the faith. This is what happened after the Resurrection of Christ, when the good news spread through the whole world and reached Babylon. God is the strong One, able to chasten all the peoples to return to Him, and no one can stand before Him. These words were repeated in (ch. 49:19-21).
Babylon has become so weak that the least of the flock draw them out, and God lays waste their land.
The collapse of great Babylon will be heard in all the earth, and the peoples will cry out because of its fall.
Continuation of the prophecies about Babylon

God declares that He will raise up a violent wind against Babylon, which stands against God and against His people. This wind is the kingdom of Media and Persia, and it will destroy her. Here God appears as the Almighty, who uses the power of the earth to carry out His will. He uses Babylon to discipline His people and the nations, then uses Media and Persia to discipline Babylon, so that perhaps all may repent.

He likens Media and Persia not only to a destructive wind but to winnowers, that is, those who separate the grain from the chaff by means of a tool called the winnowing fan. Since Babylon has no goodness in her, which is symbolized by the grain, the winnowers scatter the chaff and it flies far away, and Babylon becomes empty, because the grain falls close by while the chaff flies far off. That is, Media and Persia will ruin Babylon and she will become desolate. He also makes clear that Media and Persia will besiege Babylon from every side, killing those in her, while only a few will escape from her.
Her chosen men: her heroes.

Utterly destroy: kill. God calls Media and Persia to kill the soldiers of Babylon, whether those who shoot arrows with the bow or those who put on armor to protect themselves and attack with swords and spears, so that Media and Persia kill the mighty men, the heroes of Babylon.
And so Babylon is filled with the corpses of the slain in all the streets.

Here God makes clear that although the Jews in the kingdoms of Judah and Israel sinned by worshiping idols or lusts and angered their God, yet He loves them, since they believe in His name above all peoples. So He disciplines them through Babylon, then punishes Babylon, which was cruel to them, and requires of her all the blood of His people.

God calls His people and all the nations who accept His prophecies through the mouth of Jeremiah to flee from Babylon because she will be destroyed. Everyone who believed the word of God and fled was saved from death.

God likens Babylon to a golden cup because of her great wealth, but she is in the hand of the Lord her Creator, who uses her to discipline His people and the nations, and when she does not repent, He disciplines her. The sin of Babylon was that she did not only do evil but made the nations stumble by her sins, and He likens this to a cup full of wine given to all the nations to drink, which seduces them and makes them fall into evil. Indeed, through the nations' immersion in evil, she lost her kingdom and became like a madwoman.
Balm: a medicine taken from a plant that grew in the south of Palestine.

God calls the angels to bring medicine for Babylon, that perhaps she may be healed, but she rejected the word of God through the mouth of the prophets, so she found no medicine that could benefit her. But the people of God accepted the medicine, that is, they repented, and so He brought them back safely to their land at the beginning of the rule of Media and Persia. Thus Babylon was shattered, while the people of God returned to worship Him in Jerusalem.
The people of God realized Babylon's insistence on evil and her refusal to repent, so they left her, saved themselves, and returned to Jerusalem.

Zion: Jerusalem. The people of God rejoiced that He had brought them back from captivity and forgiven their sins, so they returned to Jerusalem proclaiming how God had rescued them when they repented and brought them back to worship Him in His temple.
God calls the soldiers of Media and Persia to prepare themselves to fight Babylon and take vengeance on her, carrying out the will of God because of her injustice toward His people.

He continues speaking to the soldiers of Media and Persia, telling them to besiege her, to set watchmen around her, and to prepare an ambush to break into the city from under its walls, through the bed of the river Euphrates, which they had dried up.

He rebukes Babylon, who relied on her wealth, on her abundance of water through the great river Euphrates that passes through her, and on the great quantity of silver and gold in her treasuries. He warns her that she will be seized by the hand of Media and Persia, and God will measure out destruction upon her. Thus He likens the destruction to a measure filled with evil and plunder which He pours out upon her.
The caterpillers: locusts.
Noise: commotion.
God concludes His words about the punishment of Babylon by saying that the armies will rush upon her in great numbers like locusts and with a great noise, and will ruin her.

Do not rely on your strength or your wealth, for all this passes away, and do not make light of evil, for God watches over everything. Return to Him with repentance, rely on Him, and trust in His love, that He will receive you however great your sins.
[2] ... and none besides Him (vv. 15-26:)

15- He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heaven by his understanding. 16- When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens; and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth: he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures. 17- Every man is brutish by his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them. 18- They are vanity, the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish. 19- The portion of Jacob is not like them: for he is the former of all things, and the rod of his inheritance, the LORD of hosts is his name. 20- Thou art my battle axe and weapons of war: for with thee will I break in pieces the nations, and with thee will I destroy kingdoms; 21- And with thee will I break in pieces the horse and his rider; and with thee will I break in pieces the chariot and his rider;
22- With thee also will I break in pieces man and woman; and with thee will I break in pieces old and young; and with thee will I break in pieces the young man and the maid;

23- I will also break in pieces with thee the shepherd and his flock; and with thee will I break in pieces the husbandman and his yoke of oxen; and with thee will I break in pieces captains and rulers.

24- And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith the LORD. 25- Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the LORD, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain. 26- And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith the LORD.

Jeremiah praises God, the Creator of the whole universe, and what he mentions here in (vv. 15-19) is a repetition of what he said before in (ch. 10:12-16). For He is the Creator of heaven and earth and the whole world.

God is also the mover of everything in the universe: He moves the winds so that the rain falls, and gives a command to the lightnings, so they come forth with their flashing and the rain falls with them. He likens the power of God the Almighty to treasuries in which He keeps the winds, and commands them, and they come out of them.
Vv. 17, 18: Brutish: he has become ignorant and foolish.

Before the greatness and knowledge of God, man's ignorance is revealed, for his knowledge is very limited before the unlimited wisdom of God. Man's ignorance is shown in his portraying gods in the form of idols that have no power in them, and so he points here to the weakness of Babylon, which trusted in idols, before the unlimited power of God. All the images that the craftsmen cast are vanity, and their weakness is shown in that they do not help their owners in times of distress, such as the attack of Media and Persia on Babylon and their destruction of her.

These are the idols of Babylon, which have no power. But as for the people of God, Israel, their King, who is indicated by the rod that the king holds in his hand, is very strong; He overcomes all the power of the world and delivers His people who rely on Him, who are His inheritance, that is, His kingdom and those who follow Him. He is also their inheritance, since they inherit in Him the Kingdom of Heaven.
After the praise offered to God ends, He addresses a great nation, which He likens to a battle axe that in war breaks in pieces everyone it meets. It is either:
1- The nation of Media and Persia, which shattered Babylon and took possession of all the nations of the world.
2- Or Babylon, which shattered the nations of the world, and then God punishes her in (v. 24).
This axe shatters all the military powers of the nations of the world, represented by horses and war chariots.
With this axe He kills all people, men and women, old and young, and all the youths.
He also kills and ruins the various kinds of trades, whether the shepherds and their flocks or the farmers and their crops. He even kills the rulers of these nations.
God decides that He will punish Babylon for all her evils and her injustice toward His people in Jerusalem.

He likens great Babylon to a mountain that exalts itself in its pride, so God burns it and rolls it down like a small stone, that is, Babylon becomes utterly weak. Just as she destroyed the rest of the earth, Babylon is now destroyed because of her evil.

The stones of this mountain become useless and are not fit as stones for any new building, whether strong stones to be placed in the corner of a wall or even ordinary stones for any building. That is, Babylon becomes ruined and abandoned, and not fit for any person to live in.

Contemplate the greatness of God in creation so that you praise Him, glorify Him, rely on Him, and rejoice in His presence with you. Then you will no longer be troubled by the movements of others and their threats, but will live in peace in the bosom of your God.
[3] The peoples shatter Babylon (vv. 27-33)

27- Set ye up a standard in the land, blow the trumpet among the nations, prepare the nations against her, call together against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz; appoint a captain against her; cause the horses to come up as the rough caterpillers. 28- Prepare against her the nations with the kings of the Medes, the captains thereof, and all the rulers thereof, and all the land of his dominion. 29- And the land shall tremble and sorrow: for every purpose of the LORD shall be performed against Babylon, to make the land of Babylon a desolation without an inhabitant. 30- The mighty men of Babylon have forborne to fight, they have remained in their holds: their might hath failed; they became as women: they have burned her dwellingplaces; her bars are broken.
31- One post shall run to meet another, and one messenger to meet another, to shew the king of Babylon that his city is taken at one end,

32- And that the passages are stopped, and the reeds they have burned with fire, and the men of war are affrighted. 33- For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; The daughter of Babylon is like a threshingfloor, it is time to thresh her: yet a little while, and the time of her harvest shall come.
Ararat: a region in Armenia, north of Lake Van.
Minni: a region next to Ararat in Armenia.
Ashchenaz: a people descended from Gomer, the grandson of Japheth (Gen 10:3), who dwell in Armenia.

God speaks to Media and Persia so that they call the surrounding peoples, whom Media had previously subjected to her authority, to go out with her to fight Babylon. The Median commander raises the banner of war and the peoples follow him to attack Babylon. The meaning is that huge numbers of soldiers fought Babylon and ruined her.

Prepare: set apart. In sum, all the peoples subject to the authority of Media will attack Babylon, since Media had become the strongest nation in the world at that time, Persia had united with her, and many peoples had submitted to her, by whom she crushed the kingdoms of the earth, the first of which was Babylon.

He portrays the greatness of the Median attack on Babylon, in that the earth shakes and trembles under the feet of the soldiers gathered around Babylon to destroy her, because God the Almighty wished to punish Babylon.
Failed: that is, dried up, and the meaning is that their courage grew very weak, that is, they became without strength.
Her bars: the timbers that support the pillars of the house and cover it as a roof.

The mighty men of Babylon, that is, the commanders of her armies, were afraid and were unable to fight, and fled, taking refuge in their strongholds, and their courage was lost, so they became as weak as women when they saw their houses and palaces burned with fire.

When any war takes place, soldiers who are able to run swiftly hurry to tell the king the outcome of the war. Here the post, that is, the swift runner, gives the news to another runner, so the news reaches the king quickly that Babylon has fallen from one end of the city to the other, that is, all of it has fallen.

And they told the king that the roads leading to the city had been taken over by the enemies, and that when the Babylonian soldiers took refuge among the stalks of the reeds to hide among them, the enemies burned the reeds to put an end to them all, and the whole Babylonian army was in weakness and confusion.

He likens Babylon to a threshingfloor, which is a broad place where grain is threshed by means of threshing sledges drawn by animals. That is, the feet of the enemies trample Babylon to kill those in her and cut off their heads from their bodies with swords, as the grain is separated from the chaff by the threshing sledge. Thus the heads of all her inhabitants will be reaped and the city will be utterly destroyed. And just as Babylon ruined the kingdom of Judah, Egypt, and Moab, so she too will be ruined (ch. 4:7).

Do not anger God by your deeds, lest He allow everyone to rise against you to trouble you; and if you sin, return to Him quickly with repentance, for He is merciful and long-suffering. [4] The destruction of Babylon because she wronged the people of ... (vv. 34-40)

34- Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon hath devoured me, he hath crushed me, he hath made me an empty vessel, he hath swallowed me up like a dragon, he hath filled his belly with my delicates, he hath cast me out. 35- The violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say; and my blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldea, shall Jerusalem say. 36- Therefore thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will plead thy cause, and take vengeance for thee; and I will dry up her sea, and make her springs dry. 37- And Babylon shall become heaps, a dwellingplace for dragons, an astonishment, and an hissing, without an inhabitant. 38- They shall roar together like lions: they shall yell as lions' whelps. 39- In their heat I will make their feasts, and I will make them drunken, that they may rejoice, and sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake, saith the LORD. 40- I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he goats.

Judah cries out like a weak woman before the cruelty of the Babylonians, saying that Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon has devoured her goods and destroyed her, and swallowed all her glory like a dragon that swallows and devours anything before it, and drank all her goods so that she became an empty vessel, and cast out all her inhabitants who fled from the swords of his soldiers.
The kingdom of Judah groans, declaring that she has been wronged and that Babylon will be called to account for the blood of Judah that was shed in the streets.

God comes forth to defend His people, and becomes an adversary to Babylon in place of His weak people. So He withholds her goods from Babylon by drying up the river Euphrates, on which the goods of Babylon depended, when Media diverted the river Euphrates and dried it up.

37: When God ruins Babylon, she becomes heaps of stones and is abandoned, not dwelt in by man but by beasts such as jackals, and everyone who passes by her is astonished, wondering how the greatest city of the world was ruined, and he knows that the reason is her evil.
Lions' whelps: cubs or young lions.
The soldiers of Media attack Babylon, and are like young lions that devour everyone they meet, consume all the goods of Babylon, and roar against her with a terrifying roar.
In their heat: in their excitement over the pleasures of eating and drinking in celebration of their god.

The Babylonians were celebrating the feast of their god Bel and drinking wine with their king, and while they were in the pleasure of their lusts, the Medes attacked them, so they drank the wrath of God and died, to end in eternal torment because of their evils.
With he goats: the plural of equipment, which means weapons of war and all of a person's possessions.
The Babylonians become like lambs and rams before the power of the Medes, who slaughter them and take their possessions and goods.

Be just in your dealings with those around you, even if they have no power. Do not wrong anyone, and give everyone his due, not only in money but in speech, in expressing himself, and in his comfort. And do not rejoice that by your selfishness you have obtained what you want at the expense of others, for you will be called to account for all of this.
[5] The ruin of Babylon and the deliverance of the people of ... (vv. 41-53:)
41- How is Sheshach taken! and how is the praise of the whole earth surprised! how is Babylon become an astonishment among the nations!

42- The sea is come up upon Babylon: she is covered with the multitude of the waves thereof. 43- Her cities are a desolation, a dry land, and a wilderness, a land wherein no man dwelleth, neither doth any son of man pass thereby. 44- And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and I will bring forth out of his mouth that which he hath swallowed up: and the nations shall not flow together any more unto him: yea, the wall of Babylon shall fall. 45- My people, go ye out of the midst of her, and deliver ye every man his soul from the fierce anger of the LORD. 46- And lest your heart faint, and ye fear for the rumour that shall be heard in the land; a rumour shall both come one year, and after that in another year shall come a rumour, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler. 47- Therefore, behold, the days come, that I will do judgment upon the graven images of Babylon: and her whole land shall be confounded, and all her slain shall fall in the midst of her. 48- Then the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein, shall sing for Babylon: for the spoilers shall come unto her from the north, saith the LORD. 49- As Babylon hath caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth.
50- Ye that have escaped the sword, go away, stand not still: remember the LORD afar off, and let Jerusalem come into your mind.
51- We are confounded, because we have heard reproach: shame hath covered our faces: for strangers are come into the sanctuaries of the LORD'S house.

52- Wherefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will do judgment upon her graven images: and through all her land the wounded shall groan. 53- Though Babylon should mount up to heaven, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, yet from me shall spoilers come unto her, saith the LORD.
Sheshach: the one sunk in water, and the meaning is Babylon, which is on the river Euphrates, that is, with abundant water around her.
God shows the reversal of fortunes in great Babylon, who used to boast over all the countries of the world, and how she collapsed and was ruined because of her pride and her evils.

He likens the attack of Media and Persia to the raging sea that covers Babylon and drowns her, that is, destroys her, since the soldiers of Media and those who follow her were very many, as if they were the sea.
After the ruin of Babylon, she will be abandoned, and no man will live in her.

The symbol of Babylon's power was her god Bel. Babylon used to wrong and devour all the peoples, and she is symbolized by the god Bel who devoured all the peoples, but he is nothing before the power of God; he is merely an image to which they offer animals for him to eat, though in truth it is his priests who eat them (Dan 13). That is, God proclaims the weakness of Babylon and of her god, who is shattered, and likewise her great walls, in which she boasts over all the peoples, are broken and torn down.

He calls His people dwelling in Babylon to flee from her when Media and Persia attack her, and not to trust in her strength, in which she prides herself, because she will be ruined, so the people of God flee from her quickly. All these prophecies God proclaimed about 70 years before the ruin of Babylon, and no one believed them except His people, who fled and so saved themselves by their obedience to God.

Ruler against ruler: Media and Persia rule over Babylon. God reassures His people when they see the attack of Media and Persia on Babylon, and declares to them that the reports of Media and Persia's domination of the world will follow one another, so they should not be troubled by the fall of Babylon and the domination of Media and Persia, because God will bring them back to their land at the beginning of the rule of Media and Persia.

By the attack of Media and Persia, they shatter Babylon and her gods, that is, her idols, to proclaim that their gods are stronger than the gods of Babylon, and they kill the men of Babylon, and everyone of them who remains alive is put to shame.

Because God is the one who commanded the ruin of Babylon, the heavens and the earth rejoice in this. The earth symbolizes the cities of the world that Babylon wronged, so they gloat over her at her ruin, while the heavens symbolize the angels who rejoice at the removal of evil and its punishment. The attack of Media and Persia on Babylon will come from the north.
Here God shows that the punishment of Babylon is because of her injustice toward the people of God, and just as she killed the men of the people of God, Media and Persia kill the men of Babylon.
He speaks to the people of God who are fleeing from Babylon, that they should hasten their flight and think of returning to Jerusalem to renew her temple and offer worship to God.
God reminds His people of the shame they felt when Babylon attacked Jerusalem, entered the temple of God, and ruined it.
Because Babylon defiled the temple of God, God shatters her idols by the hand of Media and Persia, and kills and wounds her inhabitants.
God decides in the end that however much Babylon exalts herself and relies on her strength and greatness, God will punish her and destroy her.

Flee from evil and from keeping company with the wicked, and from their places that make you stumble, and from everything that makes you fall into sin, for this flight of yours means your faith in God and purity, and God will help you, bless you, and keep every evil far from you. [6] The shattering of great Babylon (vv. 54-58:)

54- A sound of a cry cometh from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans: 55- Because the LORD hath spoiled Babylon, and destroyed out of her the great voice; when her waves do roar like great waters, a noise of their voice is uttered: 56- Because the spoiler is come upon her, even upon Babylon, and her mighty men are taken, every one of their bows is broken: for the LORD God of recompences shall surely requite.

57- And I will make drunk her princes, and her wise men, her captains, and her rulers, and her mighty men: and they shall sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake, saith the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts. 58- Thus saith the LORD of hosts; The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken, and her high gates shall be burned with fire; and the people shall labour in vain, and the folk in the fire, and they shall be weary.

God describes what will happen in Babylon when Media and Persia attack her: the sound of the shattering of her houses and walls will rise, accompanied by the cry of her inhabitants, who fall by the sword and are ruined, and the voices of pride coming from the king and the princes will come to an end and be replaced by the sound of fear and shame and the cry of those who flee.
God punishes Babylon for her evils, so He shatters her by means of Media and Persia, kills her heroic soldiers, and shatters her weapons of war.
All the princes and great men of Babylon fall like those who have drunk a great deal of wine, so they reel and fall to the ground, and will not rise, because they have died.

Weary: very tired. This shows the weakness of men however great their strength: Babylon spent great effort and vast sums in building her walls, but they will be shattered, so that all the peoples may know that protection comes from God and not from material strength.

Do not waste all your time in the works of the world and forget your goal, who is God. And if anxiety fights you, turn to Him, and not to gathering money and mustering the forces of the world, for they will neither protect you nor give you peace.
[4] The reading of the prophecies in Babylon (vv. 59-64:)

59- The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, when he went with Zedekiah the king of Judah into Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. And this Seraiah was a quiet prince. 60- So Jeremiah wrote in a book all the evil that should come upon Babylon, even all these words that are written against Babylon. 61- And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, When thou comest to Babylon, and shalt see, and shalt read all these words; 62- Then shalt thou say, O LORD, thou hast spoken against this place, to cut it off, that none shall remain in it, neither man nor beast, but that it shall be desolate for ever. 63- And it shall be, when thou hast made an end of reading this book, that thou shalt bind a stone to it, and cast it into the midst of Euphrates: 64- And thou shalt say, Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise from the evil that I will bring upon her: and they shall be weary. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.

Jeremiah chose a believing man from among the followers of King Zedekiah, Seraiah the son of Neriah, the prince of the camp, that is, the chief of the city in which the people settle and dwell. It seems that he was a ruler over Jerusalem, and he was a devout man and the brother of Baruch the son of Neriah, the prophet, the scribe of Jeremiah's prophecies and his disciple. Seraiah was going with King Zedekiah in the fourth year of his reign to Babylon to renew his covenants and his allegiance to Babylon, although after his return he broke his covenant and began to incline toward the king of Egypt.

Jeremiah wrote his prophecies that he had proclaimed about Babylon, which are written in chs. 50, 51. He wrote them himself in a book, that is, a large piece of leather or papyrus. Because of the gravity of these prophecies, Jeremiah wrote them himself and did not have Baruch write them, so as not to expose him to danger from Babylon's anger against him and the occupation of his land, and he bore the responsibility, risking his life in carrying out the commands of God. Here Jeremiah's fatherhood and his self-giving as a servant appear.
Jeremiah asked Seraiah, when he entered Babylon, to gather the Jews who had been taken captive to Babylon and read to them the words of this book, and to affirm that Babylon will be ruined.

This speech may seem very strange to unbelievers: how did Jeremiah call his people to submit to Babylon and now declare that she will be ruined? The reason, of course, is that they should accept God's discipline by submitting to Babylon until they repent, and then not cling to the goods of Babylon nor seek shelter in her, because she will be ruined on account of her evil, and they must believe in God and take refuge in Him.

Jeremiah commanded that the ruin of Babylon be confirmed by an illustrative example: that he should bind the book in which the prophecies are written to a stone and then throw it before the eyes of the people into the river Euphrates, declaring that Babylon will sink in this way, that is, be ruined.

God alerts you to the events of the world so that you repent and return to Him. So He shows you the fall of the powers of the world and the punishment of the wicked, so that you do not rely on the wicked world. Contemplate the works of God before you so that you may believe in Him and live with Him.

A summary of the events of the fall of Jerusalem and the captivity. Jeremiah mentioned the fall of Jerusalem in chs. 39, 40, and this event is also mentioned in (2 Kgs 24, 25) and (2 Chr 36:17-21). He closed the end of ch. 51 by saying that these words are the end of the prophecies of Jeremiah, from which it is understood that ch. 52 was added to the book, and most likely the one who wrote it was Ezra the priest. It summarizes the events of the fall of Jerusalem, the plundering of the spoils of the temple, and the captivity of the Jews, then the beginning of God's mercies, which will be completed by the return from captivity.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: After Babylon took Jehoiachin, king of Judah, captive, the king of Babylon chose his uncle Mattaniah in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah (2 Kgs 24:17), and made him king when he was twenty-one years old. He was weak in character: he would show his loyalty to Babylon, then turn back and speak with Egypt, and he cast Jeremiah into prison, then turned back and consulted him. The reign of Zedekiah lasted 11 years, in which he lost his ability to lead his people and lost the trust of Babylon in him. This was by God's ordering, to discipline Zedekiah and all his kingdom because of their sins.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Zedekiah walked in evil like his brother Jehoiakim, although he sometimes pretended to submit to God and to His prophet Jeremiah.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The reign of Zedekiah over the kingdom of Judah ended with his rebellion against the king of Babylon, so the latter rose against him, took him captive, and shattered and burned Jerusalem because of the sins of her people.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: In the ninth year of King Zedekiah the armies of Babylon came and besieged Jerusalem and built around her ramparts and towers, to prevent her people from escaping from her, to be able to know what was going on inside her, and to make it easy to break into her. This was in the month of January of the year 588 BC, which corresponds to the tenth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of the reign of Zedekiah.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The siege of Jerusalem continued for a year and a half, that is, until the month of July of the year 587 BC, which corresponds to the ninth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year of King Zedekiah. At this time the famine became severe among the inhabitants of Jerusalem until they were nearly dying, so they looked for a way to flee and save themselves.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: In a last attempt to escape, the Jews made a breach in the wall of the city and went out through it. It was between the two walls, near the king's garden.

If you want to overcome your enemies the demons, you must rely on God and not on your own thoughts or strength, because they are stronger than you, and in this way you save yourself from their hands however much their tricks and wars surround you.
[2] The trial of Zedekiah (vv. 8-11:)
8- But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.

9- Then they took the king, and carried him up unto the king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath; where he gave judgment upon him. 10- And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: he slew also all the princes of Judah in Riblah. 11- Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in two chains of brass, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The plains of Jericho: a valley next to the city of Jericho, which lies beside the river Jordan, northeast of Jerusalem.
King Zedekiah fled from the city of Jerusalem, but the armies of Babylon were able to seize him when he reached the plains of Jericho.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Riblah: a city near Hamath and the river Orontes, which is now in Syria, and lies north of Jericho. The soldiers of Babylon took King Zedekiah and went with him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who was staying in Riblah to prevent any Egyptian reinforcements from reaching the Jews from the Egyptians living there, and because there is a trade route between Egypt and Babylon.
V. 10: In order to frighten and humiliate Zedekiah, Nebuchadnezzar killed his sons before his eyes, then the princes of his people.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him with chains of brass, that is, strong chains so that he would not flee, and led him captive to Babylon and cast him into prison until the end of his life.

Nebuchadnezzar humiliated Zedekiah, and years later Nebuchadnezzar lost his reason and was cast out like the animals, away from people, for a period of seven years. Do not humiliate others lest you be humiliated, and do not wrong anyone, but be merciful and you will obtain the mercies of God.
[3] The fall of Jerusalem and the plundering of the temple (vv. 12-23)

12- Now in the fifth month, in the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, which served the king of Babylon, into Jerusalem, 13- And burned the house of the LORD, and the king's house; and all the houses of Jerusalem, and all the houses of the great men, burned he with fire. 14- And all the army of the Chaldeans, that were with the captain of the guard, brake down all the walls of Jerusalem round about. 15- Then Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive certain of the poor of the people, and the residue of the people that remained in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude. 16- But Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left certain of the poor of the land for vinedressers and for husbandmen. 17- Also the pillars of brass that were in the house of the LORD, and the bases, and the brazen sea that was in the house of the LORD, the Chaldeans brake, and carried all the brass of them to Babylon. 18- The caldrons also, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the bowls, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered, took they away. 19- And the basons, and the firepans, and the bowls, and the caldrons, and the candlesticks, and the spoons, and the cups; that which was of gold in gold, and that which was of silver in silver, took the captain of the guard away. 20- The two pillars, one sea, and twelve brazen bulls that were under the bases, which king Solomon had made in the house of the LORD: the brass of all these vessels was without weight. 21- And concerning the pillars, the height of one pillar was eighteen cubits; and a fillet of twelve cubits did compass it; and the thickness thereof was four fingers: it was hollow.

22- And a chapiter of brass was upon it; and the height of one chapiter was five cubits, with network and pomegranates upon the chapiters round about, all of brass. The second pillar also and the pomegranates were like unto these. 23- And there were ninety and six pomegranates on a side; and all the pomegranates upon the network were an hundred round about.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: After the capture of Jerusalem, the taking of the king captive, the killing of the great men, and the captivity of many to Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar sent the captain of the guard, who represents the commander of the army or the minister of the interior, and who was called Nebuzaradan, to Jerusalem. This was on the tenth day of the fifth month in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The work of Nebuzaradan was the complete destruction of Jerusalem, so that she would never think of rebelling against Babylon. So he burned the temple of Solomon, the king's palace, and the palaces of the great men, after plundering what was in them. The first plundering of the temple had been completed by Babylon in the year 597 BC, when she took the silver and gold that were in it.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Nebuzaradan also tore down the walls of Jerusalem by means of the men of the army, so that Jerusalem would lose her fortification and protection and could not resist Babylon.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Nebuzaradan chose everyone he saw who was energetic or strong or of distinguished character from among the poor of the people, as well as those who wished to surrender themselves to Babylon, and took them all as captives to Babylon. He left in Jerusalem and its surroundings a group of the poor who worked as farmers to work the land and keep it, but who had no strength to carry out a revolt against Babylon.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: What remained in the temple of the Lord were the brass works, the most important of which were the two brass pillars, the brazen sea in which the priests used to wash, and likewise the bases of the pillars.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Caldrons: large brass vessels in which meat or ashes are placed.
Shovels: the plural of shovel, a brass scoop for gathering the ashes from the altar of brass. Snuffers: the plural of snuffer, one of the tools of the altar of brass.
Bowls: a small vessel that may be of brass, silver, or gold, with which blood is poured. Spoons: small dishes of brass or gold.
Basons: vessels for gathering blood in.
Firepans: golden vessels for putting coals and incense in.
Candlesticks: the plural of lampstand, which is of gold and is lit with oil.
Cups: small cups.
Nebuzaradan took all the vessels of the temple, small or large, made of gold or silver or brass.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: In these verses he makes clear the huge quantities of brass that Nebuzaradan took from the temple, whether in the pillars and their bases or in the sea and its bases made in the form of bulls. He makes clear the measurements of the brass pillar, whose height was eighteen cubits, about nine meters, whose circumference was about twelve cubits, and whose thickness was 4 fingers, about 7 cm, and the chapiter on the pillar, whose height was five cubits, with network upon the chapiter and pomegranates numbering one hundred. All this was made of pure brass, so the weight of the brass was very great.
Sin strips you of all your pride and glory, so hasten to repentance to regain your sonship and your glory as a child of God, and return to the way of life and the striving in the way of the Kingdom.
[4] The killing of the priests and the captivity of the people (vv. 24-30)
24- And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door:

25- He took also out of the city an eunuch, which had the charge of the men of war; and seven men of them that were near the king's person, which were found in the city; and the principal scribe of the host, who mustered the people of the land; and threescore men of the people of the land, that were found in the midst of the city. 26- So Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them, and went

... to the king of Babylon to Riblah. 27- And the king of Babylon smote them, and put them to death in Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive out of his own land. 28- This is the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand Jews and three and twenty: 29- In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar he carried away captive from Jerusalem eight hundred thirty and two persons: 30- In the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred forty and five persons: all the persons were four thousand and six hundred.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Nebuzaradan seized the rest of the great men in Jerusalem. He took the priest Seraiah, the foremost, and the priest next to him, Zephaniah, and likewise the keepers of the door of the temple, who were three of the priests, in addition to the eunuch in charge of the men of war, who represents the minister of defense. He also seized seven men of the king's counselors, and the scribe who gathers the men of war for conscription, and added to them sixty men who were the greatest he found among the people.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: After Nebuzaradan seized the great men who were in Jerusalem, he brought them to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who tortured them and then killed them in Riblah, where he was staying.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: In this verse and the following verses he mentions those whom Nebuchadnezzar took captive to Babylon, in three stages. The first stage was the captivity of 3023, and this was in the seventh year of Nebuchadnezzar, that is, in the year 598 BC. It is noted that this number is of men only, apart from the women and children, who are all mentioned in (2 Kgs 24:14-16), and this, of course, is apart from those he killed.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The second stage of the captivity was of 832 men, and that was in the year 587 BC, in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: As for the third stage of the captives, it was of 745 men, and that was in the twenty-third year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, that is, in the year 582 BC, in the days of Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon appointed governor over Jerusalem. Thus the total number of men taken captive to Babylon was 4600.

Do not shatter the strength of others so that you alone remain strong, because God is able to strengthen them and restore their glory to them, as He brought His people back from captivity. And to the extent that you are gentle with others, God supports you and is gentle with you.
[5] The end of King Jehoiachin (vv. 31-34:)

31- And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the five and twentieth day of the month, that Evilmerodach king of Babylon in the year of his reign lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brought him forth out of prison,

32- And spake kindly unto him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon, 33- And changed his prison garments: and he did continually eat bread before him all the days of his life. 34- And for his diet, there was a continual diet given him of the king of Babylon, every day a portion until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Jehoiachin, king of Judah, remained in prison after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took him captive to Babylon, until he had completed 37 years in prison. Then Nebuchadnezzar died and his son Evilmerodach reigned over Babylon. He wished to show his good administration and his kindness toward his subjects, so he brought Jehoiachin out of prison to live with him in his palace, and even gave him more honor than the kings or governors who were imprisoned with him, and brought them out as well, as a proclamation of the mercy of the new rule, especially since Jehoiachin had reached the age of eighty, his people in Jerusalem had become poor and weak, and the Jews in Babylon had settled and acquired property and their inclination to return to Jerusalem had weakened. That is, there was no longer any danger of Jehoiachin carrying out a revolt against Babylon.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Jehoiachin lived in the palace of the king of Babylon and ate food at his table, and a salary was given him to spend as he wished, that is, he lived honored until the end of his life in Babylon. This was a prelude to the return of the people from captivity, that is, God is able to free the king and his people from slavery and fetters.

Be confident in the power of God, who is able to lift tribulations from you however heavy they may be, and even turns tribulations into blessings, so that you are freed from your sins and receive the reward of your bearing tribulations with thanksgiving.
